One should meditate upon Raudrī, seated upon a bull and a lotus, at the time when the sun has half-set and is reddish.

At midnight, at the *dvādaśānta*, all [the goddesses] bear black collyrium; they are witnesses of all ritual acts, joined with emission (*sṛṣṭi*) and the other [phases], and devoid of the fourth quality (*guṇa*). Thus, in due order, the preceptor (*ācārya*) is one who has been initiated into the specific pledge (*samaya*), liberated, and consecrated.

Having meditated according to the principle of "one, two, three, four" in accordance with each respective authority, [one should contemplate] Śiva-Śakti alone as the witness of all activities, which are differentiated by the various causes such as Brahmā and the rest. Then, the *samayins*, *putrakas*, and others, having meditated in sequence upon the aforementioned twilight (*sandhyā*) at the heart, the *bindu*, and the *brahmarandhra* according to the appropriate time for each, [should perform the rite].
One should visualize her as slender as a lotus fiber, red, white, or otherwise colored;
one may make her form black, or she is visualized as being led by the wind.

These [syllables] should be meditated upon in their respective locations previously mentioned— namely, the heart-seed, the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), and the *dvādaśānta*— in due order. Then, taking water with the right hand and pouring it into the left hand, one should consecrate it once with the *saṃhitā* mantra and,
using the *kumbha-mudrā*, [utter] "vauṣaṭ" until the end.

One should sprinkle [the disciple] on the head with the root mantra. Having grasped [the vessel] as before, having consecrated it as before, and having placed it as before, one should sprinkle water flowing from the base of the little finger of the left hand onto the head with the right hand, using the *saṃhitā* mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. Then, taking the remaining water in the right hand, one should draw pure water into the left nostril by means of the *pūraka* breath.

Having performed the *kumbhaka* after [the breath] has entered, and having washed [it] while it is situated within, one should contemplate it as having a black form. Having drawn it in through the right nostril by means of *recaka*, one should burn it with the fire arising from the big toe of the right foot. Then, having sipped water (*ācamana*) and performed the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).

Having offered three *arghya* oblations to the Goddess Gāyatrī; having performed the recitation (*japa*) of the Goddess Gāyatrī ten times; having approached (*upasthāna*) Gāyatrī as residing within the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) and offered *arghya*; and having performed the libation (*tarpaṇa*) for the Mantras, Devas, Ṛṣis, humans, spirits, ancestors, teachers, and other chosen deities by means of the root mantra, the five Brahmans, and the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) mantra—namely: to Īśāna, the head...

Svāhā! To the face of Tatpuruṣa, svāhā. To the heart of Aghora, svāhā. To the secret organ of Vāmadeva, svāhā. To the form of Sadyojāta, svāhā. Oṃ hāṃ, to the heart, svāhā. Oṃ hiṃ, to the head, svāhā.

Oṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the crest-lock! Oṃ haiṃ, svāhā to the armor! Oṃ hoṃ, svāhā to the eyes! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the weapon! Oṃ, svāhā to all mantras! Svāhā to all gods! Vaiṣaṭ to all humans! Oṃ, [svāhā] to all ancestors!

Svadhā to all mothers; svadhā to all teachers; svadhā to all kinsmen. Having performed the libation for the beloved deities, having sipped water, and having performed the placement of mantras on the hands and limbs, the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*) is made on this auspicious lunar day. (p26b, f23a, l1)

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "I shall perform the specific libation (*tarpaṇa*) as a constituent part of the ritual bathing (*kriyāsnāna*), which is itself a subsidiary of the rites in the Śiva-sacrifice consisting of the restoration of the ancient temple and the eight-fold binding of Lord Sadāśiva of Veṇuvana," [the officiant] should offer [the water] with the tips of the fingers using the *devatīrtha* [part of the hand], together with *kuśa* grass, as follows: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ śivāya svāhā*; *oṃ hauṃ īśānamūrdhāya svāhā*.
Oṃ he(heṃ) tatpuruṣa(l3) vaktrāya svāhā | Oṃ hauṃ ghorahṛdayāya svāhā | Oṃ hiṃ vāmadevaguhyāya svāhā | Oṃ haṃ sadyojātamūrtaye svāhā | Oṃ hāṃ hṛdayāya (l4) svāhā ||

Svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the crest-lock. Oṃ haiṃ, svāhā to the armor. Oṃ hauṃ, svāhā to the eyes. (L5) Oṃ haḥ, svāhā to the weapon. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Ananteśa. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Sūkṣmeśa. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śivottama.
Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Ekanetra! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Ekarudra! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Trimūrti! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śrīkaṇṭha! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śikhaṇḍin! Oṃ... (l7)

Hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the lord of the principle of Śiva (śivatattvādhipati). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of Power (śaktitattva). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the lord of the principle of Power, the possessor of power (śaktimant). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Sadāśiva. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Brahmā, the lord of the principle of Sadāśiva (sadāśivatattvādhipati). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the lord of the principle of Īśvara (īśvaratattvādhipati).

Oṃ hāṃ! To Ananta, the sovereign lord of the principle of Īśvara, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ! To the pure principle, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ! To Īśvara, the sovereign lord of the pure principle, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ! To the principle of Māyā, [svāhā]! To the sovereign lord of the principle of Māyā...

To Gaganeśa, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of time (kālatattva), svāhā! To the lord of the principle of time, named Kāla, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the lord of the principle of time, the drop of knowledge (jñānabindu), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of necessity (niyatitattva), svāhā! To the lord of the principle of necessity, the Restrainer (niyāmaka), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ...

Svāhā to the reality of knowledge! Svāhā to the lord of the reality of knowledge, the destroyer of ignorance! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the reality of passion! Svāhā to Kāma, the lord of the reality of passion! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the reality of the person! Oṃ hāṃ... (line 6)

To the Lord of the principle of the person (*puruṣa-tattva*), the subtle body, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the principle of primordial nature, the primary body (*pradhāna-kāya*), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of the qualities (*guṇa-tattva*), svāhā! To the Lord of the principle of the qualities, the three bodies (*tri-deha*), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of the intellect (*buddhi-tattva*), svāhā! To the Lord of the principle of the intellect...

To the Awakened One, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of egoity (ahaṅkāra-tattva), svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the lord of the principle of egoity, Ahaṅkṛti, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of mind (manas-tattva), svāhā!
To the lord of the principle of mind, Saṅkalpa, svāhā!

Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of hearing! Svāhā to Vyomeśa, the lord of the principle of hearing! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of touch! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Sarvāṅga, the lord of the principle of touch! (l3) Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of sight! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Prakāśa, the lord of the principle of sight! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the tongue! Oṃ...

Hāṃ! To the Great One, the lord of the principle of the tongue, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ! To the principle of the nose, svāhā! To Vilambaka, the lord of the principle of the nose, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ! To the principle of speech, svāhā!
Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the principle of speech, Dindubhi, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of feet, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the principle of feet, Ramaṇīśa, svāhā!
(l6) Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of hands, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the principle of hands, Somadāna, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of the anus, svāhā!

Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the element of water, the maker of water, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the element of the sexual organ, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the Lord of the element of the sexual organ, Ghanānanda, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the element of sound, svāhā! (p28a, l1)

Svāhā to the Lord of the element of sound, the Subtle One! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element of touch! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the most powerful Lord of the element of touch! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element of form! Svāhā to the Radiant One, the Lord of the element of form! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element of mind! Oṃ hāṃ, [svāhā] to the Lord of the element of mind...

To the water-element, svāhā! (l3) Oṃ hāṃ, to the element of fragrance, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the lord of the element of fragrance, the limb of fragrance, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the element of space, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to the lord of the element of space, Sūkṣma, (l4) svāhā!

Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element of wind. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Mātariśvan, the lord of the element of wind. Oṃ, svāhā to the element of fire. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Tviṣāṃnidhi, the lord of the element of fire. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element of water. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Jaleśa, the lord of the element of water.

Svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the element earth (kṣmā-tattva). Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śrīkaṇṭha, the lord of the element earth. Having thus offered libations, [one says]: Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Ādityas. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Vasus. Oṃ hāṃ... (l7)
Svāhā to the Rudras! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Viśvedevas! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Sādhyas! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Maruts! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Bhṛgus! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the Aṅgirases!

Having thus gratified the groups of eight deities, [the officiant], wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (upavītī), with the joints of the fingers joined together, [offers]: Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Vasiṣṭha; svāhā to Pulastya; Oṃ hāṃ...

Svāhā to Kratu! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhāradvāja! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Viśvāmitra! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Pracetas! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Hrasvakāya! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Agastya! Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Dadhīci! Oṃ hāṃ... (line 3)
"Salutation to Durvāsas. Having thus gratified the eleven sages with the [appropriate] *parva-sandhis*, [one offers]: "Vauṣaṭ to Sanaka! "Oṃ hāṃ, vauṣaṭ to Sanandana!
"Oṃ hāṃ, vauṣaṭ to Sanātana! "Oṃ hāṃ, vauṣaṭ to Sanatkumāra! "Oṃ hāṃ, vauṣaṭ to Kapila! "Oṃ hāṃ, vauṣaṭ to Pañcaśikha! (ll. 4–5)

"Oṃ hāṃ, to Ṛṣabha, vauṣaṭ!"—having thus gratified the seven ancestors; "To all beings, vauṣaṭ," [offering] with the base of the fingers. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*upavītin*), with the tips of *kuśa* grass, water mixed with sesame seeds, and using the leaf-cup as a vessel: "Oṃ hāṃ, to Kavyavāhana, svadhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Somapa, svadhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Yama, svadhā! Oṃ hāṃ... (l7)

To the Brahman-sages, *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to the drinkers of clarified butter (*ājyapa*), *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to the drinker of Soma (*somapa*), *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to Aryaman, *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to Anipattā, *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to Anala, *svadhā*.
Thus [are offered] to the divine ancestors (*devapitṛ*). Oṃ hāṃ, to the father Īśa, *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to the grandfather Sadāśiva, *svadhā*. Oṃ hāṃ, to Īśānta...

"Prapitāmahāya svadhā"—thus [he offers] to the specific ancestors. (l2) Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the fathers; oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the grandfathers; oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the great-grandfathers; oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the great-great-grandfathers; oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the mothers; oṃ hāṃ... (l3)

Svadhā to the grandmothers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the great-grandmothers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the great-great-grandmothers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all the paternal ancestors. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all the mothers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all the kinsmen. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all the teachers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all...
Svadhā to the friends! Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the divine ancestors!
Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the ancestors! Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the mothers! Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the planets! Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the Rākṣasas!
Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the Vasus! Oṃ hāṃ... (line 6)

Svadhā to the wives who have had but one husband. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all gurus. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to those who drink soma. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all ācāryas. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all brothers. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to the upādhyāyas. Oṃ hāṃ, svadhā to all maternal uncles. Oṃ hāṃ, *astrāya* huṃ phaṭ namaḥ—thus [one should offer] to desire and anger.

For the purpose of warding off all obstacles, one should cast [the grass] together with kuśa grass onto the bank of water. Then, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, with the tips of the hands holding counter-kuśa blades: *oṃ hāṃ gaṇapataye svāhā*. *oṃ hāṃ devyai svāhā*. *oṃ hāṃ subrahmaṇyāya svāhā*. *oṃ*... (l2)

Hāṃ, obeisance to Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (Oṃ Hāṃ) Svāhā to Ānandabhairava. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Trimūrti. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Rudragaurī. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Āmūrti. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Rudragaurī. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Ṛṣabha. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Kṣetrapāla. Oṃ Hāṃ, svāhā to Caṇḍeśa. Oṃ Hāṃ.

*Śivasūryāya svāhā*. *Oṃ hāṃ śivāya gurave svāhā*. *Oṃ astrāya svāhā*. Having thus offered libations, then, having sipped water (*ācamana*) and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and limbs, one should grasp the nectar situated within the water with the root mantra and the goad-mudrā (*aṅkuśamudrā*).

Having visualized entry into the station of the *bindu* by means of the heart-mantra, having emerged from the water, having recited the root mantra one hundred and eight times, having meditated upon the Śiva-gāyatrī, and having offered the fruit of the recitation, one should satisfy [the deity]. (l6) Thus ends the procedure for the specific libation (*tarpaṇa*) which is a limb of the eightfold binding ritual.
(The entry into the sacrificial hall:

This [procedure], however, is primarily a subsidiary rite common to all scriptural traditions; it is recorded here by virtue of its illustrative force. In the case of the divine initiation (*devadīkṣā*), the performance should be carried out according to that specific method, as well as the special libation (*viśeṣatarpaṇa*). Thereafter, preceded by the recitation for an auspicious day (*puṇyāhavācana*), accompanied by the sounding of all musical instruments and the chanting of benedictions (*svastivācana*)—

Having entered the interior preceded by a distinguished gift for the right foot, one should perform the worship of Gaṇeśa. This is the sacrifice to Vighneśvara. From the first leaf of this book up to the twelfth leaf, it should be performed here as well according to the method of worshipping Vighneśvara.

Then the preceptor, having performed the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkṛtya*), having prepared the general water offering (*sāmānyārghya*), having worshipped Vighneśvara according to the prescribed rite, and having offered prayers, makes the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "On this auspicious lunar day,

for the purpose of removing all misfortunes and attaining all desired goals for all people— including ourselves and others, such as Brāhmaṇas and so forth, residing in this place, as well as for those who perform righteous deeds, for lords, and for those who cause the performance of Śiva-dharma."

In accordance with the method taught in the *Kāmikāgama*, for the sake of attaining the complete fruit of the worship— free from deficiencies in mantra-practice and meditative cultivation— for the rite of restoring the dilapidated and performing the eight-fold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*) that is about to be performed, [I offer this] to this Goddess, Śrī...

"Having made the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): 'In the Śiva-sacrifice for the restoration of the dilapidated temple and its eight-fold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*) of Sadāśiva, the Lord of Veṇuvana, which is about to be performed, I shall first perform the Anujñāpājā; as a limb of that, I shall perform the Puṇyāhavācana,' [the officiant] should, at the conclusion of the Mahāsandhi-pūjā arranged by the Nityapūjā-ācārya, duly prepare the Puṇyāha, the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), and the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*)."
Immediately thereafter, the teacher,

having seated himself facing north upon a tortoise-seat to the south of the altar, having performed the ritual integration of the limbs (*sakalīkaraṇa*), and having carried out the rites beginning with the purification of oneself (*ātmaśuddhi*) and ending with the purification of the mantras (*mantraśuddhi*) preceded by breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), [he should place] Śiva before him.

On a purified altar-platform, adorned with colored powders, garlands, and the like, having placed the *prahya* and other items there, and having strewn it around with *darbha* grass, flowers, and parched grain (*lāja*), one should place upon it a new copper jar (*ghaṭa*) of the capacity of a *droṇa* of water— or a *lakṣmavardhanī* of that same kind— wrapped with thread, fumigated, washed, and consecrated for the Śiva-sacrifice and the water-pot (*kumbha*).

Having placed upon the sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍila*) a *vardhanī* vessel—characterized by such marks, capable of holding four *prasthas* of water, and distinguished by being wrapped with thread—and sixteen jars each measuring two *prasthas*, [one should recite] these [mantras]: "The waters indeed are all this...
(*āpo vā idaṃ sarvam*).

All beings are water; the *praṇava* is water; cattle are water; food is water; immortality is water. The sovereign (*samrāj*) is water; the radiant one (*virāj*) is water; the all-ruling one (*surāj*) is water. The meters are water; the lights are water; truth is water;
all deities are water. *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, the waters are *oṃ*. He leads forward the waters; by means of these very peaceful waters, he [removes] his impurity.

One pacifies [the site] by filling those [vessels] with water filtered through a cloth; then, with the root mantra, one places the fourteen substances together with the nine gems and gold— namely, the water for the feet (*pādya*), the water for sipping (*ācamana*), the respectful offering (*arghya*),
and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).

Kuśa-water, milk, curd, and ghee—these are for the preparation of the nine jars. Sandalwood, powdered saffron, *laghumāṃsī*, *mura*, honey, combined with *strīvera* and turmeric, constitute the sixteen-fold bath (*asnāpana*).

Having thus arranged these sixteen substances with the root mantra, and having adorned [the jars] internally with *kūrca*-grass, mango sprouts, and so forth, [one recites]: "O Earth, be soft... (*syonā pṛthivī bhavā na*).

Having recited the mantra: "May that which dwells upon the mountain peaks, which is vast and wide, grant us protection," one should worship with: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; obeisance to Ananta; obeisance to Dharma; obeisance to Jñāna;
obeisance to Vairāgya; obeisance to Aiśvarya; obeisance to Adharma.*

Salutation to Ignorance (*ajñāna*). Salutation to Non-detachment (*avairāgya*). Salutation to Non-sovereignty (*anaiśvarya*). Salutation to the lower covering (*adhacchadana*). Salutation to the upper covering (*ūrdhvacchadana*). Salutation to the bulbous root (*kanda*). Salutation to the seed (*bīja*). Salutation to the stalk (*nāla*). Salutation to the non-terrible ones (*aghora*). Salutation to the thorns (*kaṇṭaka*). (L4) Salutation to the filaments (*kesara*). Salutation to the lotus (*padma*). Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Vāmā. Salutation to Jyeṣṭhā. Salutation to Raudrī. Salutation to Kālī.

Salutation to Kalavikaraṇī; salutation to Balavikaraṇī; (l5) salutation to Balapramathanī; salutation to Sarvabhūtadamanī; salutation to Manonmanī; salutation to the Solar Orb; salutation to Brahmāṇī, the sovereign of the Solar Orb; salutation to the Lunar Orb; (l6)

Salutation to Vaiṣṇavī, the sovereign of the lunar maṇḍala. Salutation to the fire maṇḍala. Salutation to Rudrāṇī, the sovereign of the fire maṇḍala. Salutation to the power maṇḍala. Salutation to Īśvarī, the sovereign of the power maṇḍala. (L7) Salutation to the earth-power. Salutation to the action-power. Salutation to the knowledge-power. Salutation to the seat of the Śrī Devī.

I worship the Goddess, who possesses the form of a female crane shining like the lord of birds (a peacock), holding arrows that are as beautiful as fish; she who, through her vow of rice, bestows desired boons upon the leader of the city of the great non-lotus (the sun). *Obeisance to the illustrious Śivamūrti. Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Illustrious Goddess.* Now, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the five Brahmans, [one should perform] the pure *Mātṛkā*.
Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of Śrīkaṇṭha and the Mātṛkās, having filled the joined palms with flowers,
(l2) having recited the root mantra of the Goddess Śrī and invoked her into the central jar, and having offered a welcome and the guest-water (*arghya*),
[one should worship] O God of gods, Lord of the World, until the concluding rite of the worship.
First, with a spirit of affection, [I invoke] you in the image:

(l3) *śrīṃ hrīṃ haiṃ*—I cause you to be present. *aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ*—I cause you to be firmly established. *oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ*—make your presence manifest, make it manifest! *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the binding of the directions. (l4)

Three claps of the hands. *Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrī kānmatyambāyai namaḥ*. O Great Goddess, united with Śiva from the center of the pericarp of the heart-lotus, enter [here] along with Kubhara and Rāvaṇa. For the benefit of all the worlds, O Mother, manifest Your presence! [Perform] the Śakti-mudrā and the Padma-mudrā.

Be present through the *mukulamudrā*, the *śaśikarṇikā*, the *manorathā*, the *yoni*, and the *namaskāramudrā*. Having thus prayed: "We know Gaṇāmbikā; we meditate upon the Great Goddess; may Gaurī inspire us. Oṃ hāṃ.

KĀYE VILA HRĪṂ HAṂSAKAHALA HRĪṂ HAṂSAṂ SA ŚRĪṂ KRĀṂ KRĪṂ KROṂ YARALAVAŚAṢASAHOṂ | HAṂSASSOHAM | Her vital breaths are here; her life-force is established here—in the principle of life (*jīvatattva*) of the venerable mother Śrīkāntimatī—her all the senses, speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and the vital airs: prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna, are right here.

"Having arrived, may they dwell happily for a long time in this jar, svāhā! Śrīṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ, I establish Gaurī. Having entered, [one offers] water for the feet, water for sipping, and the arghya offering, ending with "namaḥ svadhā svāhā," having given them while accompanied by the heart-mantra.

Having offered the *arghya* on the head with the *Īśāna* mantra; having adorned [the deity] with garments, scents, saffron, flower garlands, and wreaths; having worshipped [him]; having offered incense and lamps with the *Kavaca* mantra; having offered fruits as the food offering (*naivedya*) with the root mantra; (l4) and again having offered water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), *arghya*, incense, lamps, the waving of lights (*ārātrika*), the purifier (*apavitra*), recitation (*japa*), and betel leaf (*tāmbūla*); and having made the prayer: "Obeisance to the seat of Manonmanī in the northeast (*īśāna*)."
(15) Salutation to the form of Manonmanī, who has the luster of pure crystal, upon the lotus of the earth.
[The syllable] beginning with *kā*, ending with *ya*, joined with *sa*, ending with *mā*, and conjoined with the letter *ma*.
The seed-syllable of Śakti is said to be joined with Bindu and Nāda.

"Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ, I invoke Manonmanī. Having thus performed the worship beginning with the invocation and ending with the recitation of the mantra, [he offers salutations]: "Homage to Vāmāsana in the east.
[I salute] Vāmā, who appears playful and is adorned with a crown and other ornaments."
One should cause the Goddess, who bears the conch and the discus, together with all her retinues, to enter from the center of the heart-lotus into the middle of the *vardhanī* vessel:
*Oṃ hāṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ sūṃ sraiṃ srauṃ sraḥ, I invoke Vāmā*. [The rites of] invocation and so forth.
Having completed the worship at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), one should worship [the deity] in the southeast pitcher (*kalaśa*) to its right with: "Obeisance to the seat of Jyeṣṭhā.
[One should meditate on] Jyeṣṭhā as being yellow in color, a traveler, lotus-eyed, adorned with all ornaments, possessing beautiful breasts, and in the full bloom of youth.

Oṃ hāṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ sūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ, I invoke Jyeṣṭhā. Having thus invoked her, and having performed the worship beginning with the ritual installation and ending with the recitation of mantras, [one offers] obeisance to the seat of Raudrī on the south (l3).
The goddess Raudrī is white in appearance, three-eyed, and holds a trident;
she is adorned with all ornaments and possesses a serene lotus-face.
Oṃ hāṃ krāṃ krīṃ kūṃ (krūṃ) kroṃ kraḥ hrīṃ, I invoke Raudrī. Having worshipped her from the invocation up to the end of the recitation: "Homage to the seat of Kālī in the southwest.
[I worship] the goddess Kālī, who resembles a dark blue cloud and holds a skull-bowl.
One should place her, adorned with all ornaments, within the pitcher.
*Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ klāṃ krīṃ klīṃ klauṃ klauṃ klaḥ srīṃ, I invoke Kālī.* Having worshipped her from the rite of installation (*sthāpana*) up to the recitation (*japa*), [one should say]:
"In the west, obeisance to the seat of Kalavikaraṇī."
She is dark-complexioned, holding a lute, a noose, a goad, and granting boons;
she is endowed with all limbs and possesses a serene lotus-face.

Salutation to the form of Kalavikaraṇī. Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ śrāṃ śrūṃ śraiṃ śrauṃ śraḥ, I invoke Kalavikaraṇī. Having performed the worship beginning with the ritual installation (sthāpana) and ending with the recitation (japa), [one offers] salutation to the seat of Balavikaraṇī in the north-western direction.
Yellowish-red in complexion, holding a sword and a shield,
adorned with all ornaments, and wearing a crown shaped like a casket.

Salutation to the form that causes the transformation of power (*balavikaraṇīmūrti*). *Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣiṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ*, I invoke Balavikaraṇī. Having performed the worship from the installation (*sthāpana*) up to the recitation (*japa*), [one says]: "In the north, salutation to the seat of Balapramathinī (*balapramathanyāsanāya namaḥ*).
The goddess Balapramathinī has a luster like a massed cloud.
She has four arms and three eyes, and is adorned with all ornaments.
O Goddess Padmā with a serene countenance, salutations to you!

Salutations to the form that subdues the powerful! Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ brāṃ brīṃ būṃ (brūṃ) braiṃ brauṃ braḥ, I invoke Balapramathanī. Having performed the worship from the installation up to the recitation of mantras, [one should offer] to the seat of Sarvabhūtadamanī in the northeast.
Homage! Homage to the form that subdues all beings!
She who subdues all beings is cloud-colored, in the full bloom of youth, endowed with all auspicious marks, and adorned with every ornament.

Salutation to the form that subdues all beings (*sarvabhūtadamani*). Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ sauṃ klīṃ eṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ śrīṃ, I invoke Sarvabhūtadamani. Having worshipped [her] from the rites of installation (*sthāpana*) up to the recitation (*japa*), [one should worship] outside of that.

In the pitchers of the eastern direction and so forth: in the east—*oṃ umāyai namaḥ*; in the southeast—*oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*; in the south—*oṃ durgāyai namaḥ*; in the southwest—*oṃ sāvitrīyai namaḥ*; in the west—*oṃ uṣāyai namaḥ*; in the northwest—*oṃ pratyuṣāyai namaḥ*;
in the north—*oṃ śamanāya namaḥ*; in the northeast—*oṃ unmanyai namaḥ*. With these [mantras], which serve as the seats and forms for these [deities]...

Having performed the worship from the invocation (*āvāhana*) up to the end of the recitation (*japa*), one should place nine lotuses made of turmeric and flour paste to the west of the bathing area. Having deposited the ritual arrays (*vyūha*) and so forth upon them, and having strewn them around with *darbha* grass and flowers, one should set the vessels upon them.

Having filled [the vessels] with pure water that has become like a garment, one should place ghee in the first vessel starting from the south, consecrating it with the root mantra (*mūla*). In the second vessel, [place] honey measuring a *kuḍava*; in the third, five *palas* of perfume;

in the fourth, *bilva*, *niguṇḍī*, *upamārga*, *śamī*, and *ulasī* leaves, each measuring one cubit (*hasta*) and consecrated separately with the root mantra; and in the fifth, the essence of sugarcane.

In the sixth vessel, having placed half a *prastha* each of *mallikā*, *jātī*, *kuṭaja*, *mālatī*, sprouts, and *mallikā* flowers, separately filling them to the capacity of an *añjali*; in the seventh vessel, the nine gems;
and in the eighth vessel, turmeric.
Half a *prastha* of powder: in a new vessel, having taken *uśīra*, *hrīvera*, fresh camphor, *kuṅkuma* flower, and *mṛgamada*, three *karṣas* each;

having placed all these in those jars with the root mantra (*mūla*), and having worshipped them with the powers beginning with Vāmā, having invoked [the deity] and performed worship, together with the Brahmins, [one should recite] the *Śrīrudracamaka*, the *Puruṣasūkta*, the *Devīsūkta*, the *Śrīsūkta*, and the *Durgāsūkta*.

Having caused those skilled in mantras to perform the recitation (*japa*) of the *abliṅga*, *hiraṇyavarṇa*, *pavamāna*, the five *śānti* mantras, as well as the mantras of Śrīvidyā, Ṣoḍaśī, Bālā, Śyāmalā, Durgā, Pratyaṅgirā, and the goddess Mātaṅgī individually according to their capacity;

Having performed the recitation according to the prescribed number, having touched the water-pot, and having performed the recitation while moving around it counter-clockwise, being authorized for the sake of the *śānti*-oblation,

he should perform the fire-ritual in the *yonikuṇḍa* according to the procedure taught for the fire-ritual— beginning with the consecration of the pit (*kuṇḍasaṃskāra*) and ending with the marriage ceremony— and having worshipped the seat in the fire, starting from Śakti and ending with Śakti.

Having invoked the Pāśupata weapon and worshipped it, [one offers] ten oblations of clarified butter with the Pāśupata mantra at the place of the food offering (naivedya). Then follows the principal homa: one hundred and eight oblations each with palāśa, apāmārga, dūrvā, and mango leaves, performed separately.

The oblation is performed with the Pāśupata [mantra]. With the Pāśupata weapon-mantra, one hundred oblations of *caru* are offered. Then follows the oblation of clarified butter (*ājya*), and then the oblation of *kramayī*. At the beginning and in the middle, there is a prayer: "O Blessed One, whatever fault has occurred in this rite through knowledge or ignorance, please grant its pacification. Having thus prayed, [the offering] is joined with all the ritual substances.

Having offered the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation with the mantra "O bearer of offerings," and having offered the *jayādi*, the *abhyātāna*, and the *rāṣṭrabhṛt* in sequence; and for the sake of removing the defects of all deficiencies, having offered separately twenty-five times with clarified butter using the five-weapon (*pañcāstra*) mantra;
[he should worship] his own fire.

Having joined the *pāśupatāstra* with the *kumbha*, having offered oblations (*homa*) with [the prescribed substances], having given the inner and outer offerings (*antarbali* and *bahirbali*), and having dismissed the fire (*agni*) and performed the ritual attendance (*upasthāna*), one should then perform the worship of the door (*dvārapūjā*). Having sprinkled the door with water from the general *arghya* vessel using the *astra-mantra*, one should place a conch on the right side of the door, saying "Salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi," and on the left, "Salutation to Padmanidhi. The wealth of these two belongs to the door.

And on both sides [are the two goddesses] holding swords and shields in their hands; they are adorned with crested crowns and embellished with a dark complexion. Having meditated [upon them] and having worshipped [them], [one should say]: "Homage to the seat of Sarasvatī in the middle above the door."
One should meditate upon Sarasvatī, who is white in complexion, clad in white garments, holding a rosary and a book with her right and left hands respectively, and is exceedingly gracious.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. On the right door-jamb (l5): obeisance to the seat of Gaṅgā.
[One should visualize] Gaṅgā seated upon a crocodile, with her two hands—the left and the right—[held in the gesture of granting boons].
She is white in form, holding a blue lotus and a full water-pot.
Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā. On the northern branch, obeisance to Yamunā seated upon a tortoise; she is dark-complexioned, and in her two hands, left and right, she holds a water-pot.
And I contemplate Yamunā, who bears a blue lotus.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Yamunā. Again, in the middle of the door: obeisance to the seat of Mahālakṣmī.
She holds a bilva fruit and a lotus in her left and right hands.
To Mahāśrī, who is golden-hued and being bathed by two elephants holding water-pots:
Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Śrī Mahālakṣmī. Again, on the southern branch: obeisance to Ṛddhi. On the northern branch: obeisance to Samṛddhi.
On the southern door-panel: obeisance to Vimalā. On the northern door-panel: [obeisance to Aruṇā].

"Salutation to Subāhu! Salutation to Brahmā, the Lord of the Site! Having thus worshipped, [he recites] "To the Weapon, *huṃ phaṭ*. For the purpose of dispelling obstacles with three strikes of the heel, he says: "Oṃ haṃ (hāṃ), to the Weapon, *phaṭ*.
(L3) Thus, he rings the bell. Having cast a flower and taken hold of the right branch, he enters within, preceded by his right foot.

In the middle of the threshold: "Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Astra-Śakti"—having thus worshipped; and on the western foot: "Salutation to Māyā-Śakti"—having thus fully honored [them], and having tied a concealed cloth, [he should proceed] upon the Kūrma-seat in the great pavilion.

Sitting facing north, one should again perform the rites from the purification of oneself (*ātmaśuddhi*) up to the purification of the mantra (*mantraśuddhi*) as previously described. Having prepared the special water-offering (*viśeṣārghya*) combined with all substances such as saffron and flowers, one should worship [it] with:
*oṃ hrīṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ*; *anantāya namaḥ*; *dharmāya namaḥ*; *jñānāya namaḥ*; *vairāgyāya*.
Salutations! Salutations to Sovereignty! Salutations to Him whose form is as radiant as ten million suns!
Salutations to the One seated upon the infinite throne! Having thus worshipped:
"We know Gaṇāmbikā; we meditate upon Mahādeva."
"May the Goddess inspire us.
Having thus worshipped, [offer] the food offering (*naivedya*), flowers, and all other items, and then perform the ritual dismissal (*nirmālya*).

Having offered [the deity] to the bearer of the *liya* (lyadhāriṇī), one should consecrate [the image] with forty substances such as the "water of Śiva" (*śivajala*) and others—consisting of pure water strained through cloth and mixed with liquid ingredients like *elā* and so forth—while reciting the *astra-mantra*: "Oṃ hrīṃ astraśaktaye namaḥ. Then, preceded by the recitation of the root mantra of Gaurī, the *Śrīrudra*, and the *Umāsūkta*, one should perform the special ablutions (*snāna*) using the sixteen substance-filled jars previously established, along with various types of water.

Having consecrated [the deity] with the root mantra, having offered the mantra-food, and having presented water for the feet, water for sipping, and the arghya offering, one should wipe [the image] with a fine cloth using the Goddess’s weapon-mantra,
and [apply] garments, perfumes, saffron, musk, camphor, and gorocana.

Having especially adorned [the deity] with garlands of *sīgandha*, *madana*, and *mālā*, as well as with *amlāna* garlands and lamps that do not go out, one should worship with the mantra: "Homage to the Obstacle-Remover in the North. Having thus worshipped and prayed, "I worship the Śrī Devī," one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*). In the region below the image, one should say: "Oṃ Hrīṃ, homage to the Support-Power (*ādhāraśakti*); homage to Ananta; homage to Dharma."

Homage! Homage to Knowledge! Homage to Dispassion! (l6) Homage to Sovereignty! Homage to the Lotus! Homage to the one whose form possesses the radiance of ten million suns, to the one seated upon the infinite throne! Having thus worshipped: "We know Gaṇāmbikā; we meditate upon Mahādeva; may that Goddess inspire us. (l7)

Having thus performed the worship, and having offered all the food offerings (*naivedya*), flowers, and so forth to the *nirmālyadhāriṇī*, one should consecrate [the deity] with forty substances such as the water of Śiva, mixed with water-ingredients like cardamom (*elā*) and purified with half-water strained through a cloth, while reciting the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*): "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the power of the weapon (*astraśakti*). Thus, with these various waters.

Having bathed [the deity] with the distinguished ablutions using the sixteen-substance jar previously established, preceded by the recitation of the *Gaurī-mūlamantra*, the *Śrīrudra*, and the *Umāsūkta*; and having offered food, the sacrificial oblation (*naivedya*), water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), and the respectful offering (*arghya*) with the root mantra, O Goddess;
[then] with the weapon mantra (*astramantra*)—

Having wiped [the image] with a fine cloth, and having adorned it with garments, perfumes, saffron, musk, camphor, *gorocana*, fragrant garlands, and so forth—especially with fresh *mālatī* flowers and lamps that have not gone out—one should worship with the mantra: "Obeisance to Pratyūhā in the North. Having thus worshipped and prayed, "I worship the Goddess Śrī," one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*).

Beneath this image (l5), in the region below: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; obeisance to Ananta; obeisance to Dharma; obeisance to Jñāna; obeisance to Vairāgya; obeisance to Aiśvarya; obeisance to Adharma; obeisance to Ajñāna (l6).

Homage to non-detachment; homage to lack of sovereignty; homage to the lower covering; homage to the upper covering; homage to the bulb; homage to the seed; homage to the stalk; homage to the sprout; homage to the thorns; homage to the petals; homage to the filaments; homage to the pericarp; *hrīṃ*, homage to the lotus; *hrīṃ*, homage to Vāmā; homage to Jyeṣṭhā.

Homage to Raudrī! Homage to Kālī! Homage to Kalavikaraṇī! Homage to Balavikaraṇī! Homage to Balapramathinī! Homage to Sarvabhūtadamanī! Homage to Manonmanī! Homage to the Solar Disk! Homage to Brahmāṇī, the Sovereign of the Solar Disk!
Salutation to the lunar maṇḍala; salutation to Vaiṣṇavī, the presiding deity of the lunar maṇḍala. Salutation to the fiery maṇḍala; salutation to Rudrāṇī, the presiding deity of the fiery maṇḍala.

Salutation to the power-maṇḍala; salutation to Īśvarī, the presiding deity of the power-maṇḍala. Salutation to the power of will; salutation to the power of action; salutation to the power of knowledge. Salutation to the seat of the Śrī Devī.
Salutations! Salutations to the form of the illustrious Goddess!

(l4) Salutations to the mother Śrī Kāntimatī! Then, having performed the placement of the five Brahmans, and having performed the placement of the Mātṛkās and so forth, as well as the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkās, in their respective locations, distinguished by the seed-syllable of Māyā; (l5)
Thereafter, the placement of the twenty-five kalās (pañcaviṃśatikalānyāsa) should be performed:
1. *Īśānāya namaḥ*—on the head;
2. *Oṃ hrīṃ tārāyai namaḥ*—on the face.
3. Oṃ heṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣā—? 4. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vidyā—in the heart. (l6. 5.
Oṃ huṃ, obeisance to Aghorā—thus everywhere.
6. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Bhṛtyu. 7. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Śraddhā.
8. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jaṭhara—on the right arm.
9. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Medhā—on the stomach.
10. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Svadhā—at the navel.
11. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Svati. (1) [This is] the ninth Aghora-kalā.
In the vulva: Oṃ hrīṃ vāmadevāyai namaḥ—in the vulva everywhere.
Oṃ hrīṃ pālinyai namaḥ—in the secret place.
Oṃ hrīṃ jvālinyai namaḥ—on the right thigh. Oṃ hrīṃ dṛṣṭāyai namaḥ—on the left thigh.
Oṃ hrīṃ dhṛtyai namaḥ—on the right knee.
Oṃ hrīṃ kṣmāyai namaḥ – on the left knee;
oṃ hrīṃ matyai namaḥ – on the left calf;
oṃ hrīṃ cintāyai namaḥ – on the back.
Oṃ hrīṃ pūtyai namaḥ — on the right side.
Oṃ hrīṃ kāntyai namaḥ — thus in the Vāmadeva-kalā (16).
On the right foot:
*oṃ hāṃ sadyojātāyai namaḥ*—thus [the mantra] is applied everywhere on the right foot.
*oṃ hrīṃ dāntyai namaḥ*—on the right hand.
Oṃ hrīṃ dayāyai namaḥ — on the left hand; (l5.
oṃ hrīṃ stutyai namaḥ — on the right breast;
oṃ hrīṃ dūtyai namaḥ — on the left breast.
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Sādhyā; [this is] the Sadyojāta-kalā. ||6|| Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Vidyādehā; oṃ hauṃ, huṃ to the eyes. ||5|| (l6. Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ vidyādehāyai namaḥ | oṃ hauṃ netrebhyo huṃ.
Oṃ hrīṃ gaurīyai namaḥ;
oṃ hrīṃ mahāgaurī rudradayite svāhā. Having thus offered a handful of flowers, one should meditate upon the body of wisdom (vidyādeha).

I worship the Goddess with the *iṣacāru* [mantra] and the heart [mantra]. Having offered the water for rinsing (*ācamana*) three times, having offered the *arghya* on the head with the *īśāna* [mantra], having consecrated [her] with the root mantra through visualization, and having sprinkled [her] with the root mantra,
one should again offer the water for washing the feet (*pādya*) and so forth.

Having wiped [the deity] with a fine cloth, having adorned [it] with garlands of fragrant flowers and with saffron, musk, kastūrī, camphor, and cold water, having offered incense and lamps with the root mantra, having presented the sacrificial oblation (*havis*), and having performed the worship (*saṃpūjya*), I shall request permission for the worship of the enclosures (*āvaraṇapūjā*). Having received permission, I worship: *namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ īśānāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ*.
Salutation to Tatpuruṣa. Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, salutation to Aghorā.
(L4) Oṃ hrīṃ hiṃ, salutation to Vāmadevā. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Sadyojāta. Oṃ hrīṃ hāṃ, salutation to Hṛdayā. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Śirodevī. Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ, salutation to Śikhādevī. (L5)

*Namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ haiṃ*, salutation to the Goddess of Armor (*kavacadevī*). *Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ*, salutation to the Goddess of the Eyes (*netradevī*). *Oṃ hrīṃ haḥ*, salutation to the Goddess of the Weapon (*astradevī*).

Having thus worshipped in the positions beginning with Īśāna, and having displayed the Lotus Mudrā (*padmamudrā*) and the Yoni Mudrā (*yonimudrā*), [one offers salutation] to Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā together with the deities of the first enclosure (*prathamāvaraṇa*). On the petals: salutation to Vāmā.

Salutation to Jyeṣṭhā. Salutation to Raudrī. Salutation to Kālī. Salutation to Kalavikaraṇī. Salutation to Balavikaraṇī. Salutation to Balapramathanī. Salutation to Sarvabhūtadamanī. Salutation to Manonmanī. [These are] the deities of the second enclosure.

Salutation to the distinguished Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā. Having worshipped Ananteśa and the others in the middle of the petals: "Salutation to the distinguished Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā together with the deities of the third enclosure" at the base of the petals. Having worshipped Indra and the other world-protectors: "Salutation to Kāntimatī Ambā together with the deities of the fourth enclosure. Having worshipped Vajra and the others on the exterior of the petals: [the mantra continues].

Salutation to the venerable Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā together with the deities of the fifth enclosure. Thus is the daily worship of the five enclosures. However, in the occasional (naimittika) worship, the deities of the first enclosure begin from Īśāna and end with Astra.

Having worshipped [the central deity] in its respective place, and having worshipped the deities beginning with Vāmā on the tips of the petals, one should worship in the middle of the petals as follows: in the east—*śrīdevyai namaḥ*; in the south—*durgāyai namaḥ*; in the west—*oṃ hrīṃ huṃ devyai namaḥ*;
in the north—*oṃ hrīṃ śaśinyai namaḥ*; in the northeast—*oṃ gāyatryai namaḥ*; and between those two—*uṣādevyai namaḥ*.

Having thus worshipped the deities of the third enclosure—at the base of the petals: in the east—*oṃ hrīṃ prajādevyai namaḥ*; in the southeast—*oṃ hrīṃ medhāyai namaḥ*; in the south—*oṃ hrīṃ śrutidevyai namaḥ*.
In the southwest—salutation to Smṛtidevī. In the west—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Svāhādevī. In the northwest—oṃ hrīṃ vauṣaṭ, salutation to Devī. In the north—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Dhṛtidevī.
In the northeast—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Medhādevī. Having thus worshipped the deities of the fourth enclosure, outside of that—in the east—salutation to Mohinīdevī.
In the southeast—*oṃ peṣiṇī* (l2) *devyai namaḥ*.
In the south—*culyadevyai namaḥ*. In the southwest—*śikhaṇḍinīdevyai namaḥ*. In the west—*ulukhalidevyai namaḥ*. In the northwest—*mudgalīdevyai namaḥ*. (l3)

In the north: *namo musalidevyai*. In the northeast: *namo vardhamānadevyai*. Having thus worshipped the deities of the five enclosures (*pañcāvaraṇa*), one worships the seven Mothers, beginning with Brāhmī, in the sixth enclosure outside of that. Outside of that, starting from the east: *namaḥ vṛṣabhāya*, *namaḥ gaṇeśvarāya*, *namaḥ skandāya*, *namaḥ mahāśāstre*.
Salutation to Dhaneśvara;

salutation to Vīrabhadra; salutation to Kṣetrapāla; salutation to Bhāskara. Having thus worshipped the deities of the seven enclosures, [one worships] outside of that the eight world-protectors beginning with Indra.

Having worshipped the deities of the enclosure, and outside of that— having worshipped the nine deities of the outer enclosure beginning with Vajra— and having again offered incense and lamps, I duly present the great oblation (*mahāhavis*) consisting of various side-dishes, foods to be chewed, eaten, licked, sucked, and drinks, together with mung-bean rice, jaggery-rice, milk-rice, oily foods, curd-rice, and black-pepper rice; may the Blessed Lady accept this.
Having offered [the deity] as Maheśvarī, having presented betel-leaf and other offerings (*tāmbūlādi-naivedya*),

[one obtains] the fruits of the worship of the great lamps (*mahādīpa*), the recitation of the Vedas (*veda-pārāyaṇa*), benedictions (*āśīrvāda*), songs, Dravidian hymns (*drāviḍa-stuti*), dance (*nṛtta*), and the recitation of the *pavitra* mantra.

Having made the offering, having requested permission for the *homa*, and having received that permission, he approaches the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). Having performed the rites up to the marriage ceremony according to the method described in the *Agnikārya*, he invokes Gaurī—endowed with her seat and extending from Śakti to Śakti—into the midst of the fire. Having presented the offerings up to the *naivedya* with the *Sthāpinī* mantra, he performs a *samidh*-oblation of twenty-five palāśa wood pieces with the Gaurī-mantra.

Then the *vyāhṛtis*. Thus the oblation of clarified butter (*ājyahoma*). Thus the oblation of the sacrificial porridge (*caruhoma*). Then the *vyāhṛtis*. Having performed the rites from the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering up to the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), he should dismiss the Goddess residing in the fire. Then, having offered the *vyāhṛtis*.

Having offered the inner oblation (*antarbali*) and the outer oblation (*bahirbali*) according to the rules; having collected the ashes from the *homa*; having offered them to the Goddess with the root mantra; having performed it himself; having dismissed the fire;

having offered the fruit of the *homa* to the deities; having offered three handfuls of flowers with the root mantra; and having meditated upon the Goddess who grants desired boons, he should proclaim [the rite] together with the image-keepers (*mūrtipa*) and the Brahmins.
O God and Goddess, O Lord of the World, O Cause of Joy to the World,
O You who possess an undivided form, who pervade the universe, and who are both moving and unmoving!

O Goddess, you whose nature is the root-mantra and the rest, you who are the form of the *mūlādhāra*, you who are the form of primordial nature (*mūlaprakṛti*), and you who are the form of the foundational pillar— [you abide] in the knowledge of Śiva, in the bliss of Śiva, in the form of Śiva, and in that which has Śiva as its refuge.
O Goddess, you who abide within the syllable Oṃ, you are Unmanī, the Sovereign of Arising.
O Goddess, you who abide in all beings, the Great Sovereign of all the worlds,
you whose form is the nature of the Suṣumṇā situated between the Iḍā and Piṅgalā.
Residing in the center of the divine earrings, she is the beloved form of the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) and so forth;
between the two, *prāṇa* and *apāna*, she is the *haṃsa* in the supreme cause. She is the Supreme, whose nature is the form of the sprout of the seed-syllable *haṃsa*.
O Viśvarūpā, Great Goddess, the cause of all auspiciousness!
I shall now announce the ritual for the restoration and consecration of the dilapidated [temple];
O Śaṅkarī, be present here as I begin it.
May the Great Goddess bring this to completion here without obstacle;
O Goddess, make the ritual action free from deficiency and fruitful.
May the kingdom of the king... be entirely devoid of all calamities.
And especially for the protection of people such as ourselves—
O Śivā, sovereign of the entire world, eternal salutations to you!
O Īśvarī, grant me permission for the performance of the eightfold binding.

"Let it be so," said the Goddess; and having received permission by the command of Śiva, that most excellent Guru, filled with devotion, should compose the Devī-tantras. Thus, upon the Goddess's authorization, [the Kāmika-āgama] arises from the daily worship.

Now, the authorization of the Brahmins: Then the teacher, having summoned distinguished Vedic scholars (*śrotriya*) and men of knowledge (*jñānin*) into the presence of the Goddess, says to each one individually: "We choose you for the purpose of authorizing the restoration of the old [temple], the eightfold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*), and the sacrifice to the Goddess.
Thus he speaks to the Brahmins...
Having seen those initiated by Śaśivat, he should worship them in their presence; having placed betel to the south, with the mantra "Obeisance to the assembly" (*namassadase*), [he recites]:

"Obeisance to the assembly, obeisance to the lord of the assembly, obeisance to the leader of friends, obeisance to the eye, obeisance to heaven, obeisance to earth, obeisance to Kaṭyā, and to the one who knows the Veda, whether he has come hither or departed."
He speaks on all sides:
"They all praise the sun alone as the first oblation, Agni as the second, and [the sun] as the third. He says in the Brāhmaṇa, "Speak of all those who are the divine powers of the gods"; therefore...
"One should pay homage day after day to the learned Brahmins; one should not proclaim the lineage of one who has perished. This alone pleases the deities. Having prayed with this mantra:
"O entire assembly, please accept this gold, whatever fee is offered, the prescribed fee, and the betel leaf, which have been presented by me at the soles of your feet. Of this—

For the sake of performing the *devīyāga*— the restoration and eightfold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*) of the Goddess, the venerable Mother Kāntimatī— grant your grace so that there may be the attainment of fitness to bring about the destruction of all [obstacles].
May the practices of the *śruti*, *smṛti*, and traditional conduct purify [this rite].

"O forms of Kāntimatī, you will grant me permission for the eight-fold binding (*aṣṭabandha*). Having thus entreated them and received their permission from them, saying "He shall do so," he should dismiss them. This, however, is the permission regarding the vital breaths (*prāṇānujñā*) according to the tradition of those who know the right method (*nyāyajñaja*). Then follows the Great Resolve (*mahāsaṅkalpa*). The preceptor, having performed the ritual of total identification (*sakalīkṛtya*), should prepare the general water offering (*sāmānyārghya*) for the purpose of worshipping Vighneśa.
Having worshipped Vighneśvara according to the prescribed rules, and having requested [permission] from the Guru and prostrated before him,

one should perform three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*)— consisting of inhalation (*pūraka*), retention (*kumbhaka*), and exhalation (*recaka*)— in their proper sequence, with counts of thirty-two and twice that number [sixty-four] respectively; then, having restrained [the breath], one should again [perform it] with both hands joined in the *saṃhitā* gesture.

Having taken darbha grass, having placed the right hand over the left and the right foot over the left, being composed, he should sit upon his seat. Recalling Śiva along with the presiding deities of the specific forms (*viśeṣaṇamūrtipaiḥ*), and together with the Brahmins learned in the Vedas (*brāhmaṇavidyā*) and all the devotees beginning with those who have acquired knowledge, he should perform the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*) and the auspicious recitations of Śiva’s names.

Reciting these two verses: "That alone is the auspicious moment, that alone is the excellence of the stars, that alone is the strength of the moon; that alone is the power of knowledge and the power of destiny—when I remember the pair of feet of the Lord of Gaurī."

Śiva, Śiva! By the command of Śambhu, on this auspicious lunar day, [may there be well-being] for all people existing in this region, including ourselves and others— especially those who perform the *śivadharma*, those who approve of it, those who incite it, those who serve it, and all living beings employed in its execution.

Specifically, for the sake of the king and Queen Kāntimatī, in order to remove royal defects caused by the decay of the eight bonds in the east, [the temple was built]; to remove the affliction of fire caused by the decay of the eight bonds in the southeast; to remove all diseases arising from the decay of the medicinal herbs in the southern direction; and to remove the defects of the village caused by the decay of the medicinal herbs in the southwest.

For the sake of removing the defects arising from old medicine located in the western quarter, and for the sake of removing the defects of women of all castes arising from old medicine located in the northwestern quarter;
[and] for the sake of [removing] the defect regarding sons arising from bondage and old [medicine] located in the northern quarter.
For the purpose of cessation: for the sake of ceasing the defects arising from the eight bonds located in the directions starting with Īśāna;
for the sake of ceasing all defects arising from the eight bonds located in the intermediate directions starting with the East;

(l5) for the sake of ceasing such defects of negligence as the disease of fever, the defect of fissures, the loss of everything, and so forth; and for the sake of ceasing the defects of famine caused by the shifting of the Nandyāvarta stone.

By means of the removal of all defects arising from the potential deficiency of the daily (*nitya*), occasional (*naimittika*), and optional (*kāmya*) worship, special worship, regular festivals, and so forth, as well as the fire-rituals (*agnikārya*), offerings of oblations (*balidāna*), and great festivals, [this leads to] the performance of all rites (*anuṣṭhitasarvakriyā*).

For the sake of attaining the complete fruit, for the sake of pleasing the illustrious Kāntimatī, through the grace of the illustrious Kāntimatī, and for the sake of accomplishing all desired objects and attaining the fourfold fruit, according to the method taught in the *Kāmika* and other Āgamas, [this work] concerning the Mother, the illustrious Kāntimatī, consists of the restoration of the dilapidated [temple] (*jīrṇoddhāra*) and the eight-fold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*), beginning with the rite of germinating seeds (*aṅkura*) and ending with the sacrifice of the three fortnights (*tripakṣayajana*).

Distinguished by [the prescribed] materials, performed morning and evening, accompanied by worship, recitation (*japa*), burnt offerings (*havana*), the complete recitation of the Vedas (*vedapārāyaṇa*), special adoration, and propitiatory oblations (*śāntihoma*) for a duration of nine days; including the complete recitation of the root mantra and many other mantras along with the Vedas; provided with the feeding of countless Brahmins; preceded by the application of the eight fragrances and the placement of the eight sounds (*aṣṭadhvanyāsa*); and intended for the pacification of the heat of bondage.

I shall perform the Devī-yāga, characterized by numerous offerings such as various consecrations— including all kinds of supreme incense, medicinal oils, and so forth— and distinguished by many ritual services,
using whatever materials are available.

I shall satisfy the illustrious Queen Kāntimatī—who is distinguished by her practice of the ten kinds of giving and other manifold mental resolves, and who is devoted to the performance of the thirty-two dharmas.
Having thus formed this resolve, the prayer follows: "I shall do this; and through your grace, for the sake of the world, I shall act for your purpose with mind, deed, and speech."

"I have no other recourse. I have been commanded by the Blessed One, who holds authority over his teachers: 'For the sake of protecting all beings, empower me and cause the ritual to be performed. O Viśvabheṣaja, [protect] me, your child," thus he should pray.

Thus concludes the Great Resolve (*mahāsaṅkalpa*). Now follows the recitation for the auspicious day (*svastipuṇyāhavācana*), in accordance with the ritual injunctions of the *Kāmikāgama*. Then the Preceptor (*deśika*), having smeared the ground in front of Śiva with cow dung, draws a square measuring two cubits on all sides. Having fashioned an eight-petaled lotus using yellow pigment and powdered flour, he [scatters] rice and other grains over a space of one cubit.
Having prepared a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) measuring one *droṇa* of rice,

half of that amount of sesame seeds, half of that amount of black gram (*māṣa*), and half of that amount of parched grain (*lāja*), and having drawn an eight-petaled lotus in its center, he should surround it with *darbha* grass and flowers, and [place] a new copper vessel.

One should prepare a *vardhanī* [water-pot] made of clay, which is twelve finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) in height, twenty-two finger-breadths in circumference, and provided with a square neck measuring half a finger-breadth; its belly is six finger-breadths in height, its base is five finger-breadths, and its spout is four finger-breadths in measure—being of such a nature, is it not? If it is made of clay, it should be completed accordingly.

Having taken up a *vardhanī* vessel that is free from defects such as being cracked by rice-grains and possesses auspicious marks like the *bimba* fruit, and having wrapped it with a thread around its opening like a lattice window, and having placed the *pavitra*,
one should perform three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) preceded by the trampling of the head of Vighneśvara.

Having made this resolve on an auspicious lunar day, [one should think]: "I shall perform the *svasti-aṣṭabandhana* and the *puṇyāhavācana* for this lady, the venerable Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā. [One should say: "Obeisance to Ramā upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*). Having worshipped Ramā, offered incense and a lamp, and filled [the vessel] with water while reciting the mantra *āpo vā idam*, [it should be prepared] together with a *kūrca* grass-bundle, a lid, cloth, and gold.

Having adorned [the deity] with flowers and other offerings: *namo 'nantāya*, *namo dharmāya*, *namo jñānāya*, *namo vairāgyāya*, *nama aiśvaryāya*, *namaḥ padmāya*. To the east—*namo brahmaṇe*; in the center—*namo viṣṇave*; at the back (*pṛṣṭhe*)—*namo rudrāya*; on the right side—*namo nandine*; to the north—[namo mahākālāya].*

—Salutation to Mahākāla. In the nose: salutation to Vighneśvara. In the midst of the water—from the east onwards: salutation to Gaṅgā; salutation to Yamunā; salutation to Narmadā; salutation to Sarasvatī; salutation to Sindhu; salutation to Godāvarī; salutation to Kāverī; salutation to Tāmraparṇī. Having worshipped thus, having invoked Varuṇa, and having displayed the great mudrās beginning with the *sthāpanā* [mudrā].
Having worshipped the body [of the deity] with offerings of enjoyment (*bhoga*) and limbs (*aṅga*), and having presented incense and lamps,

and having performed worship up to the food offering (*naivedya*) and the recitation (*japa*); then, having summoned Brahmins well-versed in the four Vedas and having chosen them for the sake of the *puṇyāha* rite, saying "We choose you," [he should worship] Śiva with his intellect.

Having worshipped them, one should place [the materials] for the *śivataṇḍula* rite—accompanied by gold, betel nuts (*kramuka*), and *bṛhatī* fruits—into a vessel near the rice. Having worshipped with the mantras, "In this [vessel], *namaḥ* to the Heart" and "*namaḥ* to Candra," and having offered incense and lamps, the preceptor says: "Permitted by you, I shall cause the proclamation of the auspicious day (*puṇyāha*) to be made. [The others respond: "Oṃ, let it be proclaimed! (*oṃ vācyatām*).

The response: "Om, O waters. The teacher's words: "May the waters be auspicious. The response: "Om, perfumes; may the fragrant ones protect. Having caused [the disciple] to recite thus as prescribed, one should sprinkle everywhere with the mantra beginning "O Lord of the Dwelling" (*vāstoṣpate*).
The dismissal of the deities of the auspicious day (*puṇyāha*) is recorded here for the sake of illustration.
Whether in the forenoon, at midday, or at the third watch of the night, the honoring of Brahmins and others leads to the increase of sons, grandsons, and so forth. (v. 3)
On all other twilight hours, when one has been defiled by contact with another caste,
one should drink water mixed with black gram and fire for the purpose of purifying the body.
For the purpose of purifying the sprinkling site, especially with *kravyapuṣpa* flowers.

Thus the *puṇyāha* [ceremony] has been declared; now hear the procedure for the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). This is the chapter on the *puṇyāha* ritual from the *Kāraṇa-pratiṣṭhā-tantra*.
Now follows the procedure for collecting earth.

Then the preceptor, having adorned himself with ornaments such as the *uṣṇīṣa* and others, having performed the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkaraṇa*), having prepared the general water offering (*sāmānyārghya*), and having worshipped Vighneśvara according to the rules, should perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and [proceed] with the rite of sowing the seed-syllables (*aṅkurārpaṇa-karma*) on this auspicious lunar day, which serves as the site for the eight-fold binding (*aṣṭabandha*) of the restoration of the ancient image of this goddess, the venerable Śrī Kāntimatī Ambā.

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "For the purpose of collecting the clay, I shall perform the worship of Astreśvarī and Caṇḍeśvarī, along with Lakuśakti, preceded by the three [substances] such as *sāra* and accompanied by consecration (*abhiṣeka*)," one should consecrate Astreśvarī and Caṇḍeśvarī according to the method of the resolve using the essence of *likuca* and other materials. Having satisfied them with the food offering (*naivedya*), [one places them] on the chariot.

Having placed Rājeśvarī and Caṇḍeśvarī upon a palanquin, which was adorned with all ornaments and topped by a parasol, and accompanied by numerous mirrors, umbrellas, chowries, songs, dances, hymns, praises, and the chanting of the Vedas,
[the procession led] by the king and all [his attendants].

Having gone outside the village together with his devotees after first praying to the *mūlaliṅga*, he should begin the rite according to the prescribed rule on the bank of a river, by a pond, in a forest, or even in a flower garden, a long tank, or at a bridge, facing either the east or the north. Having reached one of such locations, there [he should prepare] a space measuring nine cubits.
Having constructed a pavilion (maṇḍapa),

adorned it with plantain leaves, mango sprouts, and so forth, and having prepared two altars (vedi) measuring one cubit each using white and black powders, he should fashion an eight-petaled lotus. Then,
on the western sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), upon a cloth spread over darbha grass—

Having installed Aṣṭreśvarī [in the northeast] and Caṇḍeśvarī [in the northwest], and having collected all the materials suitable for the rite of gathering earth— namely the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), leaves, flowers, milk, sandalwood, and water from a milk-bearing spring— one should sit upon the tortoise-seat (*kūrmāsana*) facing north. Having performed the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkaraṇa*), prepared the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*), and worshipped Vighneśvara, [one should proceed] on an auspicious lunar day.

The rites for the offering of the germinating seeds (*aṅkurārpaṇa*), the recitation of the *puṇyāha* formula, the purification by means of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), the self-purification, the recitation of the King of Weapons (*astrarāja*), and the worship of the mandala, which constitute the constituent parts of the rite of the goddess sacrifice (*devīyāga*) for the restoration of the ruins and the eightfold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*) of the venerable Mother Śrī Kāntimatī.

Having performed the purification of the site (*khaniśuddhi*), having performed the placement of the *mātṛkā* letters, and the placement of the thirty-eight *kalās*, one should then perform the placement of the planetary spheres (*grahagolakanyāsa*). Having performed the placement thus: "Salutation to the letter Na on the head; salutation to the letter Ma on the mouth; salutation to the letter Śrī on the heart; salutation to the letter Ca on the navel; salutation to the letter Ya on the two feet," and having prepared the special water offering (*viśeṣārghya*).

Having applied a *tilaka* on the forehead with sandalwood paste, having placed a flower upon one’s own head, and having meditated upon oneself as being identical with the Goddess by reciting "Oṃ, obeisance to the Self in the form of Gaurī," one should sprinkle oneself with the water of the special *arghya* while reciting the *astra-mantra*. [Then one should worship] the Queen of the Sovereign Astras (*Astrarājeśvarī*).
One should worship: *Namaḥ* to Ananta; *namaḥ* to Dharma; *namaḥ* to Jñāna; *namaḥ* to Vairāgya; *namaḥ* to Aiśvarya; *namaḥ* to Padma; *namaḥ* to Astreśvaryāsana;
*namaḥ* to Astreśvaryamūrti; *namaḥ* to Astreśvarī. On the central petal—*namaḥ* to Rudra; on the right—*namaḥ* to Brahmā; on the left—*namaḥ* to Viṣṇu.

Homage! On the back-slab, homage to Pārvatī. At the region of the *kumbha*, homage to Senānī. At the front of the *kumbha*, homage to Vighnarāja. At the tip of the staff, homage to Damanā. In the middle of the staff, homage to Bhāskara.
At the base of the staff, homage to Caṇḍeśvarī. At the tip of the eastern petal, homage to Mahālakṣmī.

*Namaḥ*. To the south: *namaḥ* to the seven beginning with Brahmā and ending with Mātaṅgī. To the west: *namaḥ* to Jyeṣṭhā. To the north: *namaḥ* to Kātyāyanī. At the root of the Śrī [tree]: *namaḥ* to the Rudras; *namaḥ* to the Ādityas; *namaḥ* to the Vasus. (L2) *namaḥ* to the seat of Aśvinī; *namaḥ* to the eighteen groups (*gaṇas*). Having worshipped these [deities] starting from the invocation (*āvāhana*) up to the lamps, and having worshipped the divisions as before.
Having worshipped [the deity] of the supreme Śaiva,

having caused the drum to be played for sport among the guards, and having beaten the kettle-drum— preceded by the sound of that very drum and the five musical instruments— he should place the *kūrca* prepared with the *vidarbha* mantra into the center of the lotus-designed maṇḍala, starting from the center and ending in the northeast (Īśāna).

One should worship Brahmā and the others: "Salutation to the seat of Brahmā," "Salutation to the form of Brahmā," "Salutation to Brahmā. Having invoked Brahmā and worshipped him, [one worships] "Salutation to Ananta" in the southeast; "Salutation to Virama" in the south; "Salutation to Bhadra" in the southwest; and "Salutation to Pariccharandani" in the northeast. Having worshipped these with their respective seats, forms, and mantras, one should invoke them.

Having worshipped [the deity] and offered incense, lamps, and so forth, one should bring the sacrificial oblation (*havis*)— consisting of milk-rice (*pāyasa*), cakes (*apūpa*), sesame seeds (*saktu*), parched grain (*lāja*), and honey— into a pure vessel. Having consecrated it with the four purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*), and taking up the oblation in a portion the size of a wood-apple (*kapittha*), one should offer the *bali* in the center and other locations.

Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Brahmā! In the east—svāhā to Ananta; svāhā to Vinata; svāhā to Bhadra; svāhā to Jayanta; svāhā to Bhramarī; svāhā to Bhrāmaṇī. (l8) In the southwest—homage to Jayanta. In the west—homage to Bhramarī. In the northwest—homage to [Bhrāma]ṇī. In the north—homage to Prasthitā.
Homage!
Svāhā to him who has set forth! Svāhā to yawning! Having thus offered the bali-oblation, and having again offered incense and lamps, one should pray and [depart] from this place.
Having yawned and said, "I shall dismiss Brahmā along with his retinue out of order," he dismisses him; having removed [the previous offerings], having smeared that place with cow-dung water,

(l3) having fashioned the Goddess of the Earth therein from powdered pigments and flour, having arranged eight petals and two circles all around, [he should perform the rite] with the water of the general *arghya* offering.
Having sprinkled [it] with the Astra-mantra, one should worship [it] with: "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of the Goddess Earth.
[She is] resembling a dark complexion, radiant, and with eyes like those of a king.
She has a golden sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), two arms, and two eyes;
she is adorned with all ornaments and wears a crown with a casket (*karaṇḍa-makuṭa*). She is clad in red garments and holds a blue lotus in her right hand.

Then, one should invoke the Earth with offerings of fragrance: "Homage to the form of the Goddess Earth! Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the form of the Goddess Earth! Having invoked her and worshipped her up to the lamps, one should worship Indra and the other guardians of the world-quarters on the petals starting from the east. Having worshipped them, [one should proceed].

...having consecrated [the image] with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) following a *puṇyāha* ceremony preceded by the ablution of pure water; having wrapped it with a thread joined with *darbha* grass and a branch of mango adorned with fresh *darbha*; and having placed it upon *kuśa* grass to the east of the mandala, [one should recite]: "Homage to the Pāśupata weapon! Homage to the form of the Pāśupata weapon! Oṃ ślīṃ paṭ!"

"Pāśu huṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the Pāśupata weapon. Having invoked the Pāśupata weapon and worshipped it, and having taken the offering-food together with flowers, one should present the bali-offering upon *kuśa* grass with the mantra: "Oṃ śi huṃ paśuṃ pāśupatāstrāya svāhā," and then wash [the hands].

Having resolved upon an auspicious lunar day, I shall perform the collection of earth (mṛtsaṃgrahaṇa), which is a constituent part of the rite of sowing seeds (aṅkurārpaṇa), and which is itself a constituent part of the ritual of the Eightfold Binding of the Goddess (aṣṭabandhanadevīyāga) for the restoration of the ruins (jīrṇoddhāra) of this venerable mother Śrī Kāntimatī.
(The Collection of Earth):

For the purpose of filling the auspicious sprout-vessels and so forth during the rite of collecting earth, I shall collect earth from the womb of the Earth-goddess who has been duly worshipped. Whatever defect may have arisen at the time of collecting the earth due to [inauspicious] lunar days, weekdays, asterisms, ascendants, yogas, karaṇas, and so forth—

In order to avoid that fault, the action being performed is completed; and in order to obtain the full fruit of the action being performed by means of avoiding that fault which arose, (l7) [it is so stated].

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) that "for the sake of pleasing Kāntimatī, I shall perform the ten gifts and the gifts of fruit," [one should offer] cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, clarified butter, clothing, grain, molasses, sacrificial porridge, salt, betel leaves, and fruits. Taking these together with ritual fees (*dakṣiṇā*), preceded by mantras and water, [one offers them] to this Mother Kāntimatī-devī.
In this undertaking for the collection of earth marked by sprouts from the eight-fold binding work of restoring what was decayed—
both in the rites already performed and those currently being performed— I, desiring the attainment of success at the auspicious moment and longing for the full realization of the fruit,
give this to you; thus [I say] to the Brāhmaṇas.

Having given [the gift] with the mantra "bhūmibhūmnā," and having prayed with "annādyāyā dada," one should wash a silver vessel with the *astra* mantra, place it to the north, and, after obtaining the permission of the Brahmins at an auspicious moment (*sumuhūrta*), take up the sacrificial ladle (*sruk*) with the mantra "devasya tvā. Then, having consecrated it with "uttiṣṭha brahman," [one proceeds] preceded by all musical instruments and the *ghora* [mantra].

Facing north, having dug three times with the *astra-mantra*, and taking earth while contemplating his own belly, he places it in a small bowl with the *mūla-mantra*. Having taken a fourth portion silently, he fills the bowl and worships it with perfumes and other offerings using the *kavaca* and *astra* mantras.

Having thoroughly cleansed [the site] with a wet cloth, *darbha* grass, and armor; having dismissed the Goddess situated within the mandala along with the *bhūta*s and others; having offered the *arghya* water facing away [from the mandala]; for the sake of pacifying Varuṇa, the deity of the earth, one should sprinkle her with the *arghya* water. Then, taking another portion of clay, filling it [with water], making it level, and worshipping it with perfumes and other offerings, [one recites]: *oṃ laṃ kroṃ*.

Having dismissed the Goddess of the Earth with the words, "Homage to the Earth," one should place the deceased upon a palanquin or a chariot joined with excellent horses, and enter the temple accompanied by the king of weapons at the forefront and the sound of all musical instruments,
distinguished by the splendor of Gaurī and Kālī.
This is what should be performed during the day; however, this is the procedure for collecting clay as taught in the Kāmika Āgama.
Now follows the ritual for the offering of the sprouts (*aṅkurārpaṇavidhi*). The preceptor, together with the image-keepers (*mūrtipa*), having performed the preparatory rites such as bathing,

and having completed the regular and special twilight prayers (*sandhyā* and *viśeṣasandhyā*), and having adorned himself with the turban (*uṣṇīṣa*) and other ornaments, [should proceed] in front of the deity, on either side, or in the northeast.

Having caused a pavilion to be constructed on a well-concealed, windless spot, measuring five cubits or nine cubits in size and perfectly square; having smeared it evenly with cow dung and other substances so that it resembles a mirror; having adorned it with mango sprouts and the like;
and having cast eight threads upon this [ground]...

One should place the foot [of the mantra] according to the threefold rule preceded by the syllable *ra*. Having performed the central *kumbha*, there are two *pālikās* and so forth; and in the intermediate directions (*vidik*), there are four feet (*catuṣpada*) in accordance with the statement.
There should be an eastward line (*prāksūtra*) consisting of eight lines (*vasusūtra*), and likewise a northward line (*udaksūtra*).
In the center, one should place a single lunar square, and around it, hot squares.
Having smeared that eastern quarter with three footprints [in the directions] south,

west, and north, having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa, having prepared the general *arghya*, having worshipped Vighneśvara, and having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) preceded by the striking of the head, on this auspicious lunar day—

Having made the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "I shall perform the ritual sowing of seeds (*aṅkurārpaṇa*), which is a subsidiary part of the goddess-worship for the restoration of the shrine of the goddess Śrī Kāntimatī," he shall then perform the subsidiary rites such as the recitation of the *puṇyāha* formula and the purification by the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).
Having touched water, [he performs] with the *puṇyāha* and the *pañcagavya*.

It should be prepared according to the rules. Having performed self-purification, and having meditated upon the excellent body as being of the nature of Amṛteśvara; having sprinkled the base of the tree with *arghya* water while reciting the *astra-mantra*; having placed rice and other grains within the footprint (*pada*); having strewn it around with *darbha* grass and flowers; and having washed with the *astra-mantra* the vessel wrapped in thread, which is capable of holding a *droṇa* measure of water, [using] the left hand...

Having offered [the vessel], having filled it with water while reciting the *mūla-mantra* and the mantra "āpo vā idam," and having established it upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) with the *aghora-mantra*, one should [place] the inner *kūrca* of cloth and the outer *kūrca* of mango sprouts and so forth with the *vāmadeva-mantra*,
and perform the *tāla* [gesture]. (l5)
Having adorned [the site], and having first recited the mantra beginning with *syonā pṛthivī*, one should place a jewel or gold with the mantra *ratnāni*.

Having consecrated [the site] up to the perfumes (*gandha*), one should, according to the previously mentioned method, fashion [structures] such as *pālikās* around the jar—at the sides of the doors, the corners, and the sides—using *darbha* grass and clay during the night. At their base...
Having wrapped firewood, a water-pot, dūrvā grass,

a water-strainer, śirīṣa shoots, and bilva leaves with a thread joined with *darbha* grass and encircled by the root-mantra, one should install them in their respective places with the heart-mantra (*hṛdayamantra*). [Then,] in a new earthen vessel capable of holding a *droṇa* measure of water, [one should place] sesame and mustard seeds...

One should prepare mung beans, black gram, rice, barley, as well as *niṣpāva*, *rāṭaka*, and horse gram, according to their availability. Having had people cast these [seeds] [into the vessel], having sprinkled them, and having purified them with the fourfold consecration (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*), one should place the seeds with the *hṛdaya-mantra* into a new earthen jar filled with cow’s milk. Covering it with a shallow bowl and concealing it with *darbha* grass, [one prepares] the jars and so forth.
One should worship: *Oṃ ādhāraśaktaye* (l3) *namaḥ*.
*Anantāya namaḥ*. *Dharmāya namaḥ*. *Vairāgyāya namaḥ*. *Aiśvaryāya namaḥ*. *Hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Saṃ amṛteśvarāya namaḥ*.
The all-pervading one, possessing a stainless form, complete with all parts, two-eyed,
holding a pair of night-lotuses in his hands, stands within the tender moon as a witness to one's actions for the sake of pacifying accumulated sins.
One should place the form together with Gaganasahita in the middle of the jar.
