With the *mṛgīmudrā*—shaped like a jujube fruit and the size of a fresh *āmalaka* fruit—together with a new ladle, [one recites]: "Oṃ hāṃ hoṃ, salutation to Śiva, svāhā."
Having offered oblations with the five Brahmans and the six ancillaries: *oṃ sakalaprāsādāya svāhā*;
*oṃ haṃ niṣkalaprāsādāya svāhā*; *oṃ hāṃ śūnyaprāsādāya svāhā*; *oṃ hāṃ kalāḍhyaprāsādāya svāhā*;
*bahisthāya svāhā*.
To the one situated within, svāhā! To the one who is to be praised in the throat (or ear), svāhā! To the self-delight, svāhā! To the self, svāhā! To the pure, svāhā!

To the root, svāhā! To the reality, svāhā! To the beginning, svāhā! To the temple of the three arts, svāhā! To the temple of the five arts, svāhā! To the temple of the six arts, svāhā! To the nine arts... svāhā!
Svāhā to the Prāsāda! Svāhā to the ten-part Prāsāda!
Svāhā to the twelve-part Prāsāda! Svāhā to the sixteen-part Prāsāda! Svāhā to the twenty-part Prāsāda!
Svāhā to the twenty-two-part Prāsāda!
Svāhā to the Gāyatrī consisting of twenty-four syllables! Svāhā to the eight parts, the digits, and the kalās! Svāhā to Medhā! Svāhā to Bindu!
Svāhā to the manifest Prakṛti! To that Manonmanā, svāhā!

Svāhā! To the Sound, svāhā! To the Drop, svāhā! To the syllable *haṃ*, svāhā! To the syllable *au*, svāhā! To the Sixth, svāhā! To the Supreme Śiva, the controller of all living beings—[consisting of] the years, seasons, months, fortnights, days, nāḍīs, breaths, and so forth—svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Śaṅkara, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Śambhu, svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Sthāṇu, svāhā!
Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śiva! Svāhā to the Lord of Beasts! Svāhā to the fierce God! Svāhā to the God Śarva! Svāhā to the God Bhava! Svāhā to the God Īśāna! Oṃ! (l5)

Hrīṃ, svāhā to Śaśiva! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Sahamāna! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Śitikaṇṭha! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Kapardin! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Tāmra! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Aruṇa! Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Apagurumāṇa! Svāhā to Hiraṇyabāhu! Svāhā to Saṃsphiñjara! Svāhā to Babhruśā!

Svāhā! With the mantra *manomahāntam*, one oblation of clarified butter; with the mantra *mānastoke*, one oblation. "O you who strike down cattle and men, O destroyer of heroes, let there be well-being for us and protection, O God, and [favor] over us."

Recite the mantra, "Speak, bestow armor, O you of double strength," and offer three oblations. Having offered thus, take portions from all the substances for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering, place them within the boundary markers, and then perform the secondary oblations (*upahoma*).

With the *sadyojāta* mantra, one performs ten oblations of *palāśa* wood fuel; with the *vāma* mantra, ten oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*); with the *aghora* mantra, ten oblations of sacrificial porridge (*caru*); with the *tatpuruṣa* mantra, ten oblations of parched grain (*lāja*); with the *īśāna* mantra, ten oblations of mustard seeds (*sarṣapa*); with the *hṛdaya* mantra, ten oblations of rice (*vāha*); and with the *śiras* mantra, oblations of sesame seeds (*tila*). With the *śikhā* [mantra...]

An oblation of bamboo; with the *kavaca* [mantra], an oblation of black gram (*māṣa*); with the *netra* [mantra], an oblation of *mudga* beans; with the *astra* [mantra], an oblation of *gulā*; with the *mūla* [mantra], an oblation of plantain fruit. Having thus offered ten oblations for each separately, [one offers] with the *prāsāda* [mantra] ending in *vauṣaṭ*.

Having offered the *pūrṇāhuti* oblation; having offered the *vyāhṛti* oblations; having taken up a five-colored thread together with a garland of *darbha* grass; having cast two *darbha* blades into the water;

[preparing] the general *arghya* offering of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) with conch-water; having sprinkled [the site] with the *vyāhṛtis*; [one should say]: "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti"; "Obeisance to the one encircled by the islands of jewels (*ratnadvīpa*)."

Homage to the great jewel-railing (*mahāmaṇivedikā*). Homage to the solar mandala (*sūryamaṇḍala*). Homage to the fire mandala (*agnimaṇḍala*). Homage to the lunar mandala (*somamaṇḍala*). Homage to the vital winds, beginning with *prāṇa* and *apāna*. Homage to all [the nāgas], beginning with Ananta. [The channels: Iḍā, Piṅgalā, Suṣumṇā, Gāndhārī, Pūṣā, Hastijihvā, Alambuṣā, Krāuñcī, and Śaṅkhinī.

(l1) Homage to the channels (*nāḍī*). Homage to the skin, bones, flesh, blood, fat, and so forth. Homage to the five states beginning with waking (*jāgrat*). Homage to those whose forms consist of pure and impure *māyā*. Homage to the principles (*tattva*) beginning with *prakṛti* and ending with *māyā*. (l2)

Salutation to the power of will, knowledge, and action, which are the very nature of Śiva’s sovereign capacity (*sāmarthya*). Salutation to those whose forms are the *bindu* and *māyā*, which are inherent in the universe. Salutation to the nine powers, beginning with Vāmā, residing in the threads. Salutation to the one in the form of a white face in the white thread. Salutation to the one possessing yellow-colored teeth in the yellow thread. Salutation to Aghora in the black-threaded [thread]. In the red thread...

Salutation to Vāmadeva, the thread; salutation to Nīlatantu, the thread whose form is black; (l4) salutation to the thread whose essential nature consists of the five *kalās*; salutation to the threads whose essential nature consists of the mantras *a*, *ka*, *u*, *ka*, and *ma*; salutation to the *kalā* Puṣṭi; salutation to the *kalā* Vijayā;
[salutation] to all [of them]. (l5)

Salutation to Mukhyā Kalā. Salutation to Vīrakalā. Salutation to Aparājitakalā. Salutation to Jayākalā. Salutation to Vijayākalā. Salutation to Vṛṣṭakalā. Salutation to Ṣaṣṭikalā. (L6) Salutation to Ajitakalā. Salutation to Manonmanī. Salutation to the one hundred and eight Rudras. Salutation to Prakṛtitattvā. Salutation to Sarvatomukhī.
Homage! Homage to the powers beginning with Vāmā. Homage to Medhākalā. (l7) Homage to Rasakalā. Homage to Viṣakalā. Homage to Bindukalā. Homage to Ardhacandrakalā. Homage to Nirodhinīkalā.
Homage to Vyāpinīkalā. Homage to Nādakalā. Homage to Nādāntakalā. (p113a, l1)

Salutation to Śaktikalā. Salutation to Vyāpinīkalā. Salutation to Vyomavyāpiṇīkalā. Salutation to Lakṣmīkalā. Salutation to Prabhākalā. Salutation to Puṣṭikalā. Salutation to Sakalasaubhāgyakalā. Salutation to those whose forms consist of the pure, the impure, and the mixed *māyā*. Above the threads is the power of concealment (*tirodhāna-śakti*).

Having invoked [the deity] with the mantra ending in *namaḥ* together with the *māyā*-seed syllable (*hrīṃ*), and having displayed the six mudrās beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*), one should offer a welcome-arghya with the root mantra. Having presented the food offering (*naivedya*), incense, and lamps, then follows the *sañcātahoma*:
*oṃ hāṃ hoṃ saśivāya svāhā*. *Oṃ hoṃ*. (l4)

To Īśāna, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. To Tatpuruṣa, *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*. Oṃ *hāṃ*, to Aghora, *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*. Oṃ *hāṃ*, to Vāmadeva, *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*. Oṃ *haṃ*, to Sadyojāta, *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*. Oṃ *hāṃ*, to the Heart, *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*. Oṃ *hrīṃ*, to the Head, *huṃ*...
*phaṭ* *rama* (*namaḥ*) *svāhā*. *Oṃ* *haiṃ* *huṃ* *phaṭ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*. *Oṃ* *hauṃ* to the eyes *huṃ* *phaṭ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*. *Oṃ* *hraḥ* to the weapon *huṃ* *phaṭ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*.
Having offered oblations into the fire with the word *svāhā*, [one should offer] the letter *ha*.

Having performed the oblation with the *saṃpāta* clarified butter in the midst of the *darbha* grass strands according to this procedure, and having then offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the *prāsāda* mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*, [he should place it] upon the deity with the words, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...
(devasya tvā savituḥ prasave).

One should perform the binding of the Śivaliṅga with two threads from a garland of *darbha* grass in a clockwise direction: first, with the seed-syllable of Māyā encasing the seed-syllable of Śiva; second, with the seed-syllable of Varma encasing the seed-syllable of Śiva; and third, with the root-seed-syllable of Mokṣa encasing the seed-syllable of Māyā, together with the *vyāhṛti*. One should bind it at the region of the *kumbha* with the *kavaca* mantra encasing the seed-syllable of the Heart.

One should effect the joining of the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*) by means of the armor-mantra (*kavaca*) of the retinue beginning with Ananta who reside upon the seat (*pīṭha*). For the purpose of expiation for any transgression regarding the rules of the ritual procedures, such as the meditation on the joining of the channels, the mantras, and the tantras,
there is the triad beginning with "unauthorized" (*anājñāta*).
The oblation, the Mahāvyāhṛti mantra—
whatever has been performed in the sacrifice out of ignorance or erroneously,
O Agni, make that right for him, for you indeed know the proper time.
The sacrifice is measured by the person; the person is encompassed by the sacrifice.
O Agni, fashion that for him, for you indeed know the proper time.

That mortal who, with a mind matured by wisdom and possessing swift skill, performs the rite of sacrifice—he, the wise one, knowing all, shall be the Agniṣṭut priest; he, the most worthy of worship, shall invoke the gods at the proper times. Having offered the Mahāvyāhṛtis and the eight oblations of various forms, he should then [proceed] with the Prasāda mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.

Having offered the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), having preserved the fire with dried cow dung, and having gone near the Great Liṅga, one should assume the tortoise posture (*kūrmāsana*) facing north. Having performed the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkaraṇa*), one should sprinkle the Great Liṅga with the water of the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*). Then, preceded by the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha*), one should perform the worship of the Form and the Lord of Forms (*mūrtimūrtīśvara*), and the worship of the Principles (*tattva*) and the Lords of the Principles (*tattveśvara*) in the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), beginning from *nivṛtti* up to *śāntyatītā*, [completing] the six [levels].

One should perform the worship of the *liṅga*. Having placed a bundle (*kūrca*) of twenty-five *darbha* grasses upon the top of the Śiva-liṅga, one should worship it with: "Aṃ, obeisance to the seat (*pīṭha*) of Kāmarūpa;
Bhuṃ, obeisance to the seat of Nevāla; Laṃ, obeisance to the seat of Pauṇḍravardhana; Uṃ, obeisance to the seat of Purastita; Ūṃ, obeisance to the seat of Carasthita; Ṛṃ..."

Salutation to Pūrṇasthitapīṭha. Salutation to Ṛṃ Aṭṭahāsapīṭha. Salutation to Ī Āmrātakeśvarapīṭha. Salutation to Eṃ Ekāmbareśvarapīṭha. Salutation to Eṃ Trasrotapīṭha. Salutation to Aiṃ Kāmakoṭipīṭha.

Oṃ, salutation to Kailāsa-pīṭha. Aṃ, salutation to Kedāra-pīṭha. Āṃ, salutation to Candra-pīṭha. Kaṃ, salutation to Śrī-pīṭha. Oṃ, salutation to Oṃkāra-pīṭha. Oṃ Gaṃ, salutation to Indrapīṭha. Ghaṃ, salutation to Mālava-pīṭha. Ṅaṃ, salutation to Alāntaka-pīṭha. Caṃ, salutation to Devikoṭāra-pīṭha. Chaṃ...
*Namaḥ* to Gokarṇa-pīṭha. *Jaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Aṭṭahāsa-pīṭha. *Jhaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Virajā-pīṭha. *Ñaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Rājagṛha-pīṭha. *Ṭaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Rājagṛha-pīṭha. *Ṭhaṃ*:
*namaḥ* to Mahāpatha-pīṭha. *Ḍaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Kolvāgiri-pīṭha. *Ḍhaṃ*: *namaḥ* to Elāpura-pīṭha.
l1) Homage to Purapīṭha! ṇaṃ Homage to Kapeśvarapīṭha! taṃ Homage to Jayantīśvarapīṭha! thaṃ Homage to Majjayanīpīṭha! daṃ Homage to Citrāpīṭha! dhaṃ Homage to Kṣirikāpīṭha! naṃ l2)

Salutation to the seat of Hastināpuri (Laṃ). Salutation to the seat of Giri-pura (Laṃ). Salutation to the seat of Oḍīśa (Paṃ). Salutation to the seat of Prayāga (Phaṃ). Salutation to the seat of Ṣaṣṭhīśa (Baṃ). Salutation to the seat of Māyāpura (Bhaṃ). (L3) Salutation to the seat of Malaya-giri (Maṃ). Salutation to the seat of Śrīśaila (Yaṃ). Salutation to the seat of Meru-giri (Raṃ). Salutation to the seat of Māhīndra-puri (Vaṃ). Salutation to [the seat of] Śaṃ.

Salutation to the Vāmanapurī-pīṭha. Saṃ, salutation to the Mahālakṣmīpura-pīṭha. Haṃ, salutation to the Oḍhyāna-pīṭha. Laṃ, salutation to the Chāyāchatra-pīṭha. Kṣaṃ, salutation to the Jaleśapura-pīṭha. Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to Keśavamūrti and Kṣaya. Āṃ... (line 5)

Salutation to Nārāyaṇa and Mūrti; iṃ, salutation to Mādhava and Iṣṭadā; īṃ, salutation to Govinda and Īśāna; uṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu and Ugrā; ūṃ, salutation to Madhusūdana and Ūrdhvanayana; ṛ, salutation to Trivikrama and Ṛddhi; ṛṃ, salutation to Vāmana and Rūpiṇī; ḷṃ.
Salutation to Hṛṣīkeśamūrti and Lūnamūrti. Salutation to Padmanābhamūrti and Ekanāsikā.

(L7) Aiṃ, salutation to Dāmodaramūrti and Ekanāsikā. Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudevamūrti and Ekāriṇī. Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudevamūrti and Aghavutī. Auṃ, [salutation] to Tva(tvā)karṣaṇamūrti and Vaukarma. (P115a, l1)

Salutation to the two agents (*kartṛbhyām*). Salutation to Pradyumna-mūrti and Janaprabhā. Salutation to Aniruddha-mūrti and Antamāladharā. Salutation to Bhapamūrti and Karabhadrā. Salutation to Śarva-mūrti and Khagabālā.
Salutation to Rudra-mūrti and Girimādiphalapradā. Salutation to Paśu-mūrti and Ghaṇṭāparā. Salutation to Ugra-mūrti and Nayanā.

*Namaḥ*! To *caṃ* and *yaṃ*, the two who bear the moon and possess the form of Mahādeva, *namaḥ*. (L3) *Chaṃ* and *daṃ*, to the two who consist of meter and possess the form of Bhīma, *namaḥ*. *Jaṃ* and *thaṃ*, to the two who are the abode of the world and possess the form of Īśa, *namaḥ*. *Jhaṃ* and *taṃ*, to the two who possess the form of Tatpuruṣa, *namaḥ*. *Jñaṃ* and *ṇaṃ*, to the two who possess the form of Aghora and consist of the sound of knowledge (*jñānanāda*), *namaḥ*. (L4)

Namaḥ! Daṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta-mūrti and Aṅkā; ṭhaṃ ḍa, obeisance to Vāmadeva-mūrti and Kṛtiyāmārī; dhaṃ, obeisance to Brahma-mūrti and Yakṣaṇī; raṃ, obeisance to Prajāpati-mūrti and Añjanī; laṃ, obeisance to Veya-mūrti and Lakṣmī; vaṃ, obeisance to Parameṣṭhi-mūrti and Varṇī; śaṃ...

Salutation to Pitāmaha-mūrti and Śaśidhāriṇī. Ṣaṃ, salutation to Vidhātṛ-mūrti and Ṣaḍādhāra-nīlī; saṃ, salutation to Viriñca-mūrti and Sarvanāyikā; haṃ, salutation to Sṛṣṭi-mūrti and Astānanā; laṃ, salutation to Caturānana-mūrti and Lalitā; kṣaṃ, [salutation to] Hiraṇyagarbha...

Salutation to Mūrti and Kṣamā. Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, [one recites]: *oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ namo 'mṛtāmbhodhinadyai* (salutation to the river of the ocean of nectar); *namo 'parājitadvipāyai* (salutation to the invincible elephant); *namo nāmāprakṣamahordānāyai* (salutation to the one of great and unsurpassed generosity).

Salutation to Santānavāṭikā; salutation to Kalpanavāṭikā; salutation to Haricandanavāṭikā; salutation to Mandāravāṭikā; salutation to Pārijātavāṭikā; salutation to Kadambavanavāṭikā; salutation to Bilvavanavāṭikā; salutation to Puṣparatnaprakārā; salutation to Padmarāgaratnavyakārā.

Homage to her who takes the form of the *gomedhika* jewel; homage to her who takes the form of the *vajra* jewel; homage to her who takes the form of the *vaiḍūrya* jewel; homage to her who takes the form of the *marakata* jewel; homage to her who takes the form of the *indranīla* jewel;
homage to her who takes the form of the *muktāphala* jewel.

Salutation to her whose ramparts are made of coral jewels; salutation to the pavilion of rubies; salutation to the pool of nectar; salutation to the pool of discernment; salutation to her who emits the glow of the morning sun; salutation to her who emits the light of the moon; salutation to the great enclosure of erotic passion; salutation to the forest of great lotuses; salutation to the abode of the wish-fulfilling gem.

Homage to the Eastern Tradition, the Eastern Gate! Homage to the Southern Tradition, the Southern Gate! Homage to the Western Tradition, the Western Gate! Homage to the Northern Tradition, the Northern Gate, and the Great Jewel Altar! [To] the jewel-lamp...

Salutation to Valayā; salutation to Mahāsiṃhāsana; salutation to the one consisting of Brahman with five legs, and to the one consisting of Viṣṇu with one and five legs; salutation to the one consisting of Rudra with one bed-leg; salutation to the one consisting of Īśāna with the bed-legs; salutation to Sadāśiva as the plank; salutation to Haṃsakula as the head-ornament of the bed.
Salutation to Haṃsakulikā. Salutation to Haṃsakulamahopadhānā, who possesses a beautiful golden bedspread. Salutation to Mahāmāyādhvanikā. Salutation to Hlauṃvidadhiptā. Salutation to Pañcavaktrā.
Salutation to Sadāśivapati.
Salutation to the Lord of Pretas. Salutation to the Lotus-Seat. Salutation to Vibhūti. Salutation to Kānti. Salutation to Kīrti. Salutation to Unnati. Salutation to Sṛṣṭi.

Salutation to Sannati. Salutation to Vyuṣṭi. Salutation to Utkṛṣṭi. Salutation to Ṛddhi. Salutation to the nine Śaktis beginning with Vāmā and ending with Manonmanī. In the *liṅga*, salutation to the Self whose nature is the Power of Knowledge (*jñānaśakti*). In the seat (*pīṭha*):

Salutation to her whose nature is the power of action (*kriyā-śakti*). Salutation to the principle of the self (*ātma-tattva*). (L5) Salutation to the lord of the principle of the self, whose nature is the power of action. Salutation to the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*). Salutation to the lord of the principle of knowledge, whose nature is the power of cognition (*jñāna-śakti*). Salutation to the principle of Śiva (*śiva-tattva*). Salutation to the lord of the principle of Śiva, [whose nature is] will (*icchā*)... (L6)

Salutation to the Self of Power (*śakti*). *lrīṃ*, salutation to the Form of Earth (*kṣmāmūrti*); salutation to Dhārikā, the Mistress of the Form of Earth. *ruṃ*, salutation to the Form of Fire (*vahnimūrti*); salutation to Dīptimatī, the Mistress of the Form of Fire. *hrīṃ*, salutation to the Form of the Sacrificer (*yajamāna*); salutation to Ugrā, the Mistress of the Form of the Sacrificer. *ṣṭrīṃ*, salutation to the Form of the Sun (*arkamūrti*); salutation to Jyotsnā, the Mistress of the Form of the Sun. *pūṃ*.
Homage to the Water-form!
Homage to Sucetanā, the presiding deity of the Water-form! Yūṃ, homage to the Wind-form! Homage to Balotkaṭā, the presiding deity of the Wind-form! Hrīṃ, homage to the Moon-form!

Salutation to the one whose form is Soma; salutation to Dhātrī, the presiding deity of the Soma-form. Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to the one whose form is space; salutation to Vibhūti, the presiding deity of the space-form. Oṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the one whose form is earth;
[salutation] to Vāmā, the presiding deity of the earth-form.

Namaḥ! Hrūṃ klīṃ, obeisance to the Water-form; obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā, the presiding deity of the Water-form. Sau, obeisance to the Fire-form; obeisance to Kriyā, the presiding deity of the Fire-form. Oṃ, obeisance to the Wind-form; obeisance to Jñānī, the presiding deity of the Wind-form. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Ether-form; obeisance to Icchā, its presiding deity. [Of the Liṅga...]
In the portion of Brahmā: *oṃ hlāṃ* (l5) *ātmatattvāya namaḥ*. *oṃ hāṃ ātmatattvādhipataye brahmaṇe namaḥ*.
In the portion of Viṣṇu: *vidyātattvāya namaḥ*. *vidyātattvādhipataye viṣṇave namaḥ*. *oṃ hūṃ* in the portion of Rudra (l6).

Salutation to the principle of Śiva (*śivatattva*). Salutation to Śiva, the lord of the principle of Śiva. At the *mūlādhāra* of the *liṅga*, salutation to the earth-form (*kṣmāmūrti*). Oṃ, salutation to Śarva, the lord of the earth-form. At the *svādhiṣṭhāna*, salutation to the fire-form (*vahnimūrti*). Salutation to Paśupati, the lord of the fire-form. At the *maṇipūraka*, salutation to the sacrificer-form (*yajamānamūrti*). Salutation to Ugra, its lord. At the heart, [salutation] to the sun-form (*arkamūrti*).

Homage! Homage to Rudra, the presiding lord of that; homage to the one whose form is water in the throat; homage to Bhava, the presiding lord of that; homage to the one whose form is wind in the mouth; homage to Īśāna, the presiding lord of that;
homage to the one whose form is the moon between the eyebrows.

Salutation to Mahādeva, the presiding lord of that [element]. Salutation to the one whose form is the sky (*vyomamūrti*), on the head. Salutation to Bhīma, the presiding lord of that. In the Brahma-sector: *Oṃ hrīṃ laṃ*, salutation to the earth element (*pṛthivītattva*). *Oṃ hauṃ*, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha, the presiding lord of the earth element. *Vaṃ*, salutation to the water element (*jalatattva*). Salutation to Jaleśvara, the presiding lord of that. *Oṃ raṃ*, salutation to the fire element (*agnitattva*). Salutation to its presiding lord...

Salutation to the treasury of splendors. Oṃ, salutation to Yaṃ, the element of air; salutation to its presiding lord, Īśvara. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the element of space; salutation to its presiding lord, Sūkṣma. Salutation to the element of smell; salutation to its presiding lord, Gandhākṣa. Salutation to the element of taste; [salutation] to its presiding lord...

Homage to the Lord of Taste! Homage to the Principle of Form! Homage to the Sun, its presiding deity! Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to the Principle of Touch! Homage to the Most Powerful One, the lord of the Principle of Touch! Homage to the Principle of Touch! Homage to the Subtle Sound, the lord of the Principle of Touch! Homage to the Principle of the Generative Organ! Homage to the Profound Bliss, the lord of the Principle of the Generative Organ!

Homage to the element of wind (*vāyu-tattva*). Homage to the lord of the element of wind, [the one] who dwells in the three worlds? Homage to the element of feet (*pāda-tattva*). Homage to the lord of the element of feet, the one who moves about (*cakramaṇa*). Homage to the element of hands (*pāṇi-tattva*). Homage to the lord of that element, the one who brings about equanimity (*samādayin*). Homage to the element of speech (*vāk-tattva*). Homage to the lord of the element of speech, the drum (*dundubhi*).

Homage! Homage to Nāsitatva. Homage to Ambika, the sovereign lord of Nāsitatva. Homage to Jihvātattva. Homage to Mahāvaktra, the sovereign lord of Jihvātattva. Homage to Cakṣustattva. Homage to Prakāśaka, the sovereign lord of Cakṣustattva.
Salutation! Salutation to the principle of skin; salutation to the lord of the principle of skin, the sovereign of all limbs. Salutation to the principle of hearing;

salutation to the lord of the principle of hearing, the sky-walker. Salutation to the principle of mind; salutation to the lord of the principle of mind, conceptualization. Salutation to the principle of ego; salutation to its lord, the ego-maker. Salutation to the principle of intellect; salutation to the lord of the principle of intellect.
Salutation to the Awakened One (*Buddha*). Salutation to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*).
(l4) Salutation to the Grandfather (*Pitāmaha*), the sovereign of the principle of primordial nature.

In the portion belonging to Viṣṇu: salutation to the principle of the person (*puruṣa-tattva*). Salutation to Viṣṇu, its sovereign. Salutation to the principle of passion (*rāga-tattva*). Salutation to Pallava, the sovereign of the principle of passion.

Homage! To the principle of necessity (*niyatitattva*), homage! To the Lord of the principle of necessity, the one born of Brahmā, homage! To the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*), homage! To the Lord of the principle of knowledge, Ghanāda, homage! To the principle of limited agency (*kalātattva*), homage! To the Lord of the principle of limited agency, Śikhivaktra, homage!

Salutation! Salutation to the principle of Time (*kālatattva*). Salutation to the bull-bannered Lord (*vṛṣadhvaja*), the sovereign of the principle of Time. Salutation to the principle of Illusion (*māyātattva*). Salutation to Viṣāṇa, the sovereign of the principle of Illusion.
In the portion of Rudra: salutation to the principle of Pure Knowledge (*śuddhavidyātattva*). (L7)

Homage to Kalyāṇa, the lord of that; homage to the principle of Īśvara; homage to Caturānana, the lord of the principle of Īśvara; homage to the principle of Sadāśiva; homage to ...yina, the lord of that; homage to the principle of Śakti;
homage to Śambhu, the lord of that; homage to the principle of Śiva; homage to Somanātha, the lord of the principle of Śiva; [homage] to the thirty-six principles and their lords.
Having eaten and worshipped, [one says] "Salutation. Having offered rice mixed with mung beans, cakes, fruits, and betel-leaf;

having presented incense and lamps; one should withdraw the worship. It is as follows: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Nivṛtti-kalā. Within the Nivṛtti-kalā: Oṃ laṃ, salutation to the Earth-tattva. Within the Earth-tattva: Kālāgni...

Salutations to the ten worlds: from the worlds of Kūṣmāṇḍa, Hāṭaka, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra; and to Kapālīśa, Arjabbuddhi, Vajradeha, Pramardana, Vibhūti, Avyaya, Śāstra, Pinākī, and Pramathādhipa. (L4) Salutations to the ten worlds: from Agnirudra, Hutāśa, Piṅgala, Khādaka, Haha, Jvalana, Dahana, Badara, Śubhasmāntaka, and Kṣayāntaka. Yā...

Salutation to the ten worlds, the three types of Mṛtyuharā as described by Kṛka, to the lords of all beings and of dharma. Salutation to the ten worlds, to those with faces for destruction and death, with cruel gazes and terrifying upward-pointing penises, the odd-eyed one, the smoke-colored, and the red-fanged ones.

Salutations to the ten worlds: to Balātibala, Pāśahasta, Mahābala, Śveta, Jaya, Bhadra, Dīrghabāhu, Jalāntaka, Meghanāda, and Sunāda. Salutations to the ten worlds: to Śīghra, Laghu, Vāyuvega, Sūkṣma, Tīkṣṇa, Kṣayāntaka, Pañcaśikha, Kapardī, Meghavāhana, and Nemi.
Salutations to the ten worlds from [the goddesses] Nidhīśā, Rūpavajrī, Saumyadehā, Jaṭādharā, Lakṣmīdhrī, Ratnadhṛk, Śrīdhṛk, Prasādā, Prakāmā, and Devī; and to Vṛṣa.

Salutation to Vṛṣadhara, Anantakrodhana, Mārutāśana, Grasana, Udumbarīśa, Phaṇīndra, and Vajradaṃṣṭra; salutation to the ten worlds. Salutation to Śambhu, Ṣī..., Adhyakṣa, Tryakṣa, Tridaśeśvara, Saṃvāha, and Vivāhana; salutation to the three-eyed ones who desire to obtain [them]; salutation to the ten worlds. Salutation to Kṣa.
Salutation to the one of single color. Oṃ, salutation to the Foot.
Oṃ, salutations again and again to Śiva. Oṃ, salutations, salutations.

Oṃ, salutations to Śiva—He who stands before Śarva, Darśa, Śiva, Sūkṣma, Śabda, Jñāna, Piṅga, Pataṅga, Kuru, and Sākṣin; may He be present. He is worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and others; He is the one who brings about the presence of all, the bestower of happiness upon all beings, the source of existence, the origin of being, and the Lord of Being (Bhava). O Śarva, first release [us]. To the Lord of Yoga, the Great Splendor, the True Being, the Sovereign (Īśvara).

Homage to Mahādeva, the twenty-eight locations. Oṃ haṃ, homage to the Sadyojāta mantra. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Heart mantra. Oṃ laṃ, homage to the sense-object of smell. Homage to the qualities of smell, taste, form, touch, and sound. Homage to the yellow, square, and solid Earth-maṇḍala marked with a vajra. Homage to the waking state. [To] the nose and the generative organ—
Salutation to the two sense organs. Salutation to the two channels, Iḍā and Piṅgalā.

Salutation to the two vital winds, Prāṇa and Apāna. Salutation to the worlds beginning with those of beasts, cattle, birds, reptiles, humans, piśācas, rākṣasas, gāndharvas, Indra, Soma, Prajāpati, and Brahmā.

Salutation to the fourteen wombs (*yonis*). Salutation to the two seed-syllables *aṃ* and *laṃ*. Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the Lord who is the efficient cause (*nimitta-kāraṇa*). Having thus meditated upon the *nivṛtti-kalā* endowed with these qualities:
Oṃ *hvīṃ*, salutation to the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*. Within the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* are *vaṃ*, *raṃ*, *yaṃ*, and *haṃ*.

Salutation to the twenty-three principles (*tattva*s): water, fire, air, ether, smell, taste, form, touch, sound, the organs of generation, excretion, feet, hands, nose, tongue, eyes, skin, ears, mind, intellect, ego, and the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti*) with its qualities. In the water-principle, [is] Amareśa;
in Prabhāsa...
Salutation to Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, Āṣāḍha, Ḍiṇḍika, Muṇḍa, Bhārabhūti, Lakulīśvara, and the eight secret worlds (*guhyāṣṭaka-bhuvana*). In the realm of *tejas*:
salutation to Hariścandra, Jalpeśa, Śrīśaileśa, Jalpeśa, Amrādikeśvara, Madhyameśvara, Mahākāla, Kedāra, and Bhairava, and to the eight extremely secret worlds (*atiguhyāṣṭaka-bhuvana*).
In the wind [region]: salutation to Gayā, Kurukṣetra, Nākhalanakhala, Vimala, Īśa, Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, Bhūmikeśvara, and to the eight worlds of the Guhyātiguhyas.
In the sky [region]: to Vastrāpada, Rudrakoṭi, and also to Muktamahābala, Gokarṇa, and Bhadrakarṇa.

Salutation to Svarṇākṣa and Sthāṇu; salutation to the worlds of the eight Sthāṇus; [salutation] to Gandha, Ādi, Ahaṃkāra, Iṣu, Gala, Ṣaṇḍa, Dviṣaṇḍa, Mākoṭa, Maṇḍaleśvara, Kālāñjana, Śaṅkukarṇa, Sthūleśvara, and Sthaleśvara.

Salutation to the worlds of the eight *pavitra*s. In the intellect (*buddhi*): salutation to the worlds of the *paiśāca*, *rākṣasa*, *yakṣa*, *gāndharva*, *aindra*, *saumya*, *prājeśa*, and *brahmayoni*; salutation to the eight worlds. In primordial nature (*prakṛti*):

salutation to the worlds of the eight—the *kṛta*, *akṛta*, *bhairava*, *brāhmaṇa*, *vaiṣṇava*, *kaumāra*, *kūrma*, and *śrīkaṇṭha*; salutation to the worlds of the eight divine origins (*devayoni*). *Laṃ*, salutation.

Haṃ namas! Saṃ namas! Ṣaṃ namas! Śaṃ namas! (l3) Vaṃ namas! Laṃ namas! Raṃ namas! Yaṃ namas! Maṃ namas! Bhaṃ namas! Baṃ namas! Paṃ namas! Phaṃ namas! Naṃ namas! Yaṃ namas! Daṃ namas! Thaṃ namas! Taṃ namas! Ṇaṃ namas! Ḍhaṃ namas! Ḍaṃ namas! Ṭhaṃ namas! Ṭaṃ namas! [These are] twenty-four (l4).

Salutations to the colors! O Maheśvara, Supreme Self, Śarva, Śiva, Source of destruction, Destruction itself, Without-destruction, Oṃ Suva, Oṃ Bhuva, Oṃ Bhūḥ! Dhū Dhū Dhū Dhū! Naṃ Naṃ Naṃ Naṃ! O Mother! O Ashless! (L5) Smokeless! Fireless! Formless! Light, Light! Splendor, Splendor! Salutations to the twenty-one words! Oṃ Hiṃ, salutations to Vāmadeva!

Oṃ hiṃ, svāhā to the head! Homage to the object of taste! Homage to the qualities of taste, form, touch, and sound! Homage to the sphere of water, which has the shape of a bright half-moon and is marked by a lotus! Homage to the state of dream! Homage to the pervasive wind (vyāna) and the upward-moving wind (udāna)!
Salutation to the two channels Suṣumnā and Gāndhārī. Salutation to the two senses, Vāyu and Rasanā. Salutation to both Bījas.
Salutation to the Lord who is the efficient cause. Salutation to Śrī Viṣṇu. Having thus meditated upon the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā as distinguished by these qualities:
Oṃ Hraṃ Bhuṃ, salutation to the Vidyā-kalā. Within the Vidyā-kalā, salutation to the principles (tattvas) of Puruṣa, Rāga, Niyati, Vidyā, Kāla, Akāla, and Māyā—to these seven principles.
Salutations! To the essence of water, to Amareśa-prabhā; salutations to Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, Āṣāḍha, Ḍiṇḍi, Muṇḍi, Bhārabhūti, Lakulīśvara, and the worlds of the eight ancestors (pilyāṣṭaka);
to Hariścandra, Śrīśaila, Jalpeśa, Āmrādikeśvara, Madhyameśa, Mahākāla...
Salutation to Kedāra and Bherava, and to the worlds of the eight most secret [shrines].
In the northwest— salutation to Gayā, Kurukṣetra, Nakhala, Nākhavimala, Īśa, Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, and Bhīmakeśvara, and to the worlds of the eight very secret [shrines].
In the sky—from Vāstra, Pādārudra, Koṭiravi, Avimuktamahālaya, Gokarṇa, Bhadrakarṇa, Svarṇākṣa, and Sthāṇu; homage to the eight worlds of Sthāṇu.

In the ego-principle (ahaṃkāra) consisting of fragrance and so forth—from Cakalaṇḍa, Dviraṇḍa, Mākoṭa, Maṇḍaleśvara, Kālāñjana, Śaṅkukarṇa, Sthūleśvara, and Sthaleśvara; [homage to] the eight sacred sites (pavitrāṣṭaka).

Salutation to the worlds (*bhuvana*). In the intellect (*buddhi*): salutation to the worlds of the Piśācas, Rākṣasas, Yakṣas, Gāndharvas, Indra, Soma, Prajāpati, and Brahmā; salutation to the eight worlds. (L7) In primordial nature (*prakṛti*): salutation to the worlds of the eight Bhairavas—Akṛta, Kṛta, Bhairava, Brāhmaṇa, Vaiṣṇava, Kaumāra, Kūrma, and Śrīkaṇṭha; salutation to the worlds of the eight classes of divine beings (*devayoni*).
To the six worlds— Vāma, Bhīma, Ugra, Bhava, Īśāna, and Ekavīra— from the world of Puruṣa: homage!
In the principle of *rāga*—salutation to the five worlds beginning with the worlds of Pracaṇḍa, Umāpati, Aja, Ananta, and Ekaśiva.
In *niyati*—salutation to Krodha and Caṇḍa. In *vidyā*—salutation to Saṃvarta and Tājya. In *kalā*—salutation to Piṅgala, Śūla, and Pañcāntaka. In *kāla*—

Salutation to Śikhe and Ekavīrā. In the Māthā [mantra]: salutation to Mahādyu, Vāmadeva, Udbhava, Bhava, Ekapingalā, Ekekṣaṇī, Īśāna, Aṅguṣṭhamātra, and Bhuvana—salutation to these eight Bhuvanas. Thus, salutation to the twenty-seven Bhuvanas.
Ña namaḥ. Jha namaḥ. Ja namaḥ. Ca namaḥ. (l4)
*Channa* obeisance! *Ṅanna* obeisance! *Ghanna* obeisance! Obeisance to the seven syllables! *Oṃ hūṃ*, obeisance to the heart of Aghora! *Oṃ hūṃ*, *vauṣaṭ* to the crest-lock!

O Pervader, O Pervader, obeisance! O Sky, O Sky, obeisance! (L5) O Consciousness of the unconscious, obeisance! Obeisance to the Lord of all Yoga! Obeisance to the Lord of all Vidyās! Obeisance to the one whose form is light! Obeisance to the Supreme Lord!
Salutation to the Endless; salutation to the Protector;
salutation to the Secret beyond the secret; *oṃ*, salutation, salutation; salutation to the form of Sadyojāta; salutation to the secret of Vāmadeva; salutation to the heart of Aghora;
salutation to the face of Tatpuruṣa; salutation to the head of Īśāna; salutation to Śiva; [salutation] to all...

Salutation to Prabhava. Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. Salutation to Dhyānahāra. Salutation to the twenty steps. Salutation to the object of form. Salutation to the qualities of form, touch, and sound. Salutation to the fire-maṇḍala adorned with a svastika of three mixed colors and red hue. Salutation to the state of deep sleep (suṣupti). Salutation to Cakṣuṣpāda. Salutation to Samāna and Rāga-vāyu. Salutation to Pūṣā and Ahasiti, the tongue and the channel.

Salutation to the seed-syllables *m* and *r*. Salutation to Rudra, the Lord who is the efficient cause (*nimittakāraṇa*). Having thus meditated upon the *vidyā-kalā* endowed with these qualities: *Oṃ haiṃ*, salutation to the *śānti-kalā*.
Salutation to the principles (*tattva*) of Śuddhavidyeśvara and Sadāśiva.
In Śuddhavidyā, [salutations] to Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikaraṇī, Balavikaraṇī, Balapramathanī, Sarvabhūtadamanī, and Manonmanī;
salutations to the nine worlds.
In the Īśvara-tattva—(l4)

Salutations to Ananta, Sūkṣma, Śivottama, Ekanetra, Ekarudra, Trimūrti, Śrīkaṇṭha, and Śikhaṇḍin; salutations to the eight worlds. In the principle of Sadāśiva: salutations to the world of Sadāśiva. Gaṃ, salutations! Khaṃ, salutations!

Kaṃ, salutations! Salutations to the three syllables. Salutations to the eternally united one. Salutations to him who is established upon the seat of yoga. Salutations to the eternal one. Salutations to the immovable one.

Homage to the Unsupported! Homage to the Lordless! Homage to the Infinite! (l6) Homage to Śiva! Homage to the All-Pervading! Homage to Him Whose Form is Space! Homage to the Space-Pervader! Homage to the Eleven Steps! Homage to the Tatpuruṣa mantra, Heṃ! Homage to the Kavaca mantra, Haiṃ! Oṃ! (l7)
Salutation to the two seed-syllables *Bī* and *Ya*. Salutation to the two channels (*nāḍī*) of Yaśas and Āla. Salutation to the Kūrma and Kṛkara winds. Salutation to the one who ordains touch.
Salutation to the qualities of sound and touch. [To the] black-colored hexagon...

Salutation to the wind-maṇḍala marked with the seed-syllable; salutation to the fourth state (*turyāvasthā*); salutation to the skin and the hands; salutation to Maheśvara, the Lord who is the efficient cause (*nimittakāraṇa*). Having thus meditated upon the *śāntikalā* as distinguished by these qualities: (l2) *Oṃ hauṃ*, salutation to the *śāntyatītakalā*; salutation to the *śakti-tattva* and *śiva-tattva* of the *śāntyatītakalā*.
In the Śaktitattva: salutation to the worlds of the five kalās—nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, and śāntyatītā. (l3.

"Starting from this day until the end of five days, during that interval, I shall renovate and re-establish [it]. Having thus prayed, thereafter follows the *saṃkalpa*: "By the command of Śiva, on this auspicious lunar day..."

"Please accept this worship, accompanied by recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth," thus he should pray. "One should perform the striking of the door-panels at the time of beginning the contraction," because it is so stated, one should perform the striking of the door-panels. Of this great mantra, the *sarvakāryajayaprada-vyaṣṭipraṇava*, Sanatkumāra is the seer (*ṛṣi*);

the single-syllabled Goddess Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); the auspicious Śiva, the bestower of victory in battles, is the deity (*devatā*); *oṃ hāṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *haṃ* is the power (*śakti*); *hrūṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*).

The application (*viniyoga*) of this mantra is for the purpose of recitation (*japa*) to achieve the accomplishment of the goal of Śatruñjaya, which is the gateway to the attainment of grace. The ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) begins with *hlām* and so forth. The ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). The visualization (*dhyāna*):
The left [hand] has the luster of blood-red and deep red, and is adorned with garlands, garments, and a sacred thread.

[One should meditate upon] the Great Hero, the Śūra-Śambhu, who has a prominent nose-tip and a *uṣṇīṣa*, and who holds a sword and a shield in his hands. One should recite the mantra: *oṃ aṃ uṃ haṃ raṃ śivaśikhan*. [This] prayer of five syllables, performed five thousand times every day, accomplishes all undertakings.

Victory is attained. With both hands holding *dūrvā* grass and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), beginning from the *mūlādhāra* of the Great Liṅga up to the *brahmarandhra*, one should perform the practice with the *pūraka* breath, preceded by the utterance of the root-mantras of the Haṃsa and Prāsāda. One should cover the *liṅga* with a cloth. With the two seed-syllables *haḥ* and *hai*, one should wrap the neck of the jar with threads and garlands of *darbha* grass. Immediately after that—

One should invoke [the deity] with the *vyāhṛtis*: "Oṃ bhūḥ, I invoke Bhava; Oṃ bhuvaḥ, I invoke Mṛḍa; Oṃ suvaḥ, I invoke Śaṅkara; Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ, I invoke Sadāśiva. Having thus invoked, one should perform the six mudrās, beginning with the *sthāpana* and *sannidhāna*, starting from the left.
1) Having displayed [the mandala] with the root mantra, and having offered a welcome and respectful water (arghya),
[he says]: "O Lord, Sovereign of the Entire World, until the conclusion of the worship..."
Therefore, remain present within this jar with a spirit of affection.
O Master, perform [the rite]. (l2) Having bowed immediately.

||1|| For the purpose of bringing about the presence of the Supreme Lord within this venerable Kumbha, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣi*) of the great mantra for the installation of life-force (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).
The *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, *Sāma*, and *Atharva* Vedas are the meters (*chandas*).
[I bow to] the one who effects the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the entire universe; *prāṇa-śakti* is the seed-syllable, the supreme deity is *hrīṃ*, and *kroṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*).
This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the recitation intended for the consecration of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) in this jar.

OṂ AṂ ĀṂ HĪṂ KROṂ ĀṂ KAṂ KHAṂ GAṂ GHAṂ ṄAṂ PṚTHIVY-AP-TEJO-VĀYU-ĀKĀŚĀTMANE KROṂ HRĪṂ ĀṂ AṄGUṢṬHĀBHYĀṂ NAMAḤ | OṂ IṂ ĀṂ EṂ KROṂ Ī CAṂ CHAṂ JAṂ JHAṂ ÑAṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ ĀṂ ŚABDA-SPARŚA-RŪPA-RASA-GANDHĀTMANE TARJANĪBHYĀṂ SVĀHĀ | OṂ HUṂ ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ Ū ṬAṂ ṬHAṂ ḌAṂ ḌHAṂ ṆAṂ...

KROṂ HIṂ ĀT VAT Cakṣuḥ-śrotra-jihvā-ghrāṇātmane, to the self of the eyes, ears, tongue, and nose, with the two middle fingers, VAUṢAṬ. OṂ EṂ TAṂ THAṂ DAṂ DHAṂ NAṂ AIṂ KROṂ HĪṂ ĀṂ Vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyu-upasthātmane, to the self of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals, with the two ring fingers.

Oṃ ā hrīṃ kroṃ auṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ. To the self consisting of mind, intellect, ego, thought, and gnosis, vauṣaṭ with the two little fingers. Oṃ aṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ aḥ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ. To the self consisting of speech, giving, emission, bliss, prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna, phaṭ with the palms and backs of the hands. Oṃ.

Aṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ āṃ—to the self of space, wind, fire, water, and earth: Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ, obeisance to the heart. Iṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ caṃ chaṃ caṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ—to the self of smell, taste, form, touch, and sound:
Īṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ, svāhā to the head.

Oṃ uṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ, to the genitals, wind, feet, hands, and speech—Āṃ Ūṃ, to the crest-lock (śikhā), vauṣaṭ. Oṃ ṛṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ṇaṃ yaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ, to the bliss, emission, movement, giving, and speech—Kroṃ Hrīṃ Āṃ Ṛṃ, to the armor (kavaca), huṃ. Oṃ Ḷṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ.

To the self of mind, ego, intellect, and manas: *maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ ḹṃ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ eṃ kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ aiṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ auṃ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*.
This is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*). The visualization (*dhyāna*):
She is seated upon a red lotus rising from a lake that shines within a sea of blood;
with her lotus-like hands she holds a noose, a bow, a rosary of *rudrākṣa* beads, a goad, and the five arrows.
Bearing a skull-bowl at the corners of her mouth, though adorned with three eyes, she is not burdened by breasts;
the Goddess, whose navel has the color of the rising sun, who bestows happiness upon the heart, is the Supreme Power, the Vital Force.

Ā Hrīṃ Kroṃ Kro? Hrīṃ Āṃ ya-ra-la-va-śa-ṣa-sa-hoṃ haṃ saḥ so’ham | So’haṃ haṃsaḥ; the vital breath of the Supreme Lord is here as my vital breaths; the individual soul is established here, as are all the senses, speech, mind, sight, and hearing.
May tongue, nose, *apāna*, *prāṇa*, *vyāna*, and *udāna* come right here and remain happily for a long time in this jar; may they live on; grant your presence, grant it!
*Svāhā!* Having recited this three times, [one says]: "O Asunīti, give back to us sight, give back breath; bestow enjoyment upon us here, and may we behold the rising sun, O Anumati!"
"Be gracious to us, O Destroyer!
May Earth give us back our life; may Goddess Heaven, may the Atmosphere, and may Soma give us back our body. May Pūṣan lead us back; come hither, O Night!
The brilliant face of the gods has risen.

[He should recite: "Of the eye and of that which stands still; and some [say] from both sides. Cows were born from that, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. Having touched [the site] with *darbha* grass up to this point, he should mutter: "Oṃ! O Ya, come, come as the messenger of immortality (*amṛtadūtī*), bringing you here. Having entered the heart of such-and-such a person, seize also his kinsmen!"
Having forcibly drawn out the jar and other vessels, cause them to enter;
establish them. Return again; remain firm in the jar. *Pauṣaṇṇaṃ namaḥ*. Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ. *Klauṃ*, paralyze!

Paralyze! Kaṃ! Oṃ hrīṃ! Messenger of Vaivasvata, come, come! Be firm in the jar! Vauṣaṭ! Namaḥ! Ā hrīṃ kroṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ klauṃ! Paralyze! Oṃ laṃ hrīṃ! Messenger Jīvahā, come! You of red form! Bring, bring [them] here by force! Cause them to enter the jar and so forth! Establish [them]!

Come again, come again! Be firm within the jar, *vauṣaṭ*! *Namaḥ*. *Oṃ* (l3) *hrīṃ* *kreṃ* *kreṃ* (*kroṃ*) *hrīṃ* *āṃ* *ya-ra-la-va-śa-ṣa-sa-hoṃ* *haṃsaḥ so'haṃ* *so haṃsaḥ*. *Klauṃ*, paralyze, paralyze! ||3||

Oṃ hrīṃ! O life-taker, come, come! O you whose form is fat, bring it, bring it! Cause the jar and so forth to enter; establish them! Come back again! Be firm within the jar! Vauṣaṭ! Namaḥ! Ā hrīṃ kroṃ kro hrīṃ āṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa.
Hoṃ haṃsassohaṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ| Klau, paralyze! ||4||

Oṃ śaṃ! O messenger, come, come! Bring, bring the unstable form! Drawing it by force, cause it to enter, cause it to enter the jar and so forth; establish it! Come again, come again! Be firm within the jar! Vauṣaṭ, namaḥ! Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ kreṃ hrīṃ āṃ slau! Paralyze! ||5||

Oṃ hrīṃ granthinī, come forth! Bring the form of a cat! Bring it, bring it! Cause it to enter the jar and so forth; establish it! Come again, come again! Be firm in the jar! Vauṣaṭ, namaḥ! Kauṃ, paralyze it! 6.
Oṃ hrīṃ haṃ Viṣphuliṅginī, come, come!
Bring forth my life-form! Enter the water-pot and other vessels; remain there! Come back again, come back! Be firm within the water-pot.
Bhavavauṣaṇṇa namaḥ | Ā hrīṃ kro kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ klaṃ vaṃ stambhaya ||7||

Oṃ laṃ! O Kṣetrapati Harī, come, come! Bring forth the form of the living being, bring it forth! Enter the jar and other vessels, enter them! Establish it, and return again! (L3) Be firm within the jar, vauṣaṭ! Homage! Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ klauṃ! Paralyze! ||8||

Oṃ hrīṃ yūṃ! O Amṛtadṛti, come, come! Having entered the heart of such-and-such a person, having seized even those of his own kind, and having forcibly drawn them forth, bring, bring him here in your form! Cause him to enter the water-pot and so forth; establish him there! Then come back, come back! [To] the water-pot.
Be firm, Vauṣaṇṇa, obeisance! Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ kreṃ hrīṃ āṃ yaralavaśaṣasahoṃ haṃsassohaṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ | Kreṃ hrīṃ āṃ klauṃ stabhaya stabhaya ||9||

Oṃ hrīṃ! O [Name], come here, come here; obeisance! O vital breaths, come here; O life-force, remain here! O all the senses, mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness of [Name], having arrived together, may you abide happily for a long time, live on, and grant your presence—svāhā! Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ yaralavaśaṣasahoṃ.

*Haṃsassohaṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ*. I establish the vital breaths (*prāṇa*), downward breath (*apāna*), pervasive breath (*vyāna*), ascending breath (*udāna*), and equalizing breath (*samāna*) within this jar. Thereafter: *Sajīni saṃyutakṣīrakramukajātaṣkajāti*.
Having offered as an oblation (naivedya) betel leaves, parched grain, mirīcika, kramuka, betel nut, fruit, milk-rice, boiled rice, black gram cakes, gulāpūpa, mudga-khaṇḍela, and gulādaka,
and having presented incense and lamps, one should then perform the limb-worship (aṅgapūjā).

Namely: Homage to Bhavā! I worship her feet. Homage to Jaganmātṛ! Homage to Jagatpitṛ! I worship her hips. Homage to Kālī! (L4) Homage to Kālāntaka! I worship her waist. Homage to Nāgendrakanyā! Homage to Nāgābharaṇā! I worship her navel.
Homage to the one who delights in praise; homage to the one worthy of praise.

(l5) I worship the breasts. Homage to Bhavasena; homage to the destroyer of existence (*bhava*). I worship the arms. Homage to the conch-necked one; homage to the dark-throated one (*kālakaṇṭha*). I worship the throat. Homage to Māyā. (l6)

Salutation to Maheśa. I worship the face. Salutation to Lalitā. Salutation to Lāsyapriyā. I worship the forehead. Salutation to Śiva. Salutation to Śiva. I worship the head. Oṃ, salutation to the remover of the distress of those who bow down. Salutation to the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down. I worship the feet. I offer ornaments. Salutation to Rudra. Water for sipping (ācamanīya).
I offer.
May the tawny steeds, mindful and white, bring you hither. Om. We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity, like a gourd from its stem.
From the bonds... [protect] me, the blind one, from the father.

(l2) Into this jar, I invoke Sāmbasadāśiva... I approach Sadyojāta; salutations indeed to Sadyojāta! O Bhava, in every existence, in that which transcends existence, favor me; salutations indeed to the source of existence. (l3)

*Namaḥ*. I offer a seat. *Sadyojātāya vai namaḥ*. I offer water for the feet (*pādya*). "In every birth, in every existence, do not transcend me; be devoted to me. I offer the guest-water (*arghya*). *Bhavodbhavāya namaḥ*. I offer water for sipping (*ācamanīya*). *Vāmadevāya namaḥ*. I offer a garment (*vastra*). *Jyeṣṭhāya namaḥ*. I offer the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*). To the Most Excellent One (*Śreṣṭhāya*).

Homage! I offer ornaments. (l5) Homage to Rudra; I offer water for sipping. Homage to Kalā; I offer perfumes. Homage to Kalavikaraṇa; I offer flowers. Homage to Balapramathana; I offer incense for you to smell. (l6)

Salutation to the Subduer of All Beings (*sarvabhūtadamanāya namaḥ*). I offer this lamp. Salutation to Him who has Transcended the Mind (*manonmanāya namaḥ*). At the proper time, I present the food offering (*naivedya*). [Recite] the prayer beginning with *aghorebhyaḥ* and so forth.

Having recited eleven times the verse beginning with *tatpuruṣāya vidmahe*, and having again offered prayers with the mantra beginning with *īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām*, one should then [worship] the fires and the digits of the Sun and Moon.
One should worship as follows:
at the lower part of the jar—Oṃ yaṃ, homage to the portion Dhūmrā; Oṃ raṃ, homage to the portion Arciṣmatī; Oṃ laṃ, homage to the portion Uṣṇā.

Oṃ vaṃ, obeisance to the Jvalanī-kalā. Oṃ śaṃ, obeisance to the Jvālinī-kalā. Oṃ ṣaṃ, obeisance to the Visphuliṅginī-kalā. (c 2) Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to the Suśrī-kalā. Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to the Kapilā-kalā. Oṃ laṃ, obeisance to the Havya-kalā. Oṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to the Kavya-kalā. Thus, on the lower part of the pitcher: obeisance to the tenfold fire-kalās. To the pitcher: obeisance to the Tapinī-kalā. (c 3)

Khaṃ baṃ, obeisance to the digit Tāvinī. Gaṃ phaṃ, obeisance to the digit Dhūmrakalā. Jhaṃ taṃ, obeisance to the digit Viśvā. Ñaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to the digit Bodhinī. Ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ, obeisance to the digit Dhāriṇī.
In the middle part of the pitcher—(c 4).

Salutations to the twelvefold digits of the Sun. Oṃ Aṃ, salutations to the digit Amṛtā. Āṃ, salutations to the digit Ānandā. Iṃ, salutations to the digit Pūṣā. Īṃ, salutations to the digit Tuṣṭi. Uṃ, salutations to the digit Puṣṭi. Ūṃ, salutations to the digit Rati. Ṛṃ, salutations to the digit Dhṛti.
l1) Oṃ ṛṃ, obeisance to Śaśinī-kalā; oṃ śaṃ, obeisance to Candrakalā; ḷṃ, obeisance to Kānti-kalā; eṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā-kalā;
aiṃ, obeisance to Śrīpadā-kalā; oṃ l2)
Salutation to Prītikalā. Oṃ, salutation to Aṅgadākalā. Aṃ, salutation to Pūrṇākalā. Aḥ, salutation to Pūrṇāmṛtakalā.
In front of the Śiva-pitcher, salutation to the sixteen lunar digits (ṣoḍaśasomakalā). Elsewhere, in front of the pitcher: Oṃ aṃ, salutation to Dīpikākalā. Āṃ, salutation to Rājasākalā. Oṃ hāṃ.

Salutation to Jvālinīkalā. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ravisthaliṅginīkalā. (l4) Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Pracaṇḍakalā. Oṃ haṃ ūṃ, salutation to Pācakākalā. Ṛṃ, salutation to Raudrīkalā. Oṃ hāṃ ṛṃ, salutation to Dāhakākalā. Oṃ hāṃ eṃ, salutation to Rohiṇī. (l5)
Salutation to Kalā. Oṃ Haṃ Aiṃ, salutation to Śiphāvanīkalā. Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Jyotiṣkalā. Thus are the eleven fire-energies (agni-kalās).
Among these, one should contemplate ten energies during activities such as cooking; the eleventh energy, Jyotis, is to be understood as the fire-energy.
In the middle part of the *kumbha*:

Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Ullolākalā. Aṃ, obeisance to Kallolinīkalā. Aṃ, obeisance to Uccalantikākalā. Oṃ kaṃ, obeisance to Unmanādikākalā. Khaṃ, obeisance to Taraṅgiṇīkalā. Gaṃ, obeisance to Śrotinīkalā.

Namaḥ! Ghaṃ, homage to Lampaṭākalā! Ṅaṃ, homage to Pravṛttakalā! Caṃ, homage to Lāharīkalā! Jaṃ, homage to Lelehānākalā! Chaṃ, homage to Lolākalā! Jhaṃ, homage to Āhlākalā! Ñaṃ, homage to Prastavantikalā! Ṭaṃ... (l2)

*Pravāhā* to the digit (*kalā*)—*namaḥ*. *Ṭhaṃ*, *Saumyā* to the digit—*namaḥ*. *Ḍaṃ*, *Pravāsakalā* to the digit—*namaḥ*. *Ḍhaṃ*, *Plavantī* to the digit—*namaḥ*. Thus are the seventeen lunar digits (*candrakalā*). Among these digits, the days (*dināni*) do not enter; having excluded sixteen digits, [the seventeenth] flows as the own digit of the single moon. In the lower part of the jar (*kumbha*), *Ṇaṃ* is for *Sthāpinīkalā*.

*Namaḥ*! *Taṃ* to the digit Sakākalā, *namaḥ*; *thaṃ* to the digit Prākalā, *namaḥ*; *daṃ* to the digit Ākuñcinīkalā, *namaḥ*; *yaṃ* to the digit Śoṣṇīkalā, *namaḥ*; *naṃ* to the digit Prabodhinīkalā, *namaḥ*;
*paṃ* to the digit Pasmarākalā, *namaḥ*.

Namaḥ! Phaṃ, obeisance to the digit Ghargharākalā. Baṃ, obeisance to the digit Ākarṣaṇīkalā. Bhaṃ, obeisance to the digit Tuṣṭivardhanakalā. Mam, obeisance to the digit Unmanekhākalā. ...... Raṇamatīkalāyai (l6) namaḥ. Raṃ, obeisance to the digit Tamohantrīkalā. Laṃ, obeisance to the digit Dharmajananīkalā. Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ, obeisance to the digit Prabhāvatīkalā. Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ.
*Kṣaṃ*, salutation to the digit of self-luminosity.
(L7) Thus are the sixteen solar digits (*sūryakalā*). Having thus worshipped, one should thereafter perform the worship of the Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-Īśvara-Sadāśiva kalpas.
It is as follows: *Kaṃ*, salutation to the digit of emanation (*sṛṣṭikalā*). *Khaṃ*... (p133b, f126a)
l1) Obeisance to Ṛddhikalā. Gaṃ, obeisance to Smṛtikalā. Ghaṃ, obeisance to Medhākalā. Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Śāntikalā. Caṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmikalā. Chaṃ, obeisance to Dūtikalā. l2)

From the feet up to the knees: *jaṃ* salutation to the digit of stability (*sthirākalā*); *jhaṃ* salutation to the digit of persistence (*sthitikalā*); *ñaṃ* salutation to the digit of accomplishment (*siddhikalā*); *akāraprabhāyai brahmakalāyai namaḥ* (salutation to the Brahma-digit, the radiance of the letter *a*). Thus one should worship from the feet up to the knees. For example: *ṭaṃ* salutation to the digit of old age (*jarākalā*); *ṭhaṃ* salutation to the digit of Vālinī; *ḍaṃ* salutation to the digit of peace (*śāntikalā*); *ḍhaṃ*.

Oṃ *Īśvarīkalāyai* namaḥ. (Ṇaṃ) *Ratikalāyai* namaḥ. Taṃ (l4) *Kāminīkalāyai* namaḥ. Thaṃ *Varadākalāyai* namaḥ. Daṃ *Hlādinīkalāyai* namaḥ. Vaṃ *Prītikalāyai* namaḥ. Naṃ *Dīrghakalāyai* namaḥ. To the radiance of the syllable *U*, to *Viṣṇukalā* (l5).

Salutation! One should worship from the knees up to the navel: *Paṃ* salutation to the Tīkṣṇā-kalā; *Phaṃ* salutation to the Raudrī-kalā; *Baṃ* salutation to the Nayā-kalā; *Bhaṃ* salutation to the Rudrā-kalā; *Maṃ* salutation to the Tandrī-kalā; *Yaṃ* salutation to the Kṣut-kalā; *Raṃ* salutation to the Krodhanī-kalā; *Laṃ* salutation to the Kriyā-kalā; *Vaṃ* salutation to the Udgārī-kalā; *Śaṃ*.

Salutation to Mṛtyukalā. Salutation to the Rudra-kalā, which has the radiance of the letter Ṣa; one should worship [her] from the navel up to the throat. Saṃ, salutation to Pitā-kalā. Saṃ, salutation to Śvetā-kalā. Haṃ, salutation to Karuṇā-kalā. Laṃ...

Homage to Sitākalā. Kṣaṃ, homage to Parākalā. Homage to Bidūdbhavā, the Īśvarakalā. One should worship from the throat up to the forehead. Aṃ, homage to Nivṛttikalā. Āṃ, homage to Pratiṣṭhākalā. Iṃ, homage to Vidyā...

Salutation to Kalā. *Īṃ*, salutation to Śāntikalā. *Uṃ*, salutation to Śāntyatītakalā. *Ūṃ*, salutation to Indhikākalā. *Ṛṃ*, salutation to Dīpikākalā. *Ṝṃ*, salutation to Rocikākalā. *Ḷṃ*, salutation to Mocikākalā. *Ḹṃ*, salutation to Ūrdhvagākalā. *Eṃ*, salutation to Vyāpinīkalā. *Aiṃ*, salutation to Vyomarūpaphaṇikalā.
Salutation! Oṃ, salutation to Anantākalā;
auṃ, salutation to Anāthākalā; aṃ, salutation to Anāśritākalā; aḥ, salutation to Akṣayiṇīkalā; [salutation] to Sadāśivākalā, who possesses the power of the syllable Oṃ.

One should worship [the deity] from the forehead up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). Thereafter, preceded by the worship of the lotus of the syllables (*lipipaṅkaja*), one should perform the worship of the thirty-six *kalās*, the worship of the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*), and the worship of the six paths (*ṣaḍadhvan*).
It is as follows: (l6)

Oṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self in the form of the Mūrti. Laṃ, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self in the form of the aperture (randhra). Vaṃ, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to Dharma, the Self in the form of the eastern knot. Laṃ, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to Jñāna, the Self in the form of the southeastern knot. Īṃ nya, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to Vairāgya, the Self in the form of the southern petal. Yaṃ nya, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to Aiśvarya, the Self in the form of the northern petal. Māṃ nya...

To Śiva, to Kaṃ... to the Self of the [eastern] filament, obeisance! To Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to Śiva, to the Self of the southeastern filament, obeisance! To Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Caṃ, obeisance to Śiva, to the Self of the [southern] filament, obeisance! To Chaṃ...

*Jaṃ jhaṃ*, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the one whose essence is the filament of the south. *Ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ*, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the one whose essence is the filament of the southwest (*nirṛti*). *Ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ*, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the one whose essence is the filament of the west. *Taṃ thaṃ daṃ*, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the one whose essence is the filament of the northwest (*vāyavya*). *Yaṃ naṃ paṃ*, obeisance to Śiva; [obeisance] to the one whose essence is the filament of the north.

*Namaḥ* | *Phaṃ vaṃ bhaṃ*, obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the filaments in the northeast; obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the eastern petal; obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the southeast petal; obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the southern petal; obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the southwest petal; obeisance to *namaśśivāya*, the essence of the [northwest] petal.

*Paścimadalātmane namaḥ* (Salutation to the essence of the western petal). *Eṃ Aiṃ namaḥ śivāya vāyavyadalātmane namaḥ* (Salutation to Śiva; salutation to the essence of the northwestern petal). *Oṃ Auṃ namaḥ śivāya uttaradalātmane namaḥ* (Salutation to Śiva; salutation to the essence of the northern petal). *Aṃ Āṃ namaḥ śivāya aiśānyadalātmane namaḥ* (Salutation to Śiva; salutation to the essence of the northeastern petal). *Ūrdhvamūrdhni īśānassarvavidyānāṃ śaśinyai namaḥ* (On the upper crown: salutation to the Moon of Īśāna, the Lord of all sciences). *Pūrvamūrdhni* (On the eastern crown)... [Īśvarassarva... (The Lord of all...).
"Salutation to Aṅgadā, the mistress of all beings"—on the right head. "Salutation to Brahmeṣṭā, the sovereign of Brahmā and the overlord of Brahmā"—on the northern head. "May Śiva be mine;
salutation to Marīci"—on the western head. "Salutation to Jvālinī, the ever-auspicious Śiva"—having thus deposited the five *kalās* on the head in the Īśāna direction.

*Oṃ hāṃ hoṃ, salutation to the one whose form is the unmanifest *praṇava*, to the *kalā* beyond peace*—thus for the upper mantra. *Oṃ, we know that Puruṣa; salutation to Peace*—on the eastern face. *We meditate upon Mahādeva; salutation to Knowledge*—on the southern face. *Oṃ heṃ, may Rudra inspire us;
salutation to Foundation*—on the northern face. *May He impel us; salutation to Cessation*—(line 2).

— at the western face; and the *tatpuruṣa*-kalā for him: *oṃ hāṃ huṃ aghorebhyaḥ stamāyai namaḥ* — at the heart; then *ghorebhyaḥ mohāyai namaḥ* — thus at the neck; *ghorajayāyai namaḥ* — on the right shoulder; *ghoratarebhyaḥ rakṣāyai namaḥ* — on the left shoulder; *śarvataḥ sarvamṛtyave namaḥ* — at the navel; *sarvebhyaḥ māyāyai*.
*Namaḥ*—to the belly. *Namaste astu* (l4)—homage to Rudrajayā—*namaḥ*—to the back. *Oṃ rudrarūpebhyo jarāyai namaḥ*—to the chest. Thus ends the eightfold group of the Bahurūpa-kalās.
*Oṃ hāṃ hiṃ vāmadevāya namo jarāyai namaḥ* (l5).

Thus—at the secret place (*guhya*): "Salutation to Jyeṣṭha for protection" (*rakṣāyai*)—at the *liṅga*. "Salutation to Rudra; salutation to Rati"—on the right thigh. "Salutation to Kālā; salutation to Pālī"—on the left thigh. "Salutation to Kalakāmā"—on the right knee. "Salutation to Vikaraṇa; salutation to Samyamatī"—thus on the left knee. "Salutation to Balakriyā"—[on the right ankle].
On the right calf: *namo vikaraṇāya*, *namo buddhyai*—on the left calf.

(l7) *namo balakārye*—on the right buttock. *namo balapramathanāya*, *namo dhātryai*—on the left buttock. *namo sarvabhūtadamanāya*, *namo brāhmaṇyai*—on the right hip. *namo mohinyai*—on the right side. (p135b, f128a)
*l1) "Salutation to Unmanā; salutation to Bhava"—on the left side. Thus are the thirteen kalās of Vāmadeva.
*Oṃ hāṃ, I take refuge in Sadyojāta; salutation to Siddhi*—on the right foot. *Sadyo* *l2)*...

"Salutation to Jātā-Ṛddhi—on the left foot; salutation to Dyuti—on the right hand; salutation to Abhavā-Lakṣmī—on the left hand; salutation to Anādibhavā-Medhā—on the nose. (L3) "Oṃ, worship me! Salutation to Kānti—on the head; Oṃ, worship [me]! Salutation to Svadhā—on the right arm; Oṃ, salutation to Udbhava—"
"Salutation to Dhṛti"—on the left arm. Thus ends the eight-fold ritual of Sadyojāta.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) starting from the thumb and ending with the little finger, and having performed the worship, one should perform the worship according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikramārcana*). Immediately thereafter—
One should perform the assignment of the fourteen worlds (*bhuvana*). It is as follows: at the feet—*aṃ*, *āṃ*, *im*.

Salutation to Sadāśiva, whose nature is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the foundational power (ādhāra-śakti) and joined with the primordial deity (mūla-devatā) of the infinite millions of secret Yoginīs residing in the blue realm of the Atala world;

Gaṃ Hyaiṃ Ī Ū Ūṃ. Salutation to Paramaśiva, accompanied by the foundational power and joined with the primordial deity of the infinite great secrets and Yoginīs residing in the blue realm of the Vitala world.
Homage!

(l7) To the calves—*ṛ ṛṃ*: Homage to Śiva, whose essential nature is the Supreme Self accompanied by Śakti, the root deity of the hundred million secret and inconceivable Yoginīs residing in the world of Sutala. ||3|| ||4?||

At the knees: *ḷṃ ḹṃ* | Salutation to Śiva, whose essential nature is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the foundational power (*mūla-śakti*) and the inconceivable Yoginīs who are the secret deities residing in the world of Nitala, numbering hundreds of millions.
At the buttocks: *eṃ aiṃ* | [Salutation to Śiva] residing in the world of Talātala... || 136a, l1–l2 ||
Salutation to Sadāśiva, whose nature is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the foundational power (Ādhāraśakti) and joined with the root deity of the hundred crore Yoginīs. ||5||

At the waist: Oṃ auṃ, obeisance to the Yoginī who is the supreme self-nature, accompanied by the foundational power (dhāraśakti) of the root deity of the Guhyayoginīs, numbering hundreds of millions, residing in the Mahātala and Pātāla worlds; for the sake of Śiva. 6.

At the navel: *Aṃ Aḥ*, obeisance to Sadāśiva, whose nature is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the foundational power (*dhāraśakti*) and the inconceivable goddess Ḍākinī, the secret deity of the hundred million worlds of the nether regions (*rasātalaloka*). ||7||

At the Mūlādhāra: Oṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ, salutations to Sadāśiva, whose nature is the Supreme Self, who resides in the world of Bhūr, who is accompanied by the hundred million secret [deities], the inconceivable Yoginīs, and the primordial deity, together with the foundational power (Ādhāra-śakti). ||8||

On the Svādhiṣṭhāna-liṅga: Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ. Salutation to Sadāśiva, whose nature is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the foundational power (Ādhāra-śakti), joined with ten million secret Ḍākinīs and Yoginīs who dwell in the Bhuvarloka, and together with the primordial deity (Mūla-devatā). ||9||

In the Maṇipūraka at the navel: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ*. Homage to the Supreme Self, Śiva, together with the foundational power (*mūladevatādhāraśakti*) of the secret Yoginīs numbering hundreds of millions who reside in the Suvarloka.
In the Anāhata [cakra]: *taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ* [residing in] Maharloka.
Salutation to the Supreme Śiva, the Self, who is the supreme secret of hundreds of millions of abodes, accompanied by the Yoginī Laṅkinī and the foundational power (Ādhāraśakti). ||11||
Regarding purification—at the root of the palate: *vāṃ*, *paṃ*, *phaṃ*, *baṃ*, *bhaṃ*, *maṃ*.

Salutation to the Supreme Self, Sadāśiva, who is accompanied by the support-power (*ādhāraśakti*), the goddess Kākinī, the one who dwells in the world of living beings, the hundred million *gapaśas*, and the primordial deity. 12.
On the forehead of the Command (ājñā): Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ.

Salutation to the Supreme Self (paramātman), Sadāśiva, who is more secret than ten million guptatara-siddhas, accompanied by the primordial deity (mūladevatā), the Yoginīs, the Ākīnīs, and the supporting power (ādhāraśakti), and who is the blue one of the world of asceticism (tapoloka). ||13||

In the aperture of Brahmā (the *brahmarandhra*): Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ. Salutation to the Supreme Self, Śiva, who resides in Satyaloka, who is dark blue, who is joined with the root deity of the Ahamakini who has attained the supreme secret, and who is accompanied by the Support-Energy (*ādhāraśakti*). ||14||

At the *dvādaśānta* is *laṃ kṣaṃ*; in that place [reside] the ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose; speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals; and the powers of digestion, giving, movement, excretion, and bliss; as well as the cognitions of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; and those known as Śāntyatīta, Kalā, Īṣṭāna, and Sadāśiva.
O Supreme Lord, I worship you, the embodiment of Īśāna, accompanied by the Śakti Hṛllekhā, who is beyond both Śiva and Śivā. ||1||
Oṃ! To the one known as Sadāśiva, the presiding deity of the Kṣetrajña, the ear, speech, sound, knowledge, peace, and the transcendent Kalās;
to the form of Īśāna, accompanied by the Śakti Hṛllekhā, O Supreme Lord whose nature is Śiva and Śivā—I worship you. 2.

In the principle of Prakṛti, I worship the one called Dākinī—the supreme lord whose nature is Śiva and Śivā, who is accompanied by Gaganā, and who is the embodiment of Tatpuruṣa, presided over by the power of tranquility through the breeze of the touch of your hand. ||3||

Oṃ! I worship you, O Supreme Lord, who are established in the arts of knowledge and the radiance of the form of the eye of wisdom, who are called Rudra, whose fierce form is endowed with the spoken [mantras], and who are the embodiment of Śiva-Śivā. 4.

In the heart: Oṃ! O you who preside over the principles (kalās) beginning with ego (ahaṅkāra), taste (rasana), the anus (pāyu), water (salila), and touch (spraṣṭṛ); O divine form of Vāmadeva, known as Viṣṇu; O Supreme Lord, whose nature is both Śiva and Śivā; I worship you. 5.

In the secret place: O Supreme Lord, whose nature is Śiva-Śivātman, who are the presiding deity of the withdrawal of the mind, nose, genitals, and smell, and who are the form of Sadyojāta known as Brahmā; I worship you, Karālīka. ||6||
At the feet: *haṃ saḥ*. "Hara jaṃ jhaṃ, salutation to Vyomaśiva Śivāya.

(L5) Now, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) and worship of the Kalāmātṛkā, as well as the placement and worship of the Mūrtīśvara and Tatvatatveśvara based on the Śrīkaṇṭhamātṛkā and the Mūrtimātṛkā.
It is as follows: *oṃ aṃ* (L6).

Salutation to Nivṛttikalā. Iṃ, salutation to Vidyākalā. Uṃ, salutation to Śāntyatītakalā. Ūṃ, salutation to Dīpikākalā. Ṛṃ, salutation to Mocikākalā. (L7) Aṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhākalā. Īṃ, salutation to Śāntikalā. Uṃ, salutation to Iḍikalā. Ṛṃ, salutation to Rocikākalā. Ḷṃ, salutation to Ūrdhvagaṃ.
Salutation to Kalā.
(p137b, f130a, c1) Ḷṃ, salutation to Varākalā; Eṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmākalā; Aiṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmāmṛtākalā; Oṃ, salutation to Jñānāmṛtākalā.

Salutations! Oṃ, salutations to the pervasive Kalā. Aṃ, salutations to the Kalā whose form is space. Aṃ, salutations to the infinite Kalā. Kaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of creation. Khaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of prosperity. Gaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of maintenance. Ghaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of wisdom. Ṅaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of beauty. Caṃ, salutations to the Kalā of fortune. Chaṃ, salutations to the Kalā of splendor. (c 3)
Jaṃ, salutation to the digit Sthirā; jhaṃ, salutation to the digit Dhṛti; ñaṃ, salutation to the digit Siddhi; ṭaṃ, salutation to the digit Jarā;

ṭhaṃ, salutation to the digit Pālinī; ḍaṃ, salutation to the digit Śānti; ḍhaṃ, salutation to the digit Īśvarī; (c 4) ṇaṃ, salutation to the digit Rati; taṃ, salutation to the digit Kāmikā; thaṃ, salutation to the digit Varadā; daṃ, salutation to the digit Svādinī; dhaṃ.

Praṃ, obeisance to the digit of Delight (prīti-kalā). Naṃ, obeisance to the digit of Long Sound (dīrgha-kākalā). Paṃ, obeisance to the digit of Sharpness (tīkṣṇa-kalā). Phaṃ, obeisance to the digit of Fierce Power (raudrī-kalā). Baṃ, obeisance to the digit of Compassion (dayā-kalā). Bhaṃ, obeisance to the digit of the Giver (dātrī-kalā). Maṃ, obeisance to the digit of Sleep (nidrā-kalā). Yaṃ, obeisance to the digit of Hunger (kṣudh-kalā). Raṃ, obeisance to the digit of Anger (krodha-kalā). Laṃ, obeisance to the digit of Action (kriyā-kalā).

Paṃ, salutation to the *kalā* named Udgā; mu, salutation to the *kalā* named Mṛtyu; ṣaṃ, salutation to the *kalā* named Pitā; su, salutation to the *kalā* named Śvetā; haṃ, salutation to the *kalā* named Raṇā; laṃ, salutation to the *kalā* named Asitā; kṣaṃ, salutation to the *kalā* named Kṣamā. (l2) Oṃ. Of this mantra for the assignment (*nyāsa*) of Śrīkaṇṭha, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (*devatā*), and Bhaṃ Sāṃ Aṃ is the seed-syllable (*bīja*).

Haṃ Suṃ Āṃ—Śakti. Haṃ Sūṃ Iṃ—Kīlaka. (L3) For the sake of my enjoyment and liberation, and for the sake of attaining the grace of Ardhanārīśvara, this is the application (*viniyoga*) in the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and recitation (*japa*). The visualization (*dhyāna*):
[He is] resembling molten gold, seated upon a beautiful throne...
We take refuge in that Śama, who holds the rosary, the noose, and the goad with his own staff-like arms,
who is adorned with fragments of arrows,
who has three eyes, and whose half [is] Ambikā; he is the abode of the city of night for the Destroyer.

Having meditated thus, and having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) from the thumb to the little finger with: *haṃ sāṃ haṃ sīḥ | haṃ sū haṃ saiṃ hā sauṃ haṃ saḥ*, this is the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
Then, at the hairline: *oṃ śrīṃ kuṃ klīṃ aṃ śrīti*.
Salutation to the throat. Salutation to Pūrṇodarī.
On the forehead: Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, salutation to Ananta and Vijayā. On the right eye: Iṃ, salutation to Sūkṣma and Śālmali.
On the left eye: *Raṃ triṃ raṃ*, obeisance to Trimūrti Lolākṣī.
On the right ear: *Uṃ*, obeisance to Amareśa Vakulākṣī.
In the left ear: *Oṃ* to Aghīśa and Dīrghakoṇā, salutation! In the right nostril: *Ṛṃ* to Bhārabhūti and Dīrghamukhī, salutation!
In the left nostril: *Ṛṃ* to Tithīśa and Gomukhī, salutation! (L2)
On the right cheek: *ḷṃ* to Sthāṇu and Dīrghajihvā, salutation.
On the left cheek: *ḹṃ* to Hara and Kuṇḍodarī, salutation.
On the upper lip: *eṃ* to Jhaṇḍīśa and Ūrdhvakeśī, salutation. (3)
On the lower lip: *Aiṃ*, salutation to Bhautika and Vikṛtāmukhī.
On the upper teeth: *Laṃ*, salutation to Sadyojāta and Jvālāmukhī.
On the lower teeth: *Auṃ*, salutation to Anugraheśa and Ulkāmukhī. (L4.)
At the chin: *aṃ* to Krūra, the chief of Śrī, obeisance.
At the mouth: *aḥ* to Mahāsena, the chief of Vidyā, obeisance. At the base of the right arm: *kaṃ* to Krodheśa, the great Kālī praised by the hosts, obeisance. (L5)
At the elbow (korpara) [and] the space (khaṃ): *namaḥ* to Caṇḍeśa and Sarasvatī.
At the wrist (maṇibandha) [1]: *gaṃ*, *namaḥ* to Pañcāntaka and Sarvasiddhi. On the palm of the hand (pāṇitala) [1]: *ghaṃ*, *namaḥ* to Śivaśakti.
At the elbow joint—... (ṅaṃ-caṃ)—obeisance to Ekanetra and Hutabhujī.
At the wrist—2—jaṃ—obeisance to Caturmukha and Lambodarī.
On the palm of the right hand—*jhaṃ*, obeisance to Ajeśa and Drāviṇī.
At the tips of the fingers—*ñaṃ*, obeisance to Śarva and Nāgarī.
On the right foot—(l7)
At the base: *Ṭaṃ* to Someśa and Khecarī, *namaḥ*. At the knees: *Ṭhaṃ* to Lāṅgalin and Mañjarī, *namaḥ*. At the shanks: *Ḍaṃ* to Darukṣa and Rūpiṇī, *namaḥ*.

On the sole of the foot—Ḍaṃ (Ḍhaṃ), salutation to Ardhanārīśvara and Virūṇyā (Piṇyā). On the tip of the foot—Ṇaṃ, salutation to Umākānta and Komarī. At the root of the left foot—Taṃ, salutation to Āṣāḍha and Pūtanyā.
On the left knee: *thaṃ* to Daṇḍin Bhadrakālī, homage!
On the shanks: *daṃ* to Atri Yoginī, homage!
On the sole of the foot—*śaṃ*, salutation to Mitā and Śaṅkhinī.
At the tip of the foot—*naṃ*, salutation to Meṣa and Garjinī. On the right side—*paṃ*, salutation to Lohita and Kālarātri. (L3)
On the left side—phaṃ ...khinetrābjinyai namaḥ.
On the back part—baṃ chagalandhāya kapardinyai namaḥ. At the navel—bhaṃ dviraṇḍāya vajriṇyai namaḥ.
In the heart: *maṃ*, salutation to Mahākāla and Jayā. In the armor: *yaṃ*, salutation to Kapālin and Sumukhī.
To blood—*raṃ*, obeisance to Bhujaṅga and Revatī;
to flesh—*laṃ*, obeisance to Pinākin and Māyavī;
to fat—*vaṃ*, obeisance to Khaḍgīśa and Vāruṇī.
In the bones: *śaṃ* to Śambaka, to Vāyavyā, obeisance.
In the marrow: *ṣaṃ* to Śveta, to Rakṣopasāriṇī, obeisance. In the semen: *saṃ*... (l6)
At the Mṛga [tattva]: *mṛgavai sahajāyai namaḥ*.
At the heart: *haṃ prāṇātmane lakulīśāya lakṣmyai namaḥ*.
At the base of the liṅga: *laṃ śivāya vyāpinyai namaḥ*.
At the tip of the *liṅga*: *kṣaṃ* to the Wrathful Self, Saṃvartaka, and to Māyā, [I offer] salutation.
One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the embodied and the lord of the embodiments (*mūrtimūrtīśvara*), which pervades both Śiva and Śakti at their root.

In the *liṅga*—that is, in the portions of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra—one should perform the worship of the installation (*nyāsa*) of the images from the feet up to the head. In the human body, [the installation is] from the feet up to the navel: *Oṃ hlāṃ, obeisance to the Ātmatattva; to its presiding deity, Brahmā.*
Homage! From the navel to the throat, homage to the Vidyā-tattva.
To its presiding deity, Oṃ hlāṃ Viṣṇave namaḥ. From the throat to the top of the head, homage to the Śiva-tattva. To the presiding deity of the Śiva-tattva, Oṃ hūṃ Rudrāya namaḥ.
In the *mūlādhāra*: *oṃ hāṃ kṣmāmūrtaye namaḥ*.
(L3) To Śarva, the lord of the earth-form (*kṣmāmūrti*), obeisance.
In the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: *oṃ hāṃ vahnimūrtaye namaḥ*. To Paśupati, the lord of the fire-form (*vahnimūrti*), obeisance.

In Maṇipūraka: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the form of the Sacrificer; salutation to Ugra, the presiding lord of the form of the Sacrificer. In the heart: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the form of Arka; salutation to Rudra, the presiding lord of the form of Arka.
At the throat: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Water-form; salutation to Bhava, the lord of the Water-form. At the palms: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Air-form; salutation to Īśāna, its lord.
In the center: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Niśākara-mūrti;
salutation to his lord, Mahādeva.
On the head: O hauṃ, salutation to Vyoma-mūrti; Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Bhīma, the lord of Vyoma-mūrti.
At the base: *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Dharāmūrti; obeisance to Brahmā, the lord of Dharāmūrti*. At the navel: obeisance to Jalamūrti; obeisance to Viṣṇu, its lord.
In the heart: homage to the form of Agni; homage to Rudra, its presiding deity. In the mouth: homage to the form of Vāyu; homage to Īśvara, its presiding deity.

On the head: *Oṃ*, salutation to the one whose form is the sky (*vyomamūrti*); salutation to Sadāśiva, the lord of that [element]. One should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the Lord of the Principles of Reality (*tattvatattveśvara*). On the feet: salutation to the Earth-principle (*pṛthivītattva*); salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha, the lord of that [element].
In the calves—*namaḥ* to the water-principle (*jalatattva*). *Taṃ ye*—*namaḥ* to the Lord of Waters (*jaleśa*).
In the navel—*namaḥ* to the fire-principle (*agnitattva*). *Taṃ ye tviṣāṃ nidhaye*—*namaḥ* to the repository of splendors.
In the heart—*namaḥ* to the wind-principle (*vāyutattva*). *Taṃ ye tṛṇabhuje*. (l3)

*Namaḥ*. On the head: *namaḥ* to the principle of space (*vyomatattva*). *Taṃ ye* to the subtle (*sūkṣma*). On the nose: *namaḥ* to the principle of smell (*gandhatattva*). *Taṃ ye* to the sense of smell (*gandhākṣa*).

In the eyes—*namaḥ* to the principle of form (*rūpa-tattva*). *Taṃ* (or *ye*)—*namaḥ* to the Sun (*bhānu*). In the tongue—*namaḥ* to the principle of taste (*rasa-tattva*). *Taṃ* (or *ye*)—*namaḥ* to the Lord of Taste (*rasādhipa*).

In the organ of touch—salutation to the principle of touch (*sparśa-tattva*); salutation to *taṃ ye*, the most powerful. In the ear—salutation to the principle of sound (*śabda-tattva*); salutation to *taṃ ye*, the subtle bliss.
In the organ of generation—(l5)
Homage to the reality of the private parts; homage to those who possess the thunderous roar. At the feet—homage to the reality of the feet; homage to those who perform the treading.
At the hands—homage to the reality of the hands; homage to those who... (l6)
Salutation to Samādāthanā.
To Vaci—the principle of speech—salutation. To Taṃ ye bhujabhyām—the two arms—salutation. To Nāsike—the two nostrils—the principle of the nose—salutation. To Taṃ ye bimbakāya—the image—salutation.
On the tongue: *jihvātattvāya namaḥ*; *taṃ ye mahāvaktrāya namaḥ*. On the eyes: *cakṣustattvāya namaḥ*; *taṃ ye prakāśakāya namaḥ*.
In the skin—homage to the principle of the skin; homage to the one who is all-limbed.
In the ear—homage to the principle of the ear.
Salutation to Vyoman, the lord thereof;

at the heart—salutation to the principle of mind (*manas-tattva*); salutation to Saṅkalpa, that [principle]; salutation to the principle of ego (*ahaṅkāra-tattva*); salutation to Ahaṅkṛti, the lord thereof;
salutation to the principle of intellect (*buddhi-tattva*); ... [the lord] thereof.

Having covered [the area], [one says]: *Namaḥ* to the Buddha; *namaḥ* to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*); *namaḥ* to the Grandfather (*pitāmaha*), the lord of the principle of primordial nature.

From the navel up to the heart: *namaḥ* to the principle of the Person (*puruṣa-tattva*); *namaḥ* to Viṣṇu, its lord. *Namaḥ* to the principle of passion (*rāga-tattva*); *namaḥ* to Taṃye Pallava. *Namaḥ* to the principle of necessity (*niyati-tattva*); *namaḥ* to Bṛhaddhvaja, its lord. *Namaḥ* to the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*); *namaḥ* to Taṃye.

Salutation to Meghanāda. Salutation to Kālatattva. Salutation to its lord, Śikhivaktra. Salutation to Kalātattva. Salutation to its lord, Dhvajādhipa. Salutation to Māyātattva. Salutation to its lord, Viṣāṇa.
On the head—in five locations—Oṃ, salutation to Śuddhavidyātattva.

Salutation to Him who is Kalyāṇa; salutation to the principle of Īśvara. Salutation to Him who is Caturānana; salutation to the principle of Sadāśiva. Salutation to Him who is Keśa; Oṃ, salutation to the principle of Śakti. Salutation to Him who is Śambhu; salutation to the principle of Śiva. Salutation to Him who is Soma; Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the thirty-six principles and their lords. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and worship.

Having performed [this], however, since it is stated in the *Kāmika* and other Āgamas that the consecration of the jar (*kumbhādhivāsa*) lasts until the eleventh day, for how long should the consecration last— is it for five days, or for as many days as are required? For that duration, there is the contraction of the jar (*kumbhasaṅkocana*).

Immediately thereafter, beginning with the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breath) and continuing up to the placement (*nyāsa*) and worship of the *mūrti*, *mūrtīśvara*, *tattva*, and *tattveśvara*, the worship and placement should be performed upon the consecrated jars (*adhivāsakumbha*). After the consecration of the jars, all of this should likewise be performed upon the *liṅga*.
