On this auspicious lunar day, for the sake of the restoration of the ancient [shrine] of this Lord of Devas, Śrī Veṇuvaneśvara, together with his consort Ambā Śrī Kāntimatī, accompanied by the Śrī Mūla-liṅga, along with his retinue, and Sadāśiva. [The rite of] the restoration of the dilapidated... (l4)

For the purpose of binding [the deity], for the sake of removing the defects of contact with artisans, for the purification of the liṅga through the removal of the garland, and for the purification of the temple such as the abode of Śiva;
and for the sake of the presence of the Liṅga preceded by the protection of devotees such as ourselves—

I shall perform the purification of the Liṅga consisting of the auspicious day (puṇyāha), the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), wiping, circumambulation with fire (paryagnikaraṇa), sprinkling with oil and water, the oblation of drops (saṃpātahoma), and the gift of a cow (godāna).

Having thus resolved, having touched the sacrificial cake (*apūpa*), and having performed the *puṇyāha* and *pañcagavya* rites according to the rules, one should sprinkle the root-linga and the pavilion with those two [liquids] using the Weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*),
using one hundred and twenty plus a half (*sārdha*) bundles of *darbha* grass.

Having wiped [the image] three times with the Pāśupata [mantra], starting from the pedestal up to the *liṅga*; having consecrated it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) while reciting the mantra "śuddhair uttha"; and having worshipped a cow together with its calf while reciting the mantra "gavām aṅge";

then, having prepared a five-compartment area in front of the deity; having fashioned an altar (*sthaṇḍila*) with rice and other grains; and having strewn it around with *darbha* grass and flowers—upon those [compartments]:

Having brought five earthen vessels, each with a capacity of one *droṇa* of water when wrapped with threads, having washed and consecrated them; having placed them in the five central and other compartments with the *Hṛdaya-mantra*; having poured oil into the center with the *Śivāstra-mantra*; and having worshipped it with that same mantra; [in the] eastern [compartment]—the *Pāśāṅkuśas*.

Having placed leaves of the *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, *plakṣa*, *palāśa*, and *bilva* trees, and having filled [the vessel] with water, one should worship it with the *Pāśupata* mantra. On the south—having placed flowers of the white *karavīra*, *kuṭaja*, *nandyāvarta*, and *pāṭalī*—one should sprinkle it with the *Aghora-astra* mantra. On the west—[fragrant substances such as] perfumes, black scents, red scents, musk, and moist camphor.

Having cast in a measure of one *karṣa*, and having sprinkled it thoroughly with the *kṣurikā* weapon-mantra, [one places] in the north: *sūryakānta*, *candrakānta*, *ayaskānta*, and *sucikānta*; having cast these in, and having filled it with water, [one recites] the *vyomāstra* weapon-mantra.

Having performed worship, and once again having prepared a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) before Śiva, one should construct the sacrificial enclosure. Having prepared the mound with rice and other grains in the four corners starting from the southeast, and having performed the rites such as inspection (*vīkṣaṇa*) upon it— measuring one *droṇa* of water— one should thus establish the vessels with the *hṛdaya-mantra*.
In an earthen vessel from the southeast, in a bull's horn, in a fertile field, in the ocean,
in an elephant's tusk, on a mountain, or on a riverbank—

having placed [the substance] in a quantity measured by a handful (*añjali*), having filled it with water purified by a cloth, and having worshipped it with the *Skanda-mantra*— [one places] the *palāśa* [leaf] in the vessel of Nirṛti.

Having filled [the vessel] with water combined with the bark of *udumbara*, *aśvattha*, *madhuka*, *plakṣa*, *pāṭalī*, and *jambu*, and having worshipped it with the ten seeds, [one should place it] in the vessel situated in the northwest corner—
[namely] *gokṣura*, *sahadevī*, *viṣṇukrāntā*, and *mallikā*.
Having filled the vessel with water and consecrated it with the *kṣurikā* mantra,
one should place in the *īśāna* vessel the tips of *dūrvā* grass, the tips of *kuśa* grass, sesame, *pāṭala*, mustard, *bhadra*, and *droṇa* flowers.

Having arranged these [mantras], filled [the vessel] with water, worshipped it with the *saṃhitā* mantras, offered incense and lamps, and presented the food offering— thus, having fully worshipped the four purificatory jars (*catuḥ-śuddhi-kalaśa*). (l5) Thus [ends the section].

Now, the procedure for immersion (*avagāha*): Having properly fashioned [the image] from *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, or *panasa* wood, in the shape of a cow’s udder and devoid of a head; having made it the size of a *liṅga*, neither too small nor too large; having joined it to the pedestal; having filled the interior with flour of mung beans and so forth; and having worshipped it with the eight-syllable mantra for a quarter-watch (*yāmapāda*).

How should one perform the immersion? Again, having washed the root-linga with pure water and having prepared the supreme *pañcagavya*, one should fill the hollow of the *golaka* above the root-linga with *pañcagavya* using the five Brahma-mantras and then immerse the vessel.
At the time of immersion—
one should perform the recitation (japa) of the *garbhageya* all around in sequence,
beginning first with the root-syllable.

In the south—the mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti; in the west—the principal seed-syllable; in the north—the Gaula mantra; and Nara in the direction of Agni (the southeast). In the southwest—the Heart; in the northwest—Vyomavyāpin; in the northeast—the Brahmagāyatrī and the Śivagāyatrī, the two Śaktis, the Trimūrti mantra, Aghora, and the five Brahmans.

Having had the Brāhmaṇas perform the recitation of the Navadurgā-mantra, the Śakti-mantra, the Mṛtyuñjaya[-mantra], the Śrīrudra, and the complete recitation (*pārāyaṇa*) of the four Vedas, and having immersed the primary liṅga [in water],
then— [he offers] cardamom, cloves, camphor, lotus, nutmeg, and jasmine.
Sandalwood, agallochum, kaccola, and uśīra, combined with saffron.
Sandalwood water, bilva, and musk—
well-prepared with these specific ingredients, it is prescribed as ten niṣkas.
Having anointed the root-liṅga with sandalwood water mixed [with the other substances], one should worship it.
Now, the water stations are described: first is water with water; second is leaf-water;
(l6) third is scented water; fourth is fruit-water; fifth is root-water; sixth is bark-water; seventh is flower-water; eighth is pacifying water; beyond this is other water. (l7)

Thus these nine... will be explained. Just as one would fill a jar up to the brim (*āḍhaka*) and then cast it into water without [opening] its mouth—[in that water are] the rivers and so forth, such as the Nandī; in that water from the jar (*kumbhajala*), *oṃ*... [should be performed] in the hand so that it may come to pass.

Having collected auspicious water as it is obtained—whether for half a month or at the end of a month—placing it in a water-jar (*ambukumbha*)... having prepared [the vessel] with *bilva* leaves and gold pieces, one should take that water... by means of which [it is purified].
The wise one should especially fill the new pitcher.
Tulasī, Bilva leaves, Tagara, Tapasvinī,
Apāmārga, and Śamī— this is what is here called "water with leaves."
Sandalwood, black iron, campaka, uśīra,
haribera, camphor, kuṣṭha, nutmeg, and uragapurīṣa.
Water combined with [fragrant substances] is known as "scented water" (*gandhodaka*).

It should possess the fragrance of *utphala*, the fragrance of blue lotus (*nīlotpala*), the fragrance of white water lily (*kumuda*), the fragrance of red lotus (*raktapadma*), and the two types of *uśīra*. Having thus prepared the root-water, [one should offer] breadfruit and coconut.
Having prepared fruit water from the two kinds of *mātuluṅga*, *nāraṅga*, *likuca*, and *cūta*; and having prepared bark-water from *māyūra*, *caturaṅgula*, *bilva*, *kapittha*, and *nirguṇḍī*;
and [having prepared flower-water] from *punnāga*, *āravaka*, *nandyāvarta*, *dhūdhūra*, *śvetārka*, and *vakula*—in this manner, one prepares the flower-water.

Having prepared *kuṭṭam*, *kuṭaja*, *medhā*, sandalwood (*candana*), saffron (*kuṅkuma*), camphor (*karpūra*), and *uśīra*, one should thus prepare the water for pacification (*śāntyodaka*). Having prepared the *māyūra* [water] with *mālatī*, *kroḍocanā*, realgar (*manaśśilā*), *nirguṇḍī*, and *girikarṇī*, and other such waters, one should prepare a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) with rice and other grains in front of the deity.

Having performed [the preliminary rites], having strewn [the area] with *darbha* grass and flowers, having arranged nine compartments, having sprinkled [them] with the *astra-mantra*, and having worshipped [them] with the *varma-mantra*, [one should prepare] new earthen vessels provided with threads, lids, cloths, and gold, and joined with leaves of the *palāśa* tree; having thus prepared such vessels filled with water for the *arghya* offering... water.

Having placed [the vessel] in the middle of the pitcher and worshipped the *manonmaṇi*, one should sequentially arrange the water for the feet and the other offerings starting from the east up to the northeast. Having worshipped the nine powers, beginning with Vāmā, within them,
and having offered worship with incense, lamps, recitation (*japa*), and so forth, [one should perform] the *saṃhitā*...

Having consecrated [the water] with mantras and having thus prepared the various divisions of water, one should place the vessel for the stream— made of gold, silver, copper, clay, or other materials, provided with two valves and distinguished by a central aperture—
above the liṅga. Having had a tortoise and a fish fashioned out of gold, one should set them upon the vessel for the stream and establish the flow of water joined with a golden nozzle.
At the time of the sacrifice, having caused the Brahmins to recite the root mantra of Rūpiṇa consisting of ten syllables,
the principal mantra, the three names, the Gāyatrī, the Umā-mantra, the Śrīsūkta, the Pavamāna, the Puruṣasūkta, the Tryambaka,
and other such mantras; and furthermore, the Śrīrudra—
Having caused [the practitioner] to recite the Camaka, the Viṣṇusūkta, the two Śāntis, and other such mantras until the end of the two ghaṭikās and the completion of the continuous stream of water,
then... [he offers] Aśoka, Paṅkaja, Nandyāvarta,
Palāśa, Droṇa, Punnāga, Mallikā, Kalhāra, Raktapadma, Utpala, Damana, Śvetārka, Śvetamandāraka, Karavīra—

Having filled [the vessel] up to the base of the pedestal with loose flowers using the root-mantra, having covered the base of the liṅga and the pedestal with a new cloth while reciting the armor-mantra (*kavaca-mantra*), and having gratified [the deity] with offerings of incense, lamps, and food,
[one should proceed] to that aforementioned pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having performed the rites from the establishment of the fire (*ādhāna*) up to the marriage according to the procedure prescribed for the fire-ritual (*agnikārya*), one should invoke Śiva— qualified by His powers (*śakti*)— into the center of the fire, beginning with Śakti and ending with the final power, as if they were Vāmā and the other [energies]. Having worshipped Him with offerings up to the final oblation (*nivedya*), one should [offer] fifty times each, in sequence, with fuel-sticks of *khadira*, *palāśa*, *vaṭa*, *bilva*, *apāmārga*, *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, and *plakṣa*.
Having offered:

clarified butter with the *samidh-ādyamantra*, ghee with the *mūla-mantra*, the *caru* with the *aghora-mantra*, parched grain (*lāja*) with the *tatpuruṣa-mantra*, mung beans (*mudga*) with the *hṛdaya-mantra*, black gram (*māṣa*) with the *śiras-mantra*, and barley (*yava*) with the *netra-mantra*;
[and] with the *vāma-mantra*.

One should offer sesame with the Īśāna mantra; rice with the Astra mantra; wheat with the Śikhā mantra; wild grain (*nīvāra*) with the Varma mantra; *saktuka* with the Pāśupata mantra; white mustard seeds with the *bījamukhya* mantras; ghee with the ten-syllable mantra; milk with the Śiva-Astra mantras; mineral essence with the Vyoman mantra; and coconut with the Netra mantra. In this manner, fifty oblations should be offered for each substance.

Having offered [the oblation], having filled [the vessel] with the dripping residue (*sampāta*), and having placed it upon the top of the *liṅga*, one should— during the time of offering the clarified butter (*ghṛta*)— recite the *Śrīsūkta*, the *Pavamāna*, the *Narasūkta*, the *Tryambaka*,
and the *Skandasūkta* according to the established procedure; then [one recites] the *Gaurī-mantra*.

Having caused the recitation of the Viṣṇusūkta, the Śāntimantra, the Navadurgā, the Umāsūkta, and the Dhāmadakṣiṇa on the south; [and] the Varuṇasūkta, the Devavrata, the Śivakavaca, the Śivasankalpa, and the Kalpasūtra on the west; [and] the Hiraṇyavarṇa on the west; having caused the recitation of the Jyeṣṭhasāman, the Virūpākṣa, the Kayānaśca, the Namaka, and the Camaka on the north—
The *sviṣṭakṛt* offering up to the dismissal of the fire;

the fruit of the muttered recitation (*japa*) and the oblation (*homa*); having offered it to the Deity; having placed the ashes upon the seat; having taken up the substances such as oil and so forth; preceded by the chanting of the Vedas; having deposited them upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) in front of Śiva; the placement of the mantras (*mantranyāsa*).

Having performed the deposition of the thirty-eight phonemes of the Mātṛkā, and having consecrated the top of the *liṅga* with the substances from the center to the northeast using the Pāśupata and Aghorāstra mantras; having rubbed it [with unguents], covered it with the Astra mantra, adorned it with garlands of fragrant flowers, offered fruits and other items as food-offering (*naivedya*) with the root mantra, and presented the waving of lights (*ārātrika*), for the purpose of the application of the Mātṛkā-deposition and so forth—

Having obtained permission, one should pray for what is desired; this is the purification of the *liṅga* as taught in the *Kāmika* and other Āgamas. (The procedure for smearing with the five fragrances.)

Then, the preceptor, having risen at dawn and completed his daily obligatory rites beginning with the morning twilight prayer (*prātaḥ-sandhyā*) and ending with the domestic fire ritual (*aupāsana*), enters the sacrificial pavilion (*yāga-maṇḍapa*). Having performed the worship of the deities of the pavilion, beginning with the Sun and ending with the Guru; having offered the seat (*āsana*) to the goddesses beginning with Śakti and ending with Śakti; and having fully worshipped [the deity] from the Vidyā-deha up to the recitation of mantras (*japa*), he performs the fire-ritual (*agnikārya*) up to the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
Having performed the adornment together with the image-worshippers,

and having completed the rites up to the daily festival of offering, he approaches the vicinity of the primary liṅga; then, having removed the flowers and other offerings worshipped during the previous night,
he bathes the primary liṅga with pure water.
Having offered a fine upper garment, and having sprinkled this fivefold fragrance— consisting of sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, saffron, and uśīra— with cold water,

one should perform an anointing with the root mantra over the primary *liṅga*, starting from the pedestal up to the top of the *liṅga* to the depth of a bean; then, having adorned it with garlands of flowers, offered incense and lamps, and presented the food offering (*naivedya*) and the *ārātrika* ceremony.
One should offer a prayer for blessings. Thus ends the procedure for the application of the five fragrances according to the Kāmikāgama.
Now follows the procedure for the placement of the *mātṛkā* syllables (*mātṛkānyāsa*).

Then, prior to the consecration by the water-pot (*kumbhābhiṣeka*) and other rites, the preceptor, having arrived at the vicinity of the primary *liṅga* in the evening on the night before the sacrifice, fire-offering, and festival, shall sit upon the tortoise-seat (*kūrmāsana*) facing north. Having gathered the materials for worship:

Having adorned [the site] with various triangular, pentagonal, trident-shaped, and arch-shaped ornaments, as well as lamps and other offerings; having decorated oneself with the five-limbed ornaments such as the *uṣṇīṣa*; having performed the ritual of complete identification (*sakalīkṛtya*); having prepared the general water-offering (*sāmānyārghya*);
and having worshipped Vighneśvara, [one should proceed] preceded by the ritual of striking the head.

Having prayed to Vighneśvara, having prostrated before the Guru, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), and having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the hands and limbs, the formal resolve (saṅkalpa) is as follows: On this auspicious lunar day, [I perform this rite] for this God of gods,
together with his mother Śrī Kāntimatī, accompanied by the venerable Mūla-liṅga,
including the entire retinue from Saura up to Caṇḍa, for the sake of the venerable Veṇuvaneśvara Sadāśiva, according to the method prescribed in the Kāmika Āgama.

In this Śiva-sacrifice, which consists of the restoration of the ancient [shrine] and the eightfold binding (aṣṭabandhana), performed today for the sake of the presence of the Liṅga here, for the attainment of the state of *tanu*, and for the full realization of the fruit of the rites performed, preceded by the protection of our own devotees and others— [Fragmentary text continues: (l5) ... [protection of our own devotees and others...]

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "For the sake of attaining the grace of Sāmbaśiva, I shall perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the venerable Veṇuvaneśvara with the *mātṛkā* and other mantras," and having touched water, having performed the rites from the purification of the self (*ātmaśuddhi*) up to the purification of the mantras (*mantraśuddhi*) as prescribed in the daily ritual (*nitya*), and having prayed, "I worship the venerable Veṇuvaneśvara," and having received permission, one should worship Śiva [beginning] with the Support Power (*ādhāraśakti*).
Homage! Homage to the bulbous root (*kanda*). Homage to the sprout (*aṅkura*). Homage to the stalk (*nāla*).
(L7) Homage to the bud (*mukula*). To the east and so forth: homage to Ananta; homage to Vāsuki; homage to Takṣaka; homage to Abjaka; homage to Mahābjaka.
Homage to Śaṅkhapāla! Homage to Kārkoṭaka! Homage to Gulika!
In the center—to the one with the radiance of ten million suns, circular in form, seated upon Ananta: *Laṃ*, homage!
Above that, in the corners beginning with the southeast—to Dharmapāla: *Jñaṃ*, homage!
Homage to the foot of power. Homage to the foot of detachment. Homage to the foot of sovereignty.

(c1, l4) In the directions beginning with the east—homage to the foot of non-dharma. Homage to the foot of ignorance. (c1, l5) Homage to the foot of non-detachment. Homage to the foot of non-sovereignty. (c1, l6)

In the center: *Oṃ saṃ* salva-guṇa-cchadanāya namaḥ | *Raṃ* rāja(guṇa)-cchadanāya namaḥ | *Taṃ* tāmasa-guṇa-cchadanāya namaḥ | Homage to the one with a mouth formidable with fangs! Homage to the three-eyed one!
Homage to the one whose form is like snow, who has a retinue of lions, who is white in color, whose shape is square, and who dwells in the great forest!
Salutation to the lion-throne.
Above it—in the corners starting from the southeast (āgneya)—salutation to the one whose form is the elements (bhūtarūpa), who is the foot of the Kṛta Yuga;
salutation to the one whose form is the elements, who is the foot of the Tretā Yuga; salutation to the one whose form is the elements, who is the foot of the Dvāpara Yuga.
Homage to the one whose form is the elements, the foot of the Kali age.
In the east and the other directions: homage to the one whose form is the elements, the vessel of the unmanifest.

Homage to the one whose form is the elements, the foot of necessity. Homage to the one whose form is the elements, the foot of time. Homage to the one whose form is the elements, the foot of the creative arts.

In the center—*Oṃ Keśavāya madhyapādāya pītavarṇāya aṣṭakoṇāya raṃ yogāsanāya namaḥ*. Above that—*Namaḥ to the coral-colored seeds; namaḥ to the silver-colored sprout; namaḥ to the lapis lazuli-colored [element]*.
Homage to the pericarp, which has blood-red petals.
Homage to the eight petals, which are conch-white in color. Homage to the secondary petals, which are red in color.
Homage to the red-colored filaments.
(c1, l5) In the center of the pericarp: Oṃ namaḥ. Āṃ namaḥ.
Raṃ namaḥ. Auṃ namaḥ. Vyoṃ namaḥ. Maṃ namaḥ. (c1, l7)
Vyāṃ, obeisance! Piṃ, obeisance! Neṃ, obeisance! Oṃ, obeisance!
At the tips of the filaments:
Vyomāyai, obeisance! Jyeṣṭhāyai, obeisance! Raudryai, obeisance! Kālyai, obeisance! Kalavikaraṇyai, obeisance! Balavikaraṇyai, obeisance!
Salutation to Balapramathanī; salutation to Sarvabhūtadamanī.
(c3) Salutation to Manonmanī. In the middle of the petals: salutation to Ananteśa; salutation to Sūkṣmeśa; salutation to Śivottama; salutation to Ekanetra; salutation to Ekarudra.
Salutation to Trimūrti. (c4) Salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha. Salutation to Śikhaṇḍin.
In the pericarp, to the south—salutation to Ātmatattva. Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to Vidyātattva. (c5)

In the center: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva. Obeisance to that lotus-seat which is the great knot of the Māyā-tattva, joined with the petals of the Vidyeśvaras, endowed with the filaments and the powers beginning with Vāmā, possessing a pericarp consisting of the Vidyā-tattva, circular in shape, white in color, marked with the letter E, and [serving as] the seat of the Lord.

Above that: *namaḥ sūryamaṇḍalāya* | *namaḥ sūryamaṇḍalādhipataye brahmaṇe* | (l2) *namaḥ somamaṇḍalāya* | *namaḥ somamaṇḍalādhipataye viṣṇave* | *namaḥ agnimaṇḍalāya* | *namaḥ agnimaṇḍalādhipataye rudrāya* | *namaḥ śaktimaṇḍalāya* | *namaḥ śaktimaṇḍalādhipataye* | (l3)

Salutation to Śiva! Salutation to the one whose form is an octagon, who is white in color, who is endowed with the destruction of the maṇḍala, who is the letter *ha*, and who possesses a stainless seat. Salutation to the embodiment of Śiva! Having formed the *āvāhana* (invocation) mudrā with flowers, having led [the deity] from the heart to the space between the eyebrows, and having visualized her in the form of light within the joined palms: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ*.

"Salutation to the form of Śiva. Having thus assigned the form, [one assigns the mantras]: "Naṃ, salutation to the head; salutation to the Supreme, whose essence is the Śiva-principle. "Uṃ, salutation to the mouth; salutation to the Supreme, whose essence is the Vidyā-principle. "Aṃ, salutation to the heart; salutation to the Supreme, whose essence is the Ātman-principle. Having thus assigned the three principles.
Now, the placement of the five principles (pañcatattvanyāsa):
on the head—Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the self of the Śāntyatīta-kalā;
in the mouth—Oṃ hyaiṃ, obeisance to the self of the Śānti-kalā.
In the heart: Oṃ hraṃ, salutation to the self of the Vidyā-kalā. In the navel: Oṃ hvīṃ, salutation to the self of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā.
At the knees: "Oṃ hlāṃ, obeisance to the self of the Nivṛtti-kalā"—having thus performed the placement of the five principles (pañcatattva).
The placement of the staff-row (daṇḍapaṅktinyāsa):
at the head— "Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to the self of the Īśāna-head."
In the mouth: Oṃ Heṃ, obeisance to the self that is the face of Tatpuruṣa.
In the heart: Oṃ Huṃ, obeisance to the self that is the heart of Aghora.
At the navel: *Oṃ hiṃ*, salutation to the secret self of Vāmadeva;

at the feet: salutation to the foot-self of Sadyojāta. Having thus performed the placement for the "breaking of the staff" (*daṇḍabhaṅgi*), one then performs the "breaking of the skull" (*muṇḍabhaṅgi*).
(The Gesture of the Shaven Head)— Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, the self of the upward-facing mouth.
Oṃ huṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, the self of the eastern-facing mouth.
Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Aghora, the essence of the southern face. Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva, the essence of the northern face.
In the west—Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta, the essence of the western face. Having thus performed the placement of the arrangement of the heads.
(The Mātṛkānyāsa) — Now one should perform the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

For the mantra of Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), and Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā). The consonants are the seeds (bījāni), and the vowels are [the power].
The powers of Śakti; the individual manifestations.

(L5) The *kīlakas* of the Lord of the Forest of Reeds (*Veṇuvaneśvara*). The application (*viniyoga*) for the placement of the *mātṛkās*: *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅam*. *Āṃ*, salutation to the two thumbs. *ḻaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ*, salutation to the two index fingers. *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ* (L6).

Ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ (ṇaṃ? to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*. Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*. Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ (ḻaṃ) kṣaṃ haḥ to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. In this manner, there should be the placement (*nyāsa*) on the heart and other limbs. One should meditate upon the body with its face, feet, belly, and chest fashioned from the distinctions of the fifty letters.
She who wears the crescent moon in her matted hair, who is as white as the moon or jasmine,
whose hands hold a rosary, a water-pot, and a cintāmaṇi, who has three eyes, who stands upon a lotus, and who belongs to the Maccha-kalpa.
I bow to that Bhāratī, who bears the burden of breasts and hips that cause her distress.
The deities should be placed upon the forehead, the face, the circular eyes, the ears, the nostrils, the two cheeks,
the two lips, the two teeth, and the tongue.
On the arms, feet, tips of the fingers, sides, back, and the region from the navel to the collarbone, one should respectively apply the letters ending in 'a'.
On the chest, shoulders, hump, and flanks, one should apply the elements (dhātus) in order.
On the two thighs, shanks, belly, and mouth, one should likewise apply the elements in sequence.
Aṃ namaḥ | Āṃ namaḥ | Iṃ namaḥ | Īṃ namaḥ | Uṃ namaḥ | Ūṃ namaḥ | Ḷṃ namaḥ | Ṛṃ namaḥ | Ṝṃ namaḥ | Ḹṃ namaḥ | ḹṃ namaḥ | (c1) Eṃ namaḥ | Aiṃ namaḥ | Oṃ namaḥ | Auṃ namaḥ | (c2)
Aṃ namaḥ | Āṃ namaḥ | Kaṃ namaḥ | Khaṃ namaḥ | Gaṃ namaḥ | Ghaṃ namaḥ | Ṅaṃ namaḥ | Caṃ namaḥ | Chaṃ namaḥ | Jaṃ namaḥ | Jhaṃ namaḥ | Jhaṃ namaḥ (repeated).
ñaṃ namaḥ | ṭaṃ namaḥ | ṭhaṃ namaḥ | ḍaṃ namaḥ | ḍhaṃ namaḥ | ṇaṃ namaḥ | taṃ namaḥ | thaṃ namaḥ | daṃ namaḥ | dhaṃ namaḥ | naṃ namaḥ | paṃ namaḥ | phaṃ namaḥ |

Baṃ namaḥ | Bhaṃ namaḥ | Maṃ namaḥ | Yaṃ namaḥ | Raṃ namaḥ | Laṃ namaḥ | Vaṃ namaḥ | Śaṃ namaḥ | Ṣaṃ namaḥ | Saṃ namaḥ | Haṃ namaḥ | Laṃ namaḥ | Kṣaṃ namaḥ. Having thus performed the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Having worshipped [the deity] from the water-vessel to the water-vessel with the five offerings (*pañcopacāra*),

having offered the oblation (*nivedya*) with the root mantra (*mūla*) and presented the *ārātrika* lamp, one should pray to the Blessed One (*bhagavant*). This same procedure is to be applied in all cases where the ritual placements (*nyāsa*) are being performed.

Now, the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā-nyāsa: for the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā-mantra, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Jagatī is the meter (chandas), Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (devatā), *haṃ sām aṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*),
*haṃ sīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *haṃ sūṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*) of the venerable Veṇuvaneśvara.

By the grace of Ardhanārīśvara, this is the application (*viniyoga*) for the *Śrīkaṇṭha-nyāsa* in order to bring about the presence of the Liṅga: *Haṃ sāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. *Haṃ sīṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*.
*Haṃ sūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*.
*Haṃ saiṃ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*. *Haṃ sauṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*. *Haṃ saḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. Thus.
The placement on the heart and other limbs (*hṛdayādinyāsa*). Meditation (*dhyāna*):
[He is] resembling the bandhūka flower and gold, seated upon a beautiful throne, holding in his own staff-like arms a garland, an eye, a noose, a goad, and the gesture of granting boons.
I perpetually take refuge in that body which bears the crescent moon as an ornament, possesses three eyes, and has half of Ambikā as its abode.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ, obeisance to Śrīkaṇṭha and Pūrṇodarī, and obeisance to Śiva and Abhayā. Thus, at the hairline.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ, obeisance to Ananta and Virajā, and obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the forehead.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ iṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣma and Śallīśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the right eye. (c2, l1) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ īṃ, obeisance to Mūrti and Lolākṣiśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the left eye. (c2, l2) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ uṃ, obeisance to Amareśvara and Vakulākṣiśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the right ear. (c2, l3)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ūṃ apaḍiśalīyasi ghoṇaśaktibhyāṃ namaśśivābhyāṃ namaḥ. Thus, on the left ear.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ bhāramiti [bhāraśaktibhyāṃ] mukhīśaktibhyāṃ namaśśivābhyāṃ namaḥ. Thus, on the right nostril.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ, obeisance to Nidhīśa and his Śakti Komukhī; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the left nostril. (c1, l3) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ, obeisance to Sthāṇu and his Śakti Dīrghajihvā; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the right cheek. (c1, l4) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ḹṃ, obeisance to Hara and his Śakti Kuṇḍodarī; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the left cheek. (c1, l5)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ eṃ jhaṇḍī ca ūrdhvakeśiśaktibhyāṃ namaśśivābhyāṃ namaḥ | Thus, on the upper lip. (c1, l6.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ bhautikavikṛtamukhiśaktiśaktibhyāṃ namaśśivābhyāṃ namaḥ | Thus, on the lower lip. (c1, l7.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ sadyojātajvālāmukhiśaktibhyāṃ namaśśivābhyāṃ namaḥ | Thus, on the upper row of teeth. (c2, l1.)

*Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ auṃ*, obeisance to Anugraheśa and Śulkāmukhī-Śakti; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the lower lip and mouth. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ*, obeisance to Akūra and Śrīmukhī-Śakti; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the head. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aḥ*, obeisance to Mahāsena and Vidyāmukhī-Śakti; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the face.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kaṃ, obeisance to Krodheśa and Mahākālī-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the base of the right arm. (c2, l5) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khaṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍeśa and Sarasvatī-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the right elbow. (c2, l6) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ, obeisance to Pañcāntaka and Siddhi-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the right wrist. (c2, l7)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ghaṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, to Śivottama and the Vidyā-Śakti of the three worlds; thus on the palm of the right hand.

(p190a, c1, l1) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, to Ekarudra and the Mantra-Śakti; thus on the tip of the right hand. (c1, l2) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ caṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, to Kūrmarūpa and the Ātman-Śakti; thus at the base of the left arm. (c1, l3)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ chaṃ, obeisance to Ekanetra and his Śakti Vibhūti; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the left elbow.
(c1, l4) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jaṃ, obeisance to Caturmukha and his Śakti Lambodarī; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the left wrist.
(c1, l5) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jhaṃ, obeisance to Aja and his Śakti Bhrāmaṇī; obeisance to the auspicious couple. Thus, on the palm of the left hand. (c1, l6)

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ, obeisance to Candrarūpa and Gatakāri-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the tip of the left hand. (c1, l7) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ, obeisance to Someśaka and Ecarī-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the root of the right thigh. (c2, l1) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Lāṅgali and Majjarī-śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the right knee. (c2, l2)

OṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ ḌAṂ! Salutation to the two Śivas and Śivās, Dārukarūpiṇī and Śakti; thus on the tip of the right calf. (c2, l3) OṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ ḌHAṂ! Salutation to the two Śivas and Śivās, Ardhanārīśvara and Vikaraṇī-Śakti; thus on the sole of the right foot. (c2, l4) OṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ ṆAṂ! Salutation to the two Śivas and Śivās, Umākānta and Kāmodarī-Śakti; thus on the tip of the sole of the right foot. (c2, l5)

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ taṃ, obeisance to Āṣāḍhīśa and Bhūtanāśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the root of the left thigh. (c2, l6) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Ḍiḍabhadraka and Kālīśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the left knee. (c2, l7) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ daṃ, obeisance to Atri and Gomatiśakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the tip of the left shank. (p190b, c1, l1)

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ ... [to] Śāna and Śaṅkhinī-Śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus on the sole of the left foot. (c1, l2) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ naṃ [to] Meṣa and Garjanī-Śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus on the tip of the left foot. (c1, l3) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ paṃ [to] Lohita and Kālarātri-Śakti, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus on the right side. (c1, l4)

Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ phaṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkhinī and Kubjanī, and to their two Śaktis; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the left side. (c1, l5) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ baṃ, obeisance to Cakalaṇḍaka and Pardanī, and to their two Śaktis; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, on the back portion. (c1, l6) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ bhaṃ, obeisance to Dviraṇḍa and Vajranī, and to their two Śaktis; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, at the navel. (c1, l7)

Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ maṃ, salutations to Mahākāla and Jayāśakti, salutations to Śiva and Śivā; thus at the heart. (c2, l1) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ yaṃ, salutations to Kapālin and Sumukheśvarīśakti, salutations to Śiva and Śivā; thus in the skin. (c2, l2) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ raṃ, salutations to Bhujaṅga and Revatīśakti, salutations to Śiva and Śivā; thus in the blood. (c2, l3)
Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ laṃ, salutation to Pinākin and Mādhavī-śakti; salutation to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, in the flesh.
(c2, l4) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ vaṃ, salutation to Khaḍgīśa and Vāruṇī-śakti; salutation to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, in the fat.
(c2, l5) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ śaṃ, salutation to Bakavāyi and Śakti; salutation to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, in the bone. (c2, l6)
Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, [namely] to Śvetarakṣa and Upasaraṇiśakti; thus, in the marrow.

(c2, l7) Oṃ hāṃ śrīṃ saṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, [namely] to Mṛga and Sahajāśakti; thus, in the semen. (p191a, c1, l1) Oṃ hāṃ haṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivā, [namely] to Lakulīśa and Lakṣmīśakti; thus, in the heart. (c1, l2)

"Oṃ hāṃ śrī laṃ, obeisance to Śiva and Śivayāpikī-śakti; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, at the base of the *liṅga*. (c1, l3) "Oṃ hāṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to Savartakeśa and Māyī-śakti; obeisance to Śiva and Śivā. Thus, as the pervasive [deity]. (c1, l4) Having thus performed the deposition (*nyāsa*) of the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā, having worshipped with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, and having offered [the oblation] with the root mantra. (c1, l5)
Having offered the *ārātrika* lamp, one should pray for blessings.
This concludes the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Śrīkaṇṭha and the Mothers.

(The Deposition of the Thirty-eight Kalās) — Now, for the mantra of the deposition of the thirty-eight kalās: Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva, and Sadyojāta are the seers (ṛṣis). Gāyatrī, Uṣṇik, and Anuṣṭubh are the meters (chandāṃsi). Bhūr, Īśvara, and Āpaḥ... [are the deities].

The deities are [the following]. *Oṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*). *Hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*). *Oṃ saḥ* for Śiva is the pin (*kīlaka*). The application (*viniyoga*) is in the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the thirty-eight digits (*kalā*). *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the two thumbs (*aṅguṣṭha*) for the All-knowing One (*sarvajñā*).
*Oṃ hrīṃ*, salutation to the two index fingers (*tarjanī*) for the one garlanded with the splendor of nectar (*amṛtatejomālinī*) and the eternally satisfied one (*nityatṛptā*).
Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to the two middle fingers, who possess the blazing crest and primordial awakening.
Oṃ haiṃ, homage to the two ring fingers, who are the wielder of the vajra, the supreme vajra, and the excellent protector.
Oṃ sauṃ, homage to the two little fingers, who are the abode of the power of the unstained.

Oṃ paśu huṃ phaṭ; salutation to both the palms and the backs of the hands. (c1, l3) The assignment of the heart and other limbs (*hṛdayādinyāsa*) is as follows: *eeṃ* (or *vaṃ*). The visualization (*dhyāna*):
The Great Lord (*maheśa*), being most gracious, holds in his arms a staff, an axe, a deer, and the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons. (c1, l4–l5)

Blazing with all ornaments, lotus-eyed, and clad in a tiger-skin garment; he should be meditated upon as having five faces, three eyes, and a lofty crown, with the radiance of his entire body shimmering with the white pollen of pearls,
while the tips of his crests are adorned with the cool-rayed moon.

Then the five faces on the head, the heart, the throat, the two shoulders, the belly, the back, the thighs, the anus, the genitals, the two thighs, as well as the pair of knees, the two shanks, the two buttocks,
the waist, the two sides, the feet, the hands, the nose, and the crown of the head— these they call [the locations].
These are the locations for the thirty-eight kalās known as the "triads" within the body of Śiva.

The kalās of Īśāna are five; those of Puruṣa are four; the kalās of Aghora are eight; those of Vāmadeva are thirteen; and the kalās of Sadyojāta are eight. Thus, thirty-eight kalās are traditionally taught. Oṃ Hoṃ! Salutation to Śaśinī, who is Īśāna of all vidyās.

Thus, on the upper head: *Īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānām*, salutation to Aṅgadā; on the eastern head. *Oṃ hoṃ brahmādhipatir brahmaṇo'dhipatir brahmā iṣṭadāyai namaḥ*; on the southern head. *Oṃ hoṃ śivo me astu*, salutation to Marīci; on the northern head.
Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to Sadāśivā Jvālinī on the western head.
Thus ends the pentad of the Īśāna-kalās.
Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to the kalā of Śāntyatītā, whose form is unmanifest.
In the upward-facing mouth:
Oṃ Hoṃ, we know the Tatpuruṣa;
salutation to Śānti. In the eastern-facing mouth.
Oṃ hoṃ, we meditate upon Mahādeva; homage to Vidyā. [This is] on the right face.
Oṃ hoṃ.
"To him, Rudra, for stability, obeisance!"—on the northern face. (c1, l8) "Oṃ Hoṃ, may he impel; obeisance to Nivṛtti"—(c2, l1) on the western face. Thus are the four kalās of Tatpuruṣa.
Oṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to Aghorā and Tamā; at the heart. Now, obeisance to Ghorā and Mohā; at the throat.

Oṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to Ghorakṣamā—on the right shoulder. Thus ends the eightfold Aghora-kalā. Oṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to Niṣṭhā from the most terrible ones—on the left shoulder. Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva.
Oṃ *huṃ*, obeisance to Rājāyī at the secret place; Oṃ *huṃ*, obeisance to Sarvamṛtyu on all sides—at the navel;
Oṃ *huṃ*, obeisance to Māyā of all—at the belly.
Oṃ hūṃ, homage to you, Bhayā; homage to her—on the back. (c2, l7) Oṃ hūṃ, homage to those of Rudra-form, Jarā; homage to her—on the chest.
(c3, l5) Oṃ hiṃ, homage to Jyeṣṭhā; [homage] to Rakṣā. (c3, l6)
*Namaḥ* at the *liṅga*.
*Oṃ hiṃ rudrāya namaḥ*—at the right thigh.
*Ratyai namaḥ*—at the left thigh.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Kālakarṣiṇī—obeisance to Pālī—at the left thigh.

Thus ends the eightfold division of Sadyojāta. (c3, l5.
Complete with the limbs mentioned above the Kalās, supporting that which is superior to the Bhuvanādhvan;
endowed with the skins mentioned in the Varṇādhvan, it is joined with the radiant Mantrādhvan. (c3, l6–l7.)
The path of words consists of the channels, flesh, semen, marrow, bones,
and skin; its vital breath is traditionally held to be Śiva, whose nature is the sixfold path of Sadāśiva.
Complete with the sacrificial offerings of the heart and other centers, he assumes a form endowed with all parts during meditation;
yet, because his true nature is partless, he is therefore both "with parts" and "partless" (sakalaniṣkala).

Having determined with the mind that the kalās extend sequentially from the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) to the forehead, from there to the neck, from there to the navel, to the knees, and finally to the feet, one should worship them with their respective mantras. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) consisting of thirty-eight [parts], one should worship [the deity] with the five offerings (*pañcopacāra*), beginning with water and ending with water.

(l4) Having worshipped [the deity] with perfumes and other offerings, having honored [them], offered incense and lamps, and presented the food offering (*nivedya*), one should pray for a blessing. This concludes the placement of the thirty-eight *kalās*. Now follows the placement of the *pīṭha* (*pīṭhanyāsa*). (c1.)

(Oṃ) Khaṃ, obeisance to Śambara-mūrti and Bālā. (Oṃ) Ghaṃ (Gaṃ), obeisance to Rudra-mūrti and Gaurī.
(Oṃ) Ghaṃ, obeisance to Paśupati-mūrti and Ghaṇṭabharaṭhā.
(Oṃ) Ṅaṃ, homage to Ugramūrti and Sunayanā.
(Oṃ) Caṃ, homage to Mahādevamūrti and Candradharā. (C2.
Oṃ Chaṃ, homage to Bhīmakīrti and Śandomayā.
(Oṃ) Jaṃ, homage to the form of Īśāna and to Gaja.
(Oṃ) Jhaṃ, homage to the form of Tatpuruṣa and to Kriyā.
(Oṃ) Ñaṃ, homage to the form of Aghora and to Jñāna.
(Oṃ) Ṭaṃ, obeisance to the Sadyojāta form and the ṭaṅka and arrow.
(Oṃ) Ṭhaṃ, obeisance to the Vāmadeva form and the ḍhakkā drum. Oṃ Ḍaṃ, obeisance to the Brahma form and the yakṣaṇī. (c3.)
Oṃ ḍhaṃ, salutation to Prajāpati-mūrti and Rajjanī. Oṃ naṃ (ṇaṃ), likewise, salutation to those respective two forms. Oṃ laṃ, salutation to Soma-mūrti and Lakṣmī.
(Oṃ) Vaṃ, obeisance to Paramaśiva and Varjiri (Jriṇī) Śūlinī. (Oṃ) Śaṃ, obeisance to Pitāmaha-mūrti and Śaśidhāriṇī. (Oṃ) Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Vidhātṛ-mūrti and Ṣaḍādhāra-nīlī. (c4.)
(Oṃ) Saṃ, obeisance to Viriñca-mūrti and Sarvanāyikā.
(Oṃ) Haṃ, obeisance to Sṛṣṭi-mūrti and Asitānanā. (Oṃ) Laṃ, obeisance to Caturānana-mūrti and Lalitā.
*(Oṃ) Kṣaṃ, salutation to the two [deities] in the forms of the deer and the ass, and to the Earth.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of Keśava and the others with *Oṃ*, and having worshipped them from water to water, and having offered the oblation, one should pray. Following the placement of Keśava and the others, for the sake of the worship of the *ardha* [offering], [one should perform] the placement of the six paths (*ṣaḍadhvan*) according to the order of emanation.*

The threefold nature of the paths (*adhvan*) therein is as follows: namely, emanation (*sṛṣṭi*), maintenance (*sthiti*), and withdrawal (*saṃhāra*); and [the paths of] reality (*tattva*), word (*pada*), world (*bhuvana*), phoneme (*varṇa*), energy (*kalā*), and mantra (*mantra*). I shall explain them in order. Regarding reality (*tattva*), it is the locus for ritual placement (*nyāsa*): "Having placed the reality (*tattva*) in the navel and the heart, the wise one [should proceed]"—such is the statement of the *Āgama*.

Thus it has also been stated by the Teachers: "One should [place] the one possessing all limbs, the final primordial nature (*prakṛti*), preceded by the intellect (*buddhi*), together with the collection of qualities such as sound, in the center of the heart; [then] in the mouth, the secret place, and the feet. In each of the three [locations], another [set] is placed in the feet. [One should place] the aggregate of the senses, beginning with the ear and speech, together with the collection of qualities such as space (*vyoman*), in the mouth, the heart, the secret place, and the feet."

The fourfold [set] beginning with the garland and the white lotus is in the center of the heart. It is well said that the five principles (*pañcatattva*) reside in the five locations [of the face]. In the five faces: *namaḥ saṃjñānaśaktyātmane* (salutation to the self whose nature is the power of consciousness);
*namaḥ sukriyāśaktyātmane* (salutation to the self whose nature is the power of auspicious action).

(L5) *haṃ namaśśivāya sadāśivātmane namaḥ* (haṃ, salutation to Śiva; salutation to the self whose nature is Sadāśiva); *kṣaṃ namaśśivāya śaktyātmane namaḥ* (kṣaṃ, salutation to Śiva; salutation to the self whose nature is Śakti); *ḷaṃ namaśśivāya maheśvarātmane namaḥ* (ḷaṃ, salutation to Śiva; salutation to the self whose nature is Maheśvara).

Yaṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is Īśvara. Saṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is the principle of Pure Knowledge (*śuddhavidyātattva*). Ṣaṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is Māyā. Śaṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is Time (*kāla*). Vaṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is Kalā. Laṃ: obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the Self that is Vidyā. Raṃ: obeisance to Śiva.

Salutation to Śiva whose nature is necessity; salutation to Śiva whose nature is passion; salutation to Śiva whose nature is the Puruṣa; salutation to Śiva whose nature is primordial matter (prakṛti). Thus, the principle of Śiva and the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva), pervading the entire body down to the level of primordial matter, [are established].
In the heart: *Baṃ namaśśivāya*, salutation to the self of intellect;
*Phaṃ namaśśivāya*, salutation to the self of ego;
*Paṃ namaśśivāya*, salutation to the self of mind. Thus in the heart.
On the head: *naṃ* obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the essence of sound (*śabdatanmātra*). On the mouth: *oṃ dhaṃ* obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the essence of touch (*sparśātman*).
In the heart: *śiṃ daṃ namaśśivāya rūpātmane namaḥ* | In the secret place: *vaṃ thaṃ namaśśivāya rasātmane namaḥ* | In the feet: *yaṃ taṃ namaśśivāya* || 3 ||
Salutation to the self of fragrance.
Regarding "each its own":
salutation to Śiva through the ear; salutation to the self of the principle of the ear.
On the skin—Ḍaṃ (Ḍhaṃ), obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the self that is the skin. In the eyes—Ṣa Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the self that is the eye.
On the tongue: *ṭhaṃ*—salutation to Śiva, salutation to the self of the tongue. In the nose: *ṭaṃ*—salutation to Śiva, salutation to the self of the sense of smell.
In the mouth: *ñaṃ*—salutation to Śiva, salutation to the self of speech.
In the hands: *jhaṃ* obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the self of the hands. In the feet: *jaṃ* obeisance to Śiva; obeisance to the self of the feet.
At the anus: *caṃ*—obeisance to Śiva, obeisance to the self in the form of the anus. At the generative organ: *chaṃ*—obeisance to Śiva, obeisance to the self in the form of the generative organ.

At the head—*ṅaṃ*, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance to the one whose self is space (*vyomātman*). In the mouth—*ghaṃ*, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance to the one whose self is air (*vāyvātman*). In the heart—*gaṃ śiṃ*, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance to the one whose self is fire (*tejasātman*).
In the secret place: *khaṃ eṃ* *namaśśivāya*, [and] *abātmane namaḥ*.
In the two feet: *kaṃ yaṃ* *namaśśivāya*, [and] *pṛthvyātmane namaḥ*.
In the four heart-lotuses: *raṃ* to the fire-maṇḍala, obeisance; to the self of the [sixteen] kalās that bestow dharma, obeisance;
*haṃ* to the sun-maṇḍala, to the self of the twelve kalās that bestow wealth (*arthaprada*), obeisance.
Saṃ, obeisance to the moon-maṇḍala, the soul of the sixteen digits that bestows all desires;
śaṃ, obeisance to Śiva, the soul of the heart-lotus;
at the head—Oṃ Heṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Śiva. (l2)
Salutation to the head of Īśāna, whose essence is the Śāntyatīta-kalā.
To the face—Oṃ haṃ hvyaiṃ, salutation to Śiva, whose essence is the Śānti-kalā; salutation to the face of Tatpuruṣa.
To the heart—Oṃ huṃ hrūṃ, salutation to Śiva, whose essence is the Vidyā-kalā. (L3)
Salutation to the Aghora-heart.

At the secret place: *Oṃ hiṃ hvīṃ namaśśivāya*, salutation to the Vāmadeva-secret, whose essence is the *Pratiṣṭhā* kalā. At the feet: *Oṃ haṃ namaḥ*, salutation to the Nivṛtti-kalā-essence, *namaśśivāya*.
Salutation to the two feet of Sadyojāta.
The hymn for the five faces—
for the upward face:
"Īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām"—this is Śiva; he should offer [the oblation] at the eastern face with "Tatpuruṣāya... (L5).
In the southern face:
"To those of non-terrible form.
In the northern face:
To the left, [one offers] to Ugrīna with "Salutation" (namas).
At the western face—
to Sadyojāta, [with] "to Bhava" (bhavāya).

After the placement of the principles (*tattva-nyāsa*), one should perform the placement of the parts (*pada-nyāsa*). [One should place them] in the directions starting from the east: on the forehead, chin, eyes, nose, cheeks, mouth, and the two ears;
on the two feet, the hands, the joints, and the tips of the fingers; and on the left [side].

Is there a fault in transgressing [the sequence] in the ears, shoulders, sides, and hips? ... In the feet... one should place [the syllables] in the other [limbs], in the seat of sacrifice (*yajipada*), in the sky-born (*vyomāṇuja*).
Above, on the head: *oṃ āṃ raṃ ūṃ oṃ namaḥ*.
On the eastern head: *namaḥ vyomavyāpine*. On the southern head: *namaḥ vyomarūpāya*.
On the northern head: *oṃ namaḥ sarvavyāpine*.
On the back of the head—salutation to Śiva.
On the forehead—salutation to Ananta. (L2) On the chin—Oṃ, salutation to Anātha.
To the right eye—homage to Anāśrita. To the left eye—homage to Dhruva. To the right ear—Oṃ, homage to Śāśvata.
In the left ear: *Oṃ yogapīṭhasaṃsthitāya namaḥ*. (L3) In the right skull: *Oṃ nityayogine namaḥ*.
In the left skull: *Oṃ dhyānāhārāya namaḥ*.
In the mouth—*oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*.
In the head—*(oṃ) sarvaprabhave namaḥ*.
On the crown—*īśānamūrdhne namaḥ*. (L4.)
In the mouth—(Oṃ) salutation to the face of Tatpuruṣa;
in the heart—Oṃ, salutation to the heart of Aghora;
at the navel—(Oṃ) salutation to the secret part of Vāmadeva.
At the two feet: *Oṃ sadyojātapādābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
At the right hand—in the five joints:
Oṃ, salutations, salutations! Oṃ, salutations to the one who is more secret than the secret! Oṃ, salutations to the protector!
Oṃ, salutation to Anidhana.
(Oṃ), salutation to Nidhana.
[From the right thumb to the little finger—]
Oṃ, homage to the Lord of all yogas!
Oṃ, homage to the one whose form is light!
Oṃ, homage to the Supreme Lord!
Oṃ, salutation to the insentient.
(Oṃ) Salutation to Vyomin.
In the joints of the left hand—
Oṃ, obeisance to the Formless One. Oṃ, obeisance to the Broad One. Oṃ, obeisance to the Radiant One. (L7.)
Oṃ jyotiḥ, obeisance! Oṃ arūpāya, obeisance!
[Recite] from the left thumb to the little finger—
(Oṃ) Homage to the fireless! Oṃ, homage to the smokeless!
Oṃ, homage to the ashless!
(Oṃ) Homage to Anādi.
Oṃ Nānā Nara, homage!
At the joints of the right foot—(p197a, l1).
Oṃ yū yū yū namaḥ | Oṃ bhū namaḥ | Oṃ bhūva namaḥ |
Oṃ suva namaḥ | Oṃ anidhanāya namaḥ | [From the right big toe to the little toe— ]
Oṃ, salutation to Nidhana.
Oṃ, salutation to Nidhanodbhava.
Oṃ, salutation to Śiva.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śarva. (l2.
Oṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Self. In the joints of the left foot—
Oṃ, salutation to Maheśvara.
Oṃ, salutation to Mahādeva. Oṃ, salutation to Sadbhāveśvara.
Oṃ, homage to the one of great splendor!
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Lord of Yoga! (L3.
[The sequence] from the big toe of the left foot to the little toe—
Oṃ muñca mañca namaḥ | Oṃ prathamaṃ namaḥ | (Oṃ) śarvāya namaḥ |
(Oṃ) Homage to Bhava.
Oṃ, homage to Bhavodbhava. On the left side—at the left ear—Oṃ, homage to Sarvabhūtasuprada. (l4)
Homage!
On the left shoulder—homage to the one who brings about the presence of all.
On the region of the left breast—Oṃ, homage to the one who is beyond Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra.
In the region of the left abdomen— Oṃ, homage to Arcitā. In the left hip— (l5) Oṃ, homage to Astu.
On the right side—at the right ear:
Oṃ, salutation to Pūrvasthita. At the right shoulder: Oṃ, salutation to Sākṣin... [etc.]
On the region of the right breast: Oṃ kuru namaḥ.
On the region of the right thigh:
Oṃ pataṅga... namaḥ.
At the right hip: *oṃ piṅgalāya namaḥ*.
From the tip of the fingers of the right hand: *oṃ jñānāya namaḥ*.
To the tips of the fingers of the left hand: *oṃ śabdāya namaḥ*—to the tips of the fingers of the right foot. (l7)
Oṃ Sūkṣma, salutation—up to the tips of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ Śivāya, salutation—at the right thigh... [Oṃ] Śarvāya, salutation—at the left thigh. Oṃ Śarvadāya, salutation—at the nose.
Oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ—on the head.
Oṃ namo namaḥ—at the base of the right hand.
Oṃ śivāya namaḥ—at the base of the left hand; [this concludes] the eleventh word, "namo namaḥ."
After the placement of the feet, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*) with the mantra "Salutation to the Power of Will" (*icchāśaktaye namaḥ*).
[One should place it] on the head, the five [faces], the four faces, the two eyes on the forehead, the two ears, the two nostrils, the two cheeks, and also the two lips.
And on the two teeth, on the tongue, at the root of the palate,
in the throat, in the heart, in the two breasts, in the region of the navel,
on the two buttocks, in the secret place, in the anus, and again on the two seed-vessels.

One should place [the mantra] upon the base, the right hand, the joints of the fingers, and the fingers themselves; likewise on the joints, the middle of the joints, the palms, and the backs of the hands;
and also on the left arm, the joints of the fingers, the fingers, and the regions of the joints.
The wise practitioner should place [the hands] upon the middle of the soles and the backs,
at the joints of the feet and the tips of the toes, and on both the surfaces of the big toes.
One should place [the mantra] on the first joint of the left foot, as well as at its tip;
one should place it on the fingers, the palm, the back of the hand, and in the middle of the joints.
One should also place it on the two hips, the two sides, the two jaws, and the two shoulders.
In the navel, the belly, the penis, the testicles, and the two elbows;
In the two temples, the two knees, the middle and the base of the thighs, as well as at their tips, in the two shanks, and likewise in the two calves; (l7. and likewise in the two stalks.
One should install the seven [deities] from the navel to the heart;
likewise, one should place *dhṛk* and *vardhanī* in the two middle parts of the shoulders and in the two eyes.
One should also place them on the sides of the forehead, at the tip of the nose, in the middle of the bridge of the nose, and in the pair of eyebrows.
In the two armors, between the eyebrows, and especially in the pair of armpits.
One should sequentially assign the worlds from the head down to the feet.
From the head down to the foundation (*ādhāra*), and from Anāśrita up to Ekapiṅgekṣaṇa, there are thirty-seven locations.

With the joints of the arms, feet, and thighs, as well as the fingers, and including the middle, palms, and backs [of the hands and feet], there are one hundred and thirty locations from Udbhava up to Mahābala.

(14) From the waist up to the pair of armpits, and from the hands holding nooses up to Kālāgni, there are forty-nine locations. Having deposited the respective mantras in each of those locations, (15)
There are two hundred and twenty-four mantra-positions.
On the fifth head: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Unsupported (Anāśrita).
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the protectorless one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the infinite one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the one whose form is space.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyāpinī.
At the five faces— (Oṃ hāṃ), salutation to Ūrdhvagāminī.
Oṃ (hāṃ) homage to Dīpikā.
Oṃ hāṃ homage to Mocikā.
Oṃ hāṃ homage to Rocikā. (l7)
Salutation!
On the forehead: Oṃ, salutation to Bhuṇḍikā. On the right eye: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Śāntyatīta-kalā.
In the left eye: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Śāntikalā. In the right ear: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Vidyākalā.
In the left ear: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā.
In the right nostril: Oṃ (hāṃ), obeisance to the Nivṛtti-kalā. In the left nostril: (l2)
— Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva.
On the right skull: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śikhaṇḍin. On the left skull: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha.
On the upper lip: *Oṃ hāṃ trimūrtaye namaḥ*.
On the lower lip: *Oṃ hāṃ ekarudrāya namaḥ*.
On the upper teeth: *oṃ hāṃ ekanetrāya namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: *oṃ (hāṃ) śivottamāya namaḥ*. On the chin: *oṃ (hāṃ) sūkṣmāya namaḥ*.
On the tongue—
(l4) (Oṃ hāṃ), salutation to Ananteśa. At the root of the palate— Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Manonmanī.
At the throat: Oṃ (hāṃ) namaḥ to Sarvabhūtadamanī.
At the heart: Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ to Balapramathanī.
(L5. At the right breast: Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ to Balavikaraṇī.
On the left breast—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kalavikaraṇī. At the navel—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kālī. On the right buttock—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Raudrī.
Salutation! On the left hip—Oṃ (Hāṃ), salutation to Jyeṣṭhā.
In the secret place—Oṃ (Hāṃ), salutation to Vāmā.
At the anus: *oṃ hāṃ aṅguṣṭhamātrāya namaḥ*.
At the right seed-syllable: *oṃ (hāṃ) bhuvaneśāya namaḥ*.
At the left seed-syllable: *oṃ (l7)*.
(Hāṃ) Salutation to Īśāna.
At the foundation (ādhāra): (Oṃ hāṃ) Salutation to Ekapiṅgekṣaṇa. 37.

On the sacrificial mounds (*staṇḍila*) of the right hand: *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Udbhava; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Bhava; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Vāmadeva; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Dvitaya; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Śikheda.
On the fingers of the right hand: *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Ekavīra; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Pañcāntaka; *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Piṅgalaśūlaka.

Oṃ hāṃ jyotiṣe namaḥ | Oṃ (hāṃ) saṃvartakāya namaḥ | On the right hand—at the thumb, the fingers, and so forth, starting from the forefoot—twice in the middle of the three [fingers]. There are five places for each finger; thus, there are twenty-five places for the five fingers.
[These mantras] are as follows: on the joints of the thumbs— *oṃ caṇḍāya namaḥ*, *oṃ krodhāya namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ ekaṃ śivāya namaḥ*.
In the middle joints of those [fingers]: *oṃ anantāya namaḥ* | *oṃ ajāya namaḥ*.
In the joints of the index fingers (*tarjanī*): *oṃ umāpataye namaḥ* | *oṃ pracaṇḍāya namaḥ* | *oṃ vīrāya namaḥ*.
In the middle of those joints: *Oṃ haṃ īśānāya namaḥ | Oṃ bhavāya namaḥ*.
In the middle joints: *Oṃ ugrāya namaḥ | (Oṃ) bhīmāya namaḥ | Oṃ vāmāya namaḥ*.
In the middle of those joints: *Oṃ śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ | Oṃ kūrmāya namaḥ*.
On the joints of the ring finger: *oṃ hāṃ kaumārāya namaḥ*; *oṃ vaiṣṇave namaḥ*; *oṃ brāhmaṇe namaḥ*; *oṃ* in the middle of that joint: *oṃ bhairavāya namaḥ*;
*oṃ hāṃ kṛtāya namaḥ*.

On the joints of the little finger: *oṃ akṛtāya namaḥ*, *oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ prājeśvarāya namaḥ*. In the middle of those joints: *oṃ saumyāya namaḥ*, *oṃ aindrāya namaḥ*. Likewise, on the joints of the left hand: *oṃ gandharvāya namaḥ*, *oṃ yakṣāya namaḥ*, *oṃ rākṣase namaḥ*, *oṃ paiśācāya namaḥ*.

Oṃ, obeisance to Sthūleśvara. ... On the fingers of the hands—obeisance to Sthaleśvara. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkukarṇa. Oṃ, obeisance to Kālāñjana. Oṃ, obeisance to Maṇḍaleśvara. Oṃ, obeisance to ...koṭa.
Oṃ, on the joints of the left thumb—(l2) Oṃ, salutation to Dviraṇḍa; Oṃ, salutation to Chagalaṇḍa; Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Sthāṇu. In the middle of those joints—Oṃ, salutation to Svarṇākṣa;
salutation to Bhadrakaṇṭha.
On the joints of the index fingers: *oṃ gokarṇāya namaḥ* | (l3) *oṃ hāṃ mahābalāya namaḥ* | On the joints of the middle fingers: (l4)
Oṃ, salutation to Avimukta. Oṃ, salutation to Bhīmeśvara. Oṃ, salutation to Vimaleśvara. Oṃ, salutation to Gayā. Oṃ, salutation to Kāla. Oṃ, salutation to Śrīśaileśvara.
(L5) In the middle of that [range]—Oṃ, salutation to Mahendra. Oṃ, salutation to Nakhalā. In the middle of that [range]—salutation to Madhyameśvara.
On the palm of the right hand:
*oṃ rudrakoṭaye namaḥ* | *oṃ aṭṭahāsāya namaḥ* | *oṃ nākhalāya namaḥ* | *oṃ kedārāya namaḥ*. In the middle of those joints:
behind that, *lakulīśvarāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ, salutation to Vastraprada. In the middle joint of that [finger]—oṃ, salutation to Kurukṣetra.
In the joints of the little finger—oṃ, salutation to Jalpeśvara.
On the palm of the left hand—oṃ, salutation to Ḍiṇḍimuṇḍa. On its back—(p200a, c1).
Salutation to Bhārabhūti.
At the joints of the right foot: Oṃ, salutation to Āṣāḍhi; Oṃ, salutation to Puṣkara; Oṃ, salutation to Naimiśa; Oṃ, salutation to Prabhāsa; Oṃ, salutation to Amareśa. (c2)

On the toes of the right foot: Oṃ, obeisance to Bhadrakālī; Oṃ, obeisance to Vīrabhadra; Oṃ, obeisance to Trilocana; Oṃ, obeisance to Lipsu; Oṃ, obeisance to Nabhas. On the big toe of the right foot—(c3)
Twice in the middle of the two joints of the hands; four locations for each finger; thus there are twenty locations for the five fingers.
In the middle of the joint of the big toe of the right foot: *Oṃ hāṃ vivihāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ saṃvāhanāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ tridaśeśvarāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ tryakṣāya namaḥ*.

In the middle of the ring finger: Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṇādhyakṣa; Oṃ, obeisance to Vibhava; Oṃ, obeisance to Śambhava; Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Daṃṣṭrin. In the middle of the middle finger: Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Vajrin; Oṃ, obeisance to Phaṇīndra; Oṃ, obeisance to Udumbarīśa; Oṃ, obeisance to Grasana.
In the middle of the ring finger joint: Oṃ, obeisance to Mārutāśana; Oṃ, obeisance to Krodha; Oṃ, obeisance to Amita; Oṃ, obeisance to Vṛṣadhara.
In the middle of the little finger joint: Oṃ, obeisance to Vṛṣa; Oṃ, obeisance to Balipriya; Oṃ, obeisance to Bhūtapāla; Oṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭha.
Oṃ, at the joints of the left foot: Oṃ, homage to Śarva; Oṃ, homage to Sureśa; Oṃ, homage to Vedapāraga; Oṃ, homage to Jñānabhuja; Oṃ, homage to Sarvajña.
At the toes of the left foot: Oṃ, homage to Īśāna; Oṃ, homage to Vidyādhipa; Oṃ, homage to Prakāmadā.
Oṃ, homage to Prasāda. Oṃ, homage to Śrīdhara. Oṃ, at the middle joint of the big toe of the left foot—homage to Ratnadhara. Homage to Lakṣmīdhara. Homage to Jaṭādharā. (c3) Homage to Saumyadeha.

In the middle of the ring finger—(Oṃ) salutation to Dhanya; Oṃ, salutation to Rūpavān; Oṃ, salutation to Nidhīśa; Oṃ, salutation to Meghavāhana. In the middle of the middle finger—(C4) Oṃ, salutation to Kapardin; Oṃ, salutation to Pañcaśikha; Oṃ, salutation to Pañcāntaka; Oṃ, salutation to Kṣayāntaka.
In the middle joint of the ring finger: *oṃ tīkṣṇāya namaḥ* | *oṃ sūkṣmāya namaḥ* | *oṃ vāyuvegāya namaḥ* | *oṃ lalāṭāya namaḥ*.
In the middle joint of the little finger: *oṃ śīghrāya namaḥ* | *oṃ sudanādāya namaḥ* | *oṃ maghanādāya namaḥ* | *oṃ jalāntakāya namaḥ*.
On the sole of the right foot: *oṃ dīrghabāhave namaḥ*. On its back: *oṃ jayabhadrāya namaḥ*.
On the sole of the left foot: *oṃ śvetāya namaḥ*. On its back: [oṃ jayabhadrāya namaḥ].
Homage to Mahābalā. [Right] armpit—homage to Pāśahasta. Left armpit—oṃ, homage to Atibala.
On the right side: Oṃ, homage to Bala.
On the left side: Oṃ, homage to Daṃṣṭravan. On the right knee: Oṃ, homage to Lohita.
On the left knee—Oṃ, salutation to Dhūmra.
On the right shoulder—Oṃ, salutation to Virūpākṣa. On the left shoulder—salutation to Ūrdhvaśepha.
In the stomach—oṃ, salutation to Bhayānaka.
In the belly—oṃ, salutation to Krūradṛṣṭi. In the penis—oṃ, salutation to Hantṛ.
To Vṛṣaṇa—oṃ, obeisance to Māraṇa. To the right elbow—oṃ, obeisance to Niruti. To the left elbow—(c3).
Oṃ, obeisance to Dharma. At the location of the right shoulder-blade: Oṃ, obeisance to Dharmapati.
At the location of the left shoulder-blade: Oṃ, obeisance to Viyoktra.
On the right conch: *oṃ yoktre namaḥ*.
On the left conch: *oṃ kartre namaḥ*. On the right thigh: *oṃ vidhātre namaḥ*.
On the left thigh— Oṃ, salutation to Dhātṛ.
In the center of the mūlādhāra— (c4) Oṃ, salutation to Hara.
In front of him: Oṃ, obeisance to Mṛtyu. On the right knee: Oṃ, obeisance to Yāmya.
On the left knee: Oṃ, obeisance to Kṣayāntaka.
On the right calf: Oṃ, homage to Bhasmāntaka.
On the left calf: Oṃ, homage to Bhruva.
On the right stalk: Oṃ, homage to Dahana.
In the navel channel—(c5) *oṃ jvalanāya namaḥ*. From the navel to the heart: *oṃ harāya namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ khādakāya namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ piṅgalāya namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ hutāśanāya*.
Homage! Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Agnirudra. Oṃ (hāṃ), homage to the Lord of the Thirty-three. Oṃ, homage to Pinākin.
In the middle of the right shoulder: Oṃ, homage to Śāstṛ.
In the middle of the left shoulder—(Oṃ) salutation to the Unmanifest.
On the right corner of the mouth—Oṃ, salutation to Vibhūti. On the left corner of the mouth—(C2).
Oṃ, homage to Pramardana. On the crown of the head: Oṃ, homage to Vajradeha.
On the right forehead: Oṃ, homage to Buddha.
On the left forehead: *oṃ ajāya namaḥ*. At the tip of the nose: *oṃ kapālīśāya namaḥ*.
In the middle of the nostril: *oṃ rudrāya namaḥ*.
To the right eyebrow: Oṃ, homage to Viṣṇu.
To the left eyebrow:
Oṃ, homage to Brahmā.
Having placed [the mantra] for remaining in one place: *oṃ hāṭakāya namaḥ*. On the two eyebrows (*bhruvoḥ*) in this manner: *oṃ kūśmāṇḍāya namaḥ*. On the two armpits (*kakṣayoḥ*)—in this manner.
Oṃ, salutation to Kāla... [and so on] ... by means of the Pāśupata weapon...
(c4). Thus ends the assignment of the worlds (bhuvananyāsa).

After the placement of the worlds (*bhuvananyāsa*), one should perform the placement of the phonemes (*varṇanyāsa*). The placement of the phonemes is declared to extend from the letter *a* to the letter *kṣ*; it has been described according to the previously mentioned method.
After the placement of the phonemes, one should perform the placement of the parts (*kalānyāsa*). (c5) (The placement of the parts)—
At the crown of the head: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the kalā Śāntyatītā.
In the mouth: Oṃ hyaiṃ, salutation to the kalā Śānti. In the heart: Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to the kalā Vidyā.
At the navel: *Oṃ hvīṃ*, obeisance to the *pratiṣṭhā* aspect (*kalā*).
At the feet: *Oṃ haṃ*, obeisance to the *nivṛtti* aspect. "Obeisance to the self of the power of will (*icchāśakti*)"—this is the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*).
After the placement of the aspects (*kalā-nyāsa*), one should perform the placement of the mantras (*mantra-nyāsa*).
(The ritual placement of mantras):
On the head—*āṃ namaḥ īśānamūrdhne namaḥ*.
On the face—*āṃ namaḥ tatpuruṣavaktrāya namaḥ*, from the forehead to the cheek. Having thus placed the sixteen vowels.
Having placed the five consonants of the *ka*-group—*kaṃ namaḥ aghorahṛdayāya namaḥ* and so forth—on the right hand;
and having placed the five consonants of the *va*-group—*vaṃ namaḥ vāmadevaguhyāya namaḥ* and so forth—on the left hand;
one should place the five consonants of the *ṭa*-group—*ṭaṃ namaḥ sadyojātapādābhyāṃ namaḥ* and so forth—on the abdomen.
*Tam* namaḥ; *hṛdayāya namaḥ*. Having thus placed the five letters of the *tavarga* on the right side; *paṃ* namaḥ; *śirase namaḥ*. Having placed the five letters of the *pavarga* on the left side;
*yaṃ* namaḥ; *śikhāyai namaḥ*. Having thus placed the four syllables of the *yavarga* on the right foot.
Having placed the four syllables of the *śa*-group with "Śaṃ namaḥ kavacāya namaḥ" on the left foot;
one should place "Oṃ namaḥ netratrayāya namaḥ" on the heart;
and "Kṣaṃ namaḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ namaḥ" at the *mūlādhāra*.
Oṃ hauṃ saśivāya klīṃ paśūṃ phaṭ pāśupatāstrāya huṃ—this is the pervasive [mantra]. The *golaka*-nyāsa:
at the heart—oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ.
*Namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the right shoulder. *Namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the left shoulder.
*Śi namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the right shoulder.
*vāṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the left thigh;
*yaṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the throat (*khaṇḍa*);
*oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the navel.
*Maṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the right side;
*naṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the left side;
*śiṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—in the right armpit.
*vāṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the left armpit;
*yaṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the head;
*oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the mouth.
Naṃ *namaśśivāya* namaḥ — on the right eye. Maṃ *namaśśivāya* namaḥ — on the left eye.
Śiṃ *namaśśivāya* namaḥ — on the two nostrils. (c2.)
VĀṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ, YAṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ— on the six joints of the right [hand].
OṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ, MAṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ, ŚIṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ, VĀṄ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ, YAṂ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ— on the six joints of the left [hand].

Oṃ śiṃ, salutation to Śiva; vāṃ, salutation to Śiva. (c4) yaṃ, salutation to Śiva—on the six joints of the right foot. Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. Oṃ naṃ, salutation to Śiva. Oṃ maṃ, salutation to Śiva. Oṃ śiṃ, salutation to Śiva.
Oṃ vaṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance.
(c5) Oṃ yaṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance—at the six joints of the left foot.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance. Naṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance. Maṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance. Śiṃ, obeisance to Śiva, obeisance. Vāṅmanaśśivāya... [obeisance].
Namaḥ.
(c6) "Oṃ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ" on the head;
"oṃ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ" on the face.
Naṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ—on the heart;
maṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ—on the belly;
śiṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ—on the thighs.
*vāṅmanaśśivāya namaḥ*—at the feet;
*yaṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—in the heart;
*oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—in the face.
Naṃ Namaśśivāya Namaḥ—on the axe;
Maṃ Namaśśivāya Namaḥ—on the deer;
Śiṃ Namaśśivāya Namaḥ—on the gesture of fearlessness.
Oṃ *namaśśivāya*—salutation for the welfare of speech and mind—at the forehead; *yaṃ namaśśivāya*—salutation at the face; *oṃ namaśśivāya*—salutation at the heart. (c2.)
*Maṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—at the feet;
*śiṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—at the thighs;
*vāṅmanaśśivāya namaḥ*—at the abdomen.
"Yaṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ" on the lower lip;
"Oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ" on the forehead;
"Naṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ" on the belly.
*Maṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the right shoulder;
*Śiṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—on the left shoulder;
*Vāṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*—in the heart.
Having worshipped [the deity] with "Yaṃ namaśśivāya hau," which pervades Śiva, as before from water to water;
(the placement of the worlds):
Oṃ pada—Oṃ aṃ ā (āṃ) iṃ [the crores of Guhya and others, the restrainers of the world of Atala] (c4).
Salutation to Śiva, who is the form of the root deity of the Yoginīs—at the secret place (guhya).

*Īṃ Ūṃ Ūṃ*—salutation to Paramaśiva, together with the supporting power (dhāraśakti) of the root deity and the innermost among the many tens of millions of great secret Yoginīs of Vitala—at the shanks (jaṅghā). *Ṛṃ Ṛṃ*—salutation to Paramaśiva, together with the supporting power of the root deity and the innermost among the many tens of millions of great secret Yoginīs of Sutala—at the knees (jānu).

*Ḷṃ namaḥ*— to the Paraśiva accompanied by the Mūladevatā and the Ādhāraśakti, together with the ten koṭis of Guhyāntayoginīs of Talātala. … *Oṃ auṃ*, obeisance to Paraśiva accompanied by the Dharāśakti and the hundred koṭis of Yoginīs of Rasātala, in the Mūlādhāra.

Aṃ Aḥ! Homage to the Supreme Śiva, accompanied by the Earth-Śakti and the hundred million Yoginīs of Rasātala, together with the Root Deity. … Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ! [Homage] to the one joined with the hundred million Yoginīs of Pātālaloka and the Root Deity.
Salutation to Paramaśiva accompanied by the Earth-Śakti.
Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ. Salutation to Paramaśiva accompanied by the Earth-Śakti, together with the ten billion secret Ḍākinīs and Yoginīs who are the root deities of the Bhūrloka.

Thus is the placement of the worlds (*bhuvananyāsa*). Having worshipped [the elements] from water to water as before, follows the placement of the principles and their lords (*tattvatattveśvaranyāsa*): *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Śiva; to Śiva, the lord of the principle of Śiva.* (L5)
*Namaḥ* | *Namaḥ śaktitattvāya* | *Namaḥ śaktitattvādhipataye śaktimate* | Thus for the portion of Rudra. *Namaḥ sadāśivāya*. *Oṃ hāṃ sadāśivatattvāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ sadāśivatattvādhi-* (l6)

Salutation to Brahmā, the Lord; salutation to the principle of Īśvara (Īśvaratattva); salutation to Ananta, the sovereign lord of the principle of Īśvara; salutation to the principle of Pure Knowledge (Śuddhavidyātattva); salutation to Śambara, the sovereign lord of the principle of Pure Knowledge. Thus [ends the section on] Viṣṇu.
In the [respective] portion: salutation to the Māyā-tattva; salutation to Gahaneśa, the lord of the Māyā-tattva; Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the subtle body (sūkṣmadeha);
salutation to the Kāla-tattva; Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the lord of the Kāla-tattva.

Salutation to the one named Kāla. Salutation to the principle of Niyati (Destiny). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kāmā, the sovereign of the principle of Niyati. Salutation to the principle of Vidyā (Knowledge). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jñānavid, the sovereign of the principle of Vidyā. (l2.)

Salutation to the principle of passion (*rāgatattva*). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the lord of the principle of passion, the bestower of desires. Salutation to the principle of the person (*puruṣatattva*). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the lord of the principle of the person, the subtle body (*sūkṣmadeha*). Salutation to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛtitattva*). (L3)
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Lord of the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*), the body of Pradhāna.

Obeisance to the principle of the qualities (*guṇa-tattva*). Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Lord of the principle of the qualities, the three-bodied one (*trideha*). Thus, in the portion of Brahmā. Obeisance to the principle of the intellect (*buddhi-tattva*). (L4)
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Budha (Buddha), the lord of the principle of intellect (buddhitattva).
Homage to the principle of ego (ahaṅkāratattva). Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ahaṅkṛta, the lord of the principle of ego. Homage to the principle of mind (manastattva). (L5)
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Saṅkalpa, the lord of the principle of the mind.
In the two ears—salutation to the principle of hearing. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyomacara, the lord of the principle of hearing.
In the skin—(l6)
Homage to the principle of the skin (*tvak-tattva*). Homage to the sovereign of the principle of the skin, the all-pervading one (*sarvagā*).
In the eyes—homage to the principle of the eye (*cakṣus-tattva*). Homage to the lord of the principle of the eye, light (*prakāśa*).
In the tongue—homage to the lord of the principle of the tongue.
Salutation to Rasanā.

At the nose: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vidumbaka, the lord of the principle of smell (nāsa-tattva). In the speech: salutation to the principle of speech (vāk-tattva); salutation to Dundubha, the lord of the principle of speech.

In the hands—homage to the reality of the hand (*pāṇitattva*); homage to Sāma, the lord of the reality of the hand. In the feet—homage to the reality of the foot (*pādatattva*); homage to Ahaṅkṛta, the lord of the reality of the foot.
In the generative organ—homage to the principle of the generative organ; homage to Ramaṇa.
In the anus—(l.
2)—homage to the principle of the anus; homage to Puṇyakṛt, the sovereign of the principle of the anus.
In the genitals—homage to the principle of the genitals; homage to Ghanānanda, the lord of the principle of the genitals.
In sound—homage to the principle of sound; homage to Sūkṣmanāda, the lord of the principle of sound.

On the sense of touch—*namaḥ* to the principle of touch (*sparśatattva*). *Namaḥ* to Bhānumat, the lord of the principle of touch. On the sense of taste—*namaḥ* to the principle of taste (*rasatattva*). *Namaḥ* to Jalada, the lord of the principle of taste. On the sense of smell—*namaḥ* to the principle of smell (*gandhatattva*). *Namaḥ* to [the lord] of the principle of smell. (l4)

Salutation to Gandhavatī. In the ether: salutation to the principle of ether; salutation to Sūkṣma, the lord of the principle of ether. In the air: salutation to the principle of air; salutation to Mātariśvan, the lord of the principle of air.
In the fire [element] (l5):

*namaḥ* to the fire-principle (*agnitattva*); *namaḥ* to the lord of the fire-principle, the treasury of splendors. In the water [element]: *namaḥ* to the water-principle (*jalatattva*); *namaḥ* to the lord of the water-principle, the Lord of Waters (*jaleśvara*).

"Salutation to the Earth Principle (*pṛthivītattva*); salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha, the Lord of the Earth Principle. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the principles and their lords, and having likewise completed the ritual placement of the principles and their lords, one should worship [the deities] from water up to water, present the offerings, and pray for one's desired object.

Now, the ritual placement of the Lords of the Embodiments (mūrtīśvaranyāsa): Oṃ hāṃ laṃ, salutation to the Earth-embodiment; Oṃ hāṃ laṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the presiding lord of the Earth-embodiment; Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Water-embodiment; salutation to Viṣṇu, the presiding lord of the Water-embodiment. (p205a, l1)
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, homage to the form of Fire; homage to Rudra, the lord of the form of Fire. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the form of Wind; homage to Maheśvara, the lord of the form of Wind.
Oṃ hāṃ haṃ, homage to the form of Space. (l2)
Salutation to Sadāśiva, the lord of the ether-form.
Oṃ hāṃ suṃ, salutation to the moon-form. Salutation to Mahādeva, the lord of the moon-form. Oṃ hāṃ ṣaṃ, salutation to the sun-form. (L3)
"Salutation to Bhava, the lord of the Sun-form (*arkamūrti*);

*oṃ hāṃ iṃ*, salutation to the Moon-form (*indumūrti*); salutation to Paśupati, the lord of the Moon-form. Having worshipped thus and having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) for each section, one should obstruct [the passage] in the Brahma-quarter.

Having thus arranged [the ritual], and having given a flower garland and protective cord (*pratisara*) for the purpose of visualization, one should conceptualize the three sections (*trikhaṇḍa*). Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) from the head down to the feet—
the portion of Rudra at the head and the portion of Brahmā at the base— one should proceed.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-principle; Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the lord of the Śiva-principle. Up to this point is the Viṣṇu portion. In the Brahma portion, one should worship up to the end of the Māyā-principle. Having divided [the area] into sections, one should block each part.
Salutation to the seeker of liberation; salutation to Sadyojāta, the lord of those seeking liberation; salutation to Nivṛtti; salutation to Mahādeva, the lord of Nivṛtti;
salutation to Pratiṣṭhā. (l7)
Salutation to Aghora, the presiding lord of pratiṣṭhā;
salutation to Vidyā; salutation to Tatpuruṣa, the presiding lord of vidyā;
salutation to Śānti; salutation to Īśāna, the presiding lord of śānti.
Salutation to Śāntyatītā.

Salutation to Sadāśiva, the presiding lord of Śāntyatītā. Having thus worshipped, then [one worships] upon the pedestal (*piṇḍikā*), beginning from the base (*nāla*): "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Power (*śaktitattva*); salutation to Śaktimān, the presiding lord of the principle of Power," and so forth.

(12) Having placed the principles (*tattva*) from the preceding [element] down to earth, together with their presiding deities, and having given the *mālāpratisara* for the purpose of viewing the three sections, [one recites] at the left side: *oṃ hrīṃ vidyātattvāya namaḥ*, [and] to the lord of the *vidyātattva*. (13)
Salutation to Icchā. On the upper part of the throat of the *pīṭha*, up to the end of the *śakti-tattva*: *oṃ hrīṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ*. Salutation to Jñāninī, the sovereign of the *śiva-tattva*.
Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, [one places it] on the lower part of the throat.
Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) of the three principles (*tritattva*) at the throat and above it, part by part, starting from the east and so forth: (c1.

*Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the embodiment of Patience (*kṣamāmūrti*); obeisance to Dhārikā, the presiding deity of the embodiment of Patience. *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the embodiment of Fire (*agnimūrti*); obeisance to Dīptimatī, the presiding deity of the embodiment of Fire.

Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the embodiment of the sacrificer; homage to Ugrā, the presiding deity of the embodiment of the sacrificer. (c2. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the embodiment of space; homage to Jyotsnā, the presiding deity of the embodiment of space.
